Book summit locks 7 days ahead. VNF vignette (péage plaisance) needed; permis plaisance eaux intérieures or recognised licence/ICC for engines >4.5 kW.

name: Canal du Rhône au Rhin, branche sud (Saint-Symphorien-sur-Saône – Doubs – Mulhouse – Niffer)
aliases: Canal du Rhône au Rhin - Branche Sud
Canal du Rhône au Rhin, branche sud
Canal du Rhône au Rhin (Branche Sud)
Canal du Rhône au Rhin - La Suarcine
reach: Saône at Saint-Symphorien-sur-Saône (lock 75, PK 0) via Dole, the canalised Doubs to Besançon and Montbéliard (Allan), the Valdieu summit (Territoire de Belfort/Haut-Rhin, PK 186), then the Rhine side to Mulhouse and the large-gauge Mulhouse–Niffer section to the Grand Canal d'Alsace

depth.notes: Summit pound (Bourogne PK 176 – lock 38 Rhine side) limited 1.60 m to 29.11.2026; it was 1.20 m from 24.07 and 1.00 m Aug–Oct 2026. Hagenbach (23N)–Brunstatt (38): silting, closed from 19.02.2024, 1.2 m since 01.03.2025 (listed Feb 2026). Rancenay bief 1.50–1.80 m by Doubs level.

current.notes: Alternates canal cuts and canalised Doubs/Allan reaches: current and floods on river sections. Flood stops: Dole–Montbéliard 23.02.2024, Montbéliard 31.05.2024, PK 0–186 from 17.02.2026 (reopened ~20.02).

locks.chamber: Freycinet; max boat 38.80 × 5.10 m
locks.notes: Doubs valley (Allenjoie–Saint-Symphorien): 65 automated locks worked by boaters with a VNF remote control. Valdieu: 12 locks in 3 km at the summit. Besançon: tunnel (~390 m) under the Citadelle. Hours not found in an official 2026 source — check VNF DT Rhône-Saône/Strasbourg.

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: RPPi 13: 10 km/h on river (Doubs) sections, 6 km/h by day and 4 km/h at night in canal and dérivation sections, under 6 km/h in tunnels; Mulhouse–Niffer (RPPi 20) 12 km/h, 6 km/h in the secondary canal.

season.closures: Winter chômage 2025–26: PK 0–174 (lock 75 – lock 8) 01.12.2025–30.01.2026; 2026–27 not yet published. Water shortage 2026: Fontenelles (8)–Dampierre (18) closed 24.09–31.10.2026; summit 1.00–1.20 m Jul–Nov. 2025: boats grouped on the summit 26.06–30.11.2025.

months.notes: Dec–Jan closed is a judgement from one winter chômage (2025–26). Low water Jul–Oct is a judgement from 2025–2026 (summit 1.00 m in Aug–Oct 2026 = impassable at 1.2 m draught); earlier drought years not confirmed. Doubs floods in Feb 2024 and Feb 2026, also May–Jun 2024.

tides.notes: Inland river/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: VNF Direction territoriale Rhône-Saône (Saône–Allenjoie, PK 0–174) and VNF Direction territoriale Strasbourg (summit and Rhine side to Niffer)

notices: https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/avisbat/ (avis à la batellerie) and https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/situation-du-reseau/ (weekly situation du réseau PDF); DTRS weekly bulletin https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/app/uploads/2019/06/2026_11_12_bulletin_hebdo_avisbat_DTRS.pdf
notes: Ports Dole, Besançon, Montbéliard, Mulhouse. Check summit and Hagenbach–Brunstatt depths before committing with 1.2 m draught; no mooring at Allenjoie lock 9 upstream pontoon in 2026. VNF vignette (péage plaisance) needed; permis plaisance eaux intérieures or recognised licence/ICC for engines >4.5 kW.

name: La Rance (Saint-Malo – Barrage de la Rance – Écluse du Châtelier – Dinan)
aliases: Écluse du Barrage de la Rance
reach: Saint-Malo/Dinard through the EDF tidal-barrage lock, the Rance basin (Saint-Suliac, Plouër, Mordreuc) to the Écluse du Châtelier (lock 48, Lyvet) and the canalised Rance to Dinan port (Vieux Pont)

depth.notes: Région/CRT carnet: whole Saint-Malo–Dinan route usable by boats up to 1.40 m draught; Mordreuc–Châtelier shallow at low basin levels, banks dry outside the buoyed channel. Since 07.08.2026 draught limited to 1.50 m Dinan Vieux Pont – Châtelier.

current.notes: Basin currents set by EDF turbining/sluicing, can exceed 5 kn in places; HW stand often >3 h. Strong stream at Port Saint-Hubert/Port Saint-Jean narrows. Strong tidal streams below the barrage.

locks.chamber: Barrage lock 65 × 13 m (lift bridge for air draught >4 m); Châtelier: canal lock
locks.hours: Barrage: every round hour when sea level ≥ +4 m CM; 20:30–04:30 only on request with 30 min notice (VHF 13, 02 99 16 37 37). Châtelier: weekly timetable set from Rance levels (Friday to Friday), works only when basin ≥ 9 m (aim for >10 m); VHF 14, 02 96 39 55 66
locks.notes: Give the barrage lock-keeper 30 min notice with draught/air draught; going to sea gates close 20 min before the hour, from sea be there 5 min before. Châtelier swing bridge may be closed to masted boats in heat waves (May 2026 notice). Châtelier was closed Dec–Jan, booking 48 h ahead Feb/Mar/Nov in 2024–25.

rules.permit: No VNF vignette (not VNF waters: EDF barrage, Région Bretagne canal); port fees only
rules.notes: Barrage lock runs only at set times from the EDF timetable (usually on the hour going up, H+30 going down; on request at night); masted boats need the road bridge lifted. Yellow-buoyed zones above and below the barrage are closed to navigation. Below the Châtelier lock the Rance is maritime water (coastal rules: 5 kn in the 300 m strip); canal part to Dinan as Ille-et-Rance.

season.closures: Barrage lock all year (tide permitting). Châtelier/canal: Région chômage 26.10.2026–01.04.2027; Châtelier closed by fallen trees from 23.10.2026, a reopening notice has followed (undated).

months.notes: Dec–Jan 'closed' = Châtelier winter closure reported for 2024–25 (judgement for 2026–27; the barrage lock still works). Basin levels follow EDF operation, not just tides: check the weekly EDF Saint-Suliac forecast.

tides.notes: Saint-Malo: mean range 8 m, up to 13.5 m at big springs. Basin above the barrage is held by EDF between about 4 and 12 m CM (Saint-Suliac gauge, weekly EDF forecast ±30 cm). Reach the barrage at the end of the flood; go Plouër/Mordreuc→Châtelier near HW (basin >10 m). Above Lyvet no tides.

authority.name: EDF Hydro (Rance barrage and lock); Région Bretagne – Canaux de Bretagne (Écluse du Châtelier, Lyvet–Dinan)

notices: https://www.edf.fr/usine-maremotrice-rance/marees-en-rance (EDF levels/lock times) and https://canaux.bretagne.bzh/actualites/avis-a-la-batellerie/ (Région avis à la batellerie, Châtelier timetable)
notes: Charts SHOM 7130 and 4233. Prohibited zones marked by buoys above and below the barrage. Ports: Saint-Malo (Vauban via Naye lock, VHF 9), Dinard, La Richardais, Saint-Suliac, Plouër (pontoon), Lyvet (pontoon), Dinan. Air draught 3 m passes the barrage bridge without a lift; Dinan old bridge starts the 2.50 m canal arches.

name: Canal d'Ille-et-Rance (Dinan – Hédé – Rennes)
reach: Dinan port (Vieux Pont) up the Rance valley via Léhon, Évran, Tinténiac and the 11 Hédé locks to the Guipel summit pound (~65 m, 7 km), then down the Ille to the Vilaine in Rennes (Écluse du Mail, n°1)

depth.notes: Official draught 1.20 m (Région), with a 30 cm 'pied de pilote' advised. 2026: 1.20 m from 03.04 (1.05 m Haut-Chalet–Brosses), 1.10 m Rennes–Dinan from 07.08.2026 (drought). 2022: −20 cm Rennes–Évran. A 1.2 m boat is at or over the limit.

current.notes: Canal with river sections, no significant current; speed 6 or 10 km/h as signed.

locks.notes: Manned locks (phone numbers per lock in the Région carnet); 27 locks up from Dinan to the summit, 20 down to Rennes; 11 Hédé locks in 2 km; falls up to 2.80 m (Calaudry). Châtelier (n°48) is on the Rance sheet. Moorings max 72 h, free except Dinan.

rules.permit: No VNF vignette (Région Bretagne waterway); moorings free except Dinan, most limited to 72 h
rules.notes: Speed 6 or 10 km/h depending on the section: follow the signs (Région Bretagne). Navigation banned in floods by notices to boaters.

season.closures: No lock service 26.10.2026–01.04.2027 (chômage; bief lowerings 30–80 cm; Tinténiac gates 30.11–11.12, Mottay, Saint-Martin, Saint-Grégoire). Flood bans in winter (2025, 2026 Évran–Dinan). Weather closure Mail–Châtelier 23–24.10.2026.

months.notes: Nov–Mar = no lock service (Région chômage, 2026–27 dates official). Low water Aug–Oct is a judgement from 2022 and 2026 draught limits; no full summit-pound drought closure found 2019–2026. Flood months a judgement (Jan 2025, 2026 notices).

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: Région Bretagne – Canaux de Bretagne, subdivision Vilaine – canal d'Ille-et-Rance

notes: Blocking for a 3 m air draught: bridge/lock arches give only 2.50 m at the springing, and 1.2 m draught exceeds the 2026 limits. Liaison Manche–Océan (via Vilaine) was cut early 2024 – 03.04.2026 (Boël lock rebuilt). Pontoons Dinan, Léhon, Évran, Tinténiac, Hédé, Betton, Rennes.

name: La Vilaine (Rennes – Redon – Barrage d'Arzal)
aliases: Jonction de la Vilaine au Canal de Nantes à Brest
reach: Rennes (Écluse Dupont-des-Loges, n°1) down the canalised Vilaine via Pont-Réan, Messac/Guipry to Mâlon (n°13) and Redon, then the lock-free impounded Vilaine maritime (Rieux, Pont de Cran, Foleux, La Roche-Bernard) to the Arzal-Camoël dam lock

depth.notes: Rennes–Redon draught 1.20–1.60 m (FVA topo); 2026 drought: 1.20 m Rennes–Redon and 1.10 m in the Mons pound from 07.08.2026. Redon–Arzal deep (4.10 m). La Roche-Bernard old port <1.50 m.

current.notes: Canalised river Rennes–Redon; impounded reservoir below Redon. Winter floods: strong current near Arzal when the dam gates evacuate at low tide; navigation banned in big floods (Oct 2024, Jan 2025).

locks.chamber: Arzal lock 85 m long; Rennes–Redon locks small (not found)
locks.hours: Rennes–Redon locks 2026 season 03.04–25.10: 09:00–12:30, 13:30–18:00 (19:00 13.06–13.09). Arzal: round-hour lockings (weekends and 01.04–30.09), up to 11 a day in summer; booking/notice via passeportecluse-arzal-camoel.com
locks.notes: 13 locks Dupont-des-Loges (1) – Mâlon (13) plus Arzal dam lock (Eaux & Vilaine). Pont de Cran swing bridge (23 m span) 5.80 m closed: ask VHF 10 or 02 99 91 80 87. Boël lock rebuilt, link reopened 03.04.2026.

rules.permit: No VNF vignette (Région Bretagne and EPTB Eaux & Vilaine waters)
rules.notes: Redon–Arzal: 5.5 kn (about 10 km/h) on the open river, 3 kn near ports (2018 guide; check the Région's 2025 RPP Vilaine). Arzal lock: restricted lockages in drought. Navigation banned in floods Rennes–Redon by notice.

season.closures: Locks unattended 26.10.2026–01.04.2027 (Région chômage). Arzal: drought restrictions 26.08–04.11.2026 (closed 31.08–04.09, then only reserved low-water 'safety' lockings, e.g. 2 per week late Sep); winter closure from 04.11.2026 (anti-salinity lock works), reopening late March 2027 not officially confirmed.

months.notes: Closed Nov–Mar = Région chômage + Arzal winter closure (official for 2026–27). Aug–Oct is a judgement from 2026, when Arzal was almost closed in September – a real risk for a September transit in a dry year. Flood bans Oct 2024, Jan 2025.

tides.notes: Non-tidal above the Arzal dam since 1970. Seaward of Arzal the estuary is tidal: come up on the flood; banks at the mouth move with dam releases. Fresh/salt water current at the lock gates.

authority.name: Région Bretagne – Canaux de Bretagne (Rennes–Redon); Eaux & Vilaine EPTB (Arzal dam and lock, Pont de Cran)

notes: Air draught 3.20 m Rennes–Redon: a 3 m boat has only 0.20 m margin. Arzal-Camoël marina (VHF 9) has 60 visitor berths, fuel; La Roche-Bernard, Foleux, Rieux, Redon (VHF 9) ports. Redon is the junction with the Canal de Nantes à Brest.

name: La Gironde and Garonne maritime (Royan/Pauillac – Bordeaux – Castets-en-Dorthe)
reach: Gironde estuary from Royan/Pointe de Grave via Pauillac and Bec d'Ambès, the tidal Garonne through Bordeaux (Pont Chaban-Delmas, Pont de Pierre, Pont François-Mitterrand), Cadillac and Langon to the canal entrance at Castets-en-Dorthe (lock 53)

depth.notes: Deep ship channel to Bordeaux; above Bordeaux depth varies with tide – no official figure found. Exit into the canal at Castets is tide- and river-level dependent.

current.notes: Very strong tidal streams, even at neaps; flood can give >10 kn over the ground near the mouth. Whirlpools and floating trees at Bordeaux bridges while the stream runs. Flood marks on bridge piers Bordeaux–Langon.

locks.notes: No locks; Castets lock 53 (manned, tide-dependent) is on the Canal latéral sheet. Pont Chaban-Delmas is a lift bridge (lifts scheduled; low motor boats pass under the lowered deck).

rules.permit: None in the estuary (maritime); VNF vignette on the VNF-managed Garonne upstream of Bordeaux
rules.notes: Estuary up to the Bordeaux stone bridge: maritime RPP (7 Dec 2015), sea rules (5 kn in the 300 m strip), call Bordeaux port VHF 12. Garonne upstream of the Pont de Pierre (RPP rivières girondines, VNF RPPi 19): 25 km/h for small craft, 20 km/h for others, 10 km/h when meeting a boat or passing moored craft; a 2017 inter-prefectoral RPP now applies, check it.

season.closures: Free navigation all year, watch floods (vigicrues). Castets lock 53 closed with the canal chômage (9.11–20.12.2026).

months.notes: High water Jan–Feb is a judgement (winter/spring Garonne floods, Feb 2026 storm stop on the canal). Mascaret is strongest on big spring tides with low river flow – late summer/September.

tides.notes: Macrotidal, range ~2–5 m (SHOM/EPOC), amplified to Bordeaux (wet season) or Cadillac (dry); tide dies out between Langon and La Réole. Ride the flood: Pauillac arrive ±5 min of HW; leave Bordeaux at LW slack, ~6 h to Castets with no safe stop. Mascaret (tidal bore) at springs between Langoiran and Podensac – keep off the banks.

authority.name: Grand Port Maritime de Bordeaux / DDTM Gironde (estuary to Bordeaux, VHF 12); VNF DT Sud-Ouest – Service Territorial Garonne (Pont François-Mitterrand to Castets and upstream)

notices: https://www.premar-atlantique.gouv.fr/avis-urgents-aux-navigateurs.html (AVURNAV) and https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/avisbat/ (avis à la batellerie, DT Sud-Ouest) and https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/situation-du-reseau/ (weekly situation du réseau PDF)
notes: Masted boats unstep at Pauillac (book crane). Call Bordeaux port VHF 12. Upstream of the Pont de Pierre waters are inland (permis eaux intérieures). Ponton d'Honneur Bordeaux (strong current); Cadillac 'Eiffel' pontoon for pleasure craft. Hire boats may not leave the canal at Castets.
sources: https://www.gironde.gouv.fr/index.php/contenu/telechargement/72103/538704/file/Fiche 3 - Règles de navigation dans l'estuaire, lacs et rivières.pdf

name: Canal latéral à la Garonne (Castets-en-Dorthe – Agen – Moissac – Toulouse)
aliases: Écluse de Descente en Tarn à Moissac
reach: Garonne at Castets-et-Castillon (lock 53, PK 193.3) via Le Mas-d'Agenais, the Agen aqueduct, Moissac (Cacor aqueduct over the Tarn, Tarn descent lock) and Montech to Port de l'Embouchure, Toulouse (PK 0)

depth.notes: VNF mouillage 1.60 m throughout; Wikipedia cites a practical 1.30 m max draught especially at Castets (2017). A 1.2 m draught is fine in normal conditions.

current.notes: Canal, 8 km/h. Strong cross-currents at the Toulouse-side locks 1–9 (VNF warning).

locks.chamber: 40.50 × 6.00 m (Castets–16 and 10–Toulouse 40.30), 31.00 × 6.00 m (15–11; Montech 30.50); Tarn descent at Moissac 30.70 × 6.00 m (double)
locks.hours: High season 25.03–01.11.2026 daily 09:00–12:00, 13:00–19:00 (26.10–01.11: 08:00–11:00, 12:00–18:00; no midday stop Embouchure–Mazérac 51); low season on demand weekdays 08:30–12:00, 13:00–16:30. Locks 52–53 on call 06 62 99 63 91 08:30–19:30 all year. Closed 1 Jan, 1 May, 11 Nov, 25 Dec
locks.notes: Automated, boater-operated (poles). Pass in one go: Montech 11–12, 13–15; Moissac 19–22, 23–25; Agen 34–37 (45 min) and 39–40; last entry 15–45 min before closing. Moissac swing bridge open permanently 2026. Lock 53 depends on tide and Garonne level, no waiting in pound 53. Montech water slope out of use.

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: RPP canal des Deux Mers: 8 km/h on the whole canal. Two crew needed at automated locks.

season.closures: Annual chômage, whole canal: 12.11–22.12.2024; 09.11–20.12.2026 (navigation stopped, drained pounds). Storm stop 12.02.2026. 2026 water management: boats grouped 18.07–31.10.

months.notes: Nov–Dec closed = VNF chômage (official 2024 and 2026 dates; 2027 to be published by VNF). Summer 2026 only grouping at locks, no draught cut found.

tides.notes: Canal non-tidal; only Castets lock 53 works to the Garonne tide (see Gironde/Garonne sheet).

authority.name: VNF DT Sud-Ouest – Service Territorial Garonne (Agen, 05 53 47 31 15) and ST Toulouse Haute-Garonne (locks 1–9)

notices: https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/avisbat/ (avis à la batellerie, DT Sud-Ouest) and https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/situation-du-reseau/ (weekly situation du réseau PDF); yearly rules in https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/app/uploads/2026/03/AvisBat_1_Sud-ouest_2026.pdf
notes: Crew of 2 needed at automated locks. Air draught: 3.60 m on the axis but 3.00 m over a 5.50 m width (Castets–16), 3.35 m Lavache–Toulouse – fine for 3 m if the high point is central. Hire boats may not pass 52–53. VNF no. 0 800 863 000. VNF vignette (péage plaisance) needed; permis plaisance eaux intérieures or recognised licence/ICC for engines >4.5 kW.

name: Canal du Midi (Toulouse – Seuil de Naurouze – Carcassonne – Béziers – Étang de Thau)
reach: Port de l'Embouchure, Toulouse (PK 0) up to the Naurouze summit (Écluse de l'Océan, PK 51.6), down via Castelnaudary, Carcassonne, Fonserannes (Béziers), the Agde round lock and the Hérault crossing to the Étang de Thau at Les Onglous/Marseillan (PK 240.1)

depth.notes: VNF mouillage 1.40 m on all sections; water-shortage closures are triggered when levels can no longer hold 1.40 m. A 1.2 m draught is OK in normal water; keep to the centre (silted banks).

current.notes: Canal, 8 km/h. Short river crossing of the Hérault between Bassin Rond (Agde) and Prades locks – check level.

locks.chamber: Béarnais–Ayguesvives 40.25–43.92 × 5.70–6.00 m; Sanglier–Fonserannes 29.70–34.35 × 5.50–6.08 m; Orb–Bagnas 40.60–42.50 × 5.85–6.08 m
locks.hours: High season 25.03–01.11.2026 daily 09:00–12:00, 13:00–19:00 (26.10–01.11: 08:00–11:00, 12:00–18:00); low season pleasure craft on demand weekdays 08:30–12:00, 13:00–16:30. Fonserannes by up/down phases (May–Sep 08:10–18:40). Agde to the sea at fixed times. Closed 1 Jan, 1 May, 11 Nov, 25 Dec
locks.notes: 15 locks Toulouse–Océan (automated, boater-operated), 48 Méditerranée–Bagnas (mostly manned, oval multiple chambers: Saint-Roch ×4, Fonserannes ×7). Malpas tunnel: long horn blast and lights before entering, extinguisher on board. Last entry 15–25 min before closing at Castelnaudary, Carcassonne, Trèbes, Fonserannes.

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: RPP canal des Deux Mers: 8 km/h on the whole canal. No mooring to the plane trees.

season.closures: Winter chômage 05.01–01.03.2026 (2027 dates not yet published). Water-shortage stop on the whole canal from 06.11.2023 (to 01.03.2024), 03.11.2025 (to Mar 2026) and now 09.11.2026–03.01.2027 (FR/2026/08762; reserves 7.3% on 10.11.2026).

months.notes: Jan–Feb = standard chômage (official 2026). Nov–Dec closed in 3 of the last 4 winters for lack of water (2023, 2025, 2026) – a judgement, the rule is low-season on-demand service. Early March reopening has slipped to mid-March (2023). Summer stays open; boats grouped from 27.06.2025.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: VNF DT Sud-Ouest – ST Toulouse Haute-Garonne (PK 0–50.6, 05 62 15 11 95) and ST Midi, Béziers (PK 50.6–240.1, 04 67 11 81 30)

notices: https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/avisbat/ (avis à la batellerie, DT Sud-Ouest) and https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/situation-du-reseau/ (weekly situation du réseau PDF); water reserves: https://www.vnf.fr/vnf/services/situation-de-la-gestion-hydraulique-du-canal-du-midi/
notes: Bridges are arches: axis 3.30 m (Sanglier road bridge, the tightest) but only 2.00 m over a 5.50 m width Sanglier–Fonserannes; Carcassonne Marengo rail bridge 3.30 m axis, 2.36–3.00 m at sides. A 3 m air draught passes only with a narrow, central high point. No mooring to plane trees (canker). VNF no. 0 800 863 000. VNF vignette (péage plaisance) needed; permis plaisance eaux intérieures or recognised licence/ICC for engines >4.5 kW.

name: Niegocin and the Giżycko canals (Łuczański, Niegociński, Piękna Góra, Tajty)
reach: Lake Niegocin (Giżycko, Wilkasy, Rydzewo side) and the two links north to Kisajno: Kanał Łuczański/Giżycki on the main route (around main km 61.8–63.9) and side route IV Niegocin – Kanał Niegociński – Tajty – Kanał Piękna Góra – Kisajno (main km 60.50 to 64.75, 4.20 km)
class: II (Niegocin); Ia (Kanał Niegociński, Kanał Piękna Góra, Tajty)

depth.notes: Transit depth class II 2.20 m, class Ia 1.50 m at low water (Giżycko gauge 89 cm, KN 2/2026). The UŻŚ order gives 1.8 m (class II lakes) and 1.5 m minimum in canals. The Niegociński detour is shallower than the lakes: raise centreboard and go slowly. Works from 16.11.2026 to remove wooden piles and dredge at the rail bridge on Kanał Niegociński (KN 40/2026).

current.notes: Lakes and short canals, practically no current.

locks.hours: Giżycko swing bridge (Kanał Łuczański), 1 Apr–31 Oct 2026, boat windows 10:30–11:00, 12:35–13:00, 14:00–14:35, 17:25–18:25; Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct on request to the operator (726 888 878), daily at these times 1 Jul–31 Aug; closed to boats Nov–Mar
locks.notes: Swing bridge of 1898, hand-operated, swings 90° (≈5 min). In heat waves the span jams: closed to boats 29–30.06.2026 (KN 15–16/2026). Masts down for the rail and road bridges on Kanał Niegociński (1.2 km) and on Kanał Piękna Góra; no clearance figures published.

rules.permit: No vignette or navigation permit; lock fees at the locks. No licence for sailing yachts ≤7.5 m hull or motor yachts ≤10 kW; motor yachts ≤13 m, ≤75 kW and built-limited to 15 km/h (houseboats) need no licence but a rented one requires the water-safety briefing (art. 37a ustawy o żegludze śródlądowej). Larger boats: patent from the Polish sailing or motorboat federation.
rules.notes: 2026: Kanał Łuczański closed to navigation km 61.8–63.93 for the DK59 Giżycko bypass bridge, except authorised passenger ships and the 1–3 May and 4–7 June weekends (ZDP Giżycko; KN 2/2026); others use Kanał Niegociński – Tajty – Kanał Piękna Góra. Combustion engines banned on Tajty except on this route (Giżycko county). Canals 10 km/h (8 km/h laden), no anchoring in canals, no wash within 50 m of shore (Zarządzenie 7/2024).

season.best: May–June, September (SSO storm-warning masts on 1 May – 31 Oct)
season.closures: Closed for the winter since 01.11.2026 (KN 37/2026) after buoys were lifted from 15.10.2026 (KN 34/2026); 2026 season ran 24.04–31.10. Routes are marked for daytime navigation only.

months.notes: SWJM waterways opened 24.04.2026 (KN 2/2026) and closed 01.11.2026 when the buoys were lifted (KN 37/2026); 2025 closure from 24.11.2025 (KN 38/2025). Locks run in winter only until the first ice. Ice months are a typical-winter estimate (ice-yachting season), not an official figure.

authority.name: PGW Wody Polskie RZGW Białystok, Zarząd Zlewni w Giżycku (tel. 87 428 39 92, Kierownik Obiektu Hydrotechnicznego 532 032 745 / 87 428 53 38)

notices: https://www.gov.pl/web/wody-polskie-bialystok/aktualne-komunikaty-nawigacyjne-obowiazujace (Komunikaty nawigacyjne RZGW Białystok; closures, lock hours, Pisa depths)
notes: Busiest charter base. Ports: Ekomarina Giżycko (238 berths), Żegluga Mazurska quay, Wilkasy (PTTK, AZS), Tajty/Piękna Góra marinas. Detour via Tajty adds traffic; pass early or late in the day. Ask in Giżycko whether the Łuczański closure continues in 2027. Emergency: 601 100 100 (water rescue), 984 (WJM), 112; MOPR posts Giżycko 87 428 23 00, Mikołajki 669 925 158, Pisz 669 925 108. SSO masts: 40 flashes/min warning, 90/min alarm (seek shelter).

name: Northern Masurian lakes: Kisajno, Dargin, Łabap, Kirsajty, Mamry, Święcajty (Giżycko – Węgorzewo)
reach: Main route from Kisajno (main km 64.75) to Węgorzewo (km 86.80, incl. the navigable Węgorapa and Kanał Węgorzewski from km 84.10), side route V Mamry (km 78.75) – Święcajty – Ogonki 8.50 km, and the Sztynort branch
class: II (Kisajno, Dargin, Mamry, Święcajty); Ia (Kirsajty, Węgorapa, Kanał Węgorzewski)

depth.notes: Transit depth 2.20 m (class II) / 1.50 m (class Ia) at Giżycko gauge 89 cm (KN 2/2026). Węgorapa reach: follow the buoys, shallows both sides. Max vessel 44 × 7 m on the lakes, 25 × 5 m on the Węgorapa/Kanał Węgorzewski (UŻŚ order).

current.notes: Lakes and short canals, practically no current.

locks.notes: No locks. Kirsajty road bridge (km 14.5 from Giżycko) needs the mast down; Kanał Węgorzewski and Kanał Sztynorcki need no mast lowering. Kanał Mazurski (from Mamry near Mamerki) is unfinished and closed.

rules.permit: No vignette or navigation permit; lock fees at the locks. No licence for sailing yachts ≤7.5 m hull or motor yachts ≤10 kW; motor yachts ≤13 m, ≤75 kW and built-limited to 15 km/h (houseboats) need no licence but a rented one requires the water-safety briefing (art. 37a ustawy o żegludze śródlądowej). Larger boats: patent from the Polish sailing or motorboat federation.
rules.notes: Jezioro Dobskie (reserve) closed to combustion engines (Giżycko county resolution). On Kisajno from Zatoka Tracz to Kanał Piękna Góra and north to Dębowa Górka, vessels other than small craft keep to the buoyed fairway. Canals 10 km/h; no wash within 50 m of shore (Zarządzenie 7/2024).

season.best: May–June, September (SSO storm-warning masts on 1 May – 31 Oct)
season.closures: Closed for the winter since 01.11.2026 (KN 37/2026) after buoys were lifted from 15.10.2026 (KN 34/2026); 2026 season ran 24.04–31.10. Routes are marked for daytime navigation only.

months.notes: SWJM waterways opened 24.04.2026 (KN 2/2026) and closed 01.11.2026 when the buoys were lifted (KN 37/2026); 2025 closure from 24.11.2025 (KN 38/2025). Locks run in winter only until the first ice. Ice months are a typical-winter estimate (ice-yachting season), not an official figure.

authority.name: PGW Wody Polskie RZGW Białystok, Zarząd Zlewni w Giżycku (tel. 87 428 39 92, Kierownik Obiektu Hydrotechnicznego 532 032 745 / 87 428 53 38)

notices: https://www.gov.pl/web/wody-polskie-bialystok/aktualne-komunikaty-nawigacyjne-obowiazujace (Komunikaty nawigacyjne RZGW Białystok; closures, lock hours, Pisa depths)
notes: Dargin and Mamry are open, deep water where wind quickly builds waves; with strong northerlies wait in Sztynort or a Kisajno bay. Ports: Sztynort, Kietlice, Trygort, Węgorzewo (several quays on the Węgorapa), Ogonki, Przystań Nautica (Święcajty, 150 berths, 1.8 m).

name: Masurian canals Niegocin – Tałty (Boczne, Jagodne, Kula, Szymoński, Mioduński, Grunwaldzki, Tałcki)
reach: Main route between Niegocin and Tałty (about main km 32.5–58): lakes Boczne, Jagodne, Szymoneckie, Szymon, Kotek, Tałtowisko and the canals Kula (110 m), Szymoński (2.3 km), Mioduński (1.9 km), Grunwaldzki/Lelecki (470 m), Tałcki (1.6 km)
class: Ia (canals, Szymon, Szymoneckie, Kotek, Tałtowisko, Jagodne); II (Boczne)

depth.notes: Canals: minimum 1.5 m (UŻŚ order), class Ia transit 1.50 m at Giżycko gauge 89 cm (KN 2/2026). Szymon is shallow and marshy: stay in the buoyed channel.

current.notes: Lakes and short canals, practically no current.

locks.notes: No locks. Road bridges over the canals (a low steel bridge at Kula): masts down in almost every canal. No clearance figures published.

rules.permit: No vignette or navigation permit; lock fees at the locks. No licence for sailing yachts ≤7.5 m hull or motor yachts ≤10 kW; motor yachts ≤13 m, ≤75 kW and built-limited to 15 km/h (houseboats) need no licence but a rented one requires the water-safety briefing (art. 37a ustawy o żegludze śródlądowej). Larger boats: patent from the Polish sailing or motorboat federation.
rules.notes: Canals 10 km/h (8 km/h laden) unless signed; no overtaking in canals, keep right; no anchoring in canals; no wash within 50 m of shore and pontoons (Zarządzenie 7/2024). Wody Polskie renovated and dredged the canals and their lake entrances.

season.best: May–June, September (SSO storm-warning masts on 1 May – 31 Oct)
season.closures: Closed for the winter since 01.11.2026 (KN 37/2026) after buoys were lifted from 15.10.2026 (KN 34/2026); 2026 season ran 24.04–31.10. Routes are marked for daytime navigation only.

months.notes: SWJM waterways opened 24.04.2026 (KN 2/2026) and closed 01.11.2026 when the buoys were lifted (KN 37/2026); 2025 closure from 24.11.2025 (KN 38/2025). Locks run in winter only until the first ice. Ice months are a typical-winter estimate (ice-yachting season), not an official figure.

authority.name: PGW Wody Polskie RZGW Białystok, Zarząd Zlewni w Giżycku (tel. 87 428 39 92, Kierownik Obiektu Hydrotechnicznego 532 032 745 / 87 428 53 38)

notices: https://www.gov.pl/web/wody-polskie-bialystok/aktualne-komunikaty-nawigacyjne-obowiazujace (Komunikaty nawigacyjne RZGW Białystok; closures, lock hours, Pisa depths)
notes: The canal chain carries all Giżycko–Mikołajki traffic: queues at the narrow canals in July–August. Lower the mast in good time before each canal. Harbours: Rydzewo, Bogaczewo, Kula, Szymonka, Jagodne, Kozin, Kula canal is the Vistula/Pregel watershed.

name: Tałty and Jezioro Mikołajskie (Mikołajki)
reach: Main route from Tałtowisko through Tałty (12.5 km long, 50 m deep) and Mikołajki to the Przeczka strait onto Śniardwy, with the junctions of side route II (Bełdany, main km 22.00) and III (Ryn, main km 32.50)

depth.notes: Class II: transit 2.20 m at Giżycko gauge 89 cm (KN 2/2026), 1.8 m in the UŻŚ order. Tałty is the deepest lake on the route (50–51 m).

current.notes: Lakes and short canals, practically no current.

locks.notes: Bridges and a footbridge at Mikołajki; no published clearances.

rules.permit: No vignette or navigation permit; lock fees at the locks. No licence for sailing yachts ≤7.5 m hull or motor yachts ≤10 kW; motor yachts ≤13 m, ≤75 kW and built-limited to 15 km/h (houseboats) need no licence but a rented one requires the water-safety briefing (art. 37a ustawy o żegludze śródlądowej). Larger boats: patent from the Polish sailing or motorboat federation.
rules.notes: Jezioro Mikołajskie is one of the Masurian Landscape Park waters where motorboats are allowed (Uchwała XLIV/635/22 §5). From the PAN station to the Mikołajki footbridge, vessels other than small craft keep to the buoyed fairway. No wash within 50 m of shore (Zarządzenie 7/2024).

name: Pisa (Pisz – Nowogród, link to the Narew)

name: Istria coast (Savudrija – Rovinj – Brijuni – Pula – Kamenjak)
reach: West coast of Istria from Savudrija and Umag via Novigrad, Poreč, Vrsar, Rovinj and the Brijuni islands to Pula, Medulin and Cape Kamenjak

depth.notes: Open sea; harbour depths ample for 1 m draught.

rules.permit: Annual navigation safety fee (by length and engine power, enautika.pomorstvo.hr; certificate on board) and tourist tax for boats over 7 m with berths (lump sum by length and period, nautika.evisitor.hr); crew list for foreign nationals
rules.notes: NN 52/2025 (amended NN 40/2026), Art. 50: max 8 kn within 300 m of the coast, in narrow channels and harbour/anchorage approaches; jet skis and planing boats only beyond 300 m. Art. 49: keep ≥50 m off the coast (<15 m LOA), ≥150 m (15–30 m), ≥300 m (≥30 m); ≥50 m from a buoyed beach. Art. 53: no anchoring where charted or banned by the harbourmaster, near cables/outfalls, <50 m from a buoyed beach or <150 m from a natural beach; shore lines max 70 m. HTZ guide still quotes 5 kn inside 150 m: obey local harbour notices. Brijuni NP: only passage to Veliki Brijun port or the authorised anchorage in front of it; no anchoring SE of Veliki Brijun (Peneda–Kumpar–Kosir).

season.closures: None; gales (bora, jugo) close passages for a day or two.

months.notes: Sea, no closures. Bora (NE, gusty, katabatic) most common in winter but summer bora of 1–3 days occurs; jugo (SE, warm, big seas) all year, stronger autumn–spring; maestral (NW sea breeze) is the regular summer afternoon wind.

tides.notes: Microtidal, mixed semidiurnal/diurnal. HHI mean daily range at Rovinj 0.47 m, the largest on the Croatian coast; jugo and low pressure raise the sea more than the tide does.

authority.name: Ministarstvo mora, prometa i infrastrukture / harbourmasters (lučke kapetanije); MRCC Rijeka (tel. 195, VHF 16)

notes: Brijuni NP: berths in Veliki Brijun port (Pula Port Authority collects entry fees from 1 May; VHF 9, +385 99 293 5491). Weather: Rijeka Radio VHF 04/20/24/81 at 05:35, 14:35, 19:35 UTC; continuous forecast VHF 73 (Pula harbourmaster). Distances: Rovinj–Pula 14–18 NM, Pula–Brijuni 4–10 NM, Pula–Mali Lošinj 36 NM.

name: Kvarner (Rijeka, Opatija, Krk, Cres, Lošinj, Rab, Velebit channel)
reach: Kvarner and Kvarnerić: east coast of Istria, Opatija and Rijeka, Krk (Punat, Krk town), Cres (Cres town, Osor), Lošinj (Mali Lošinj), Unije, Susak, Ilovik, Rab, northern Pag, Senj and the Velebit channel

depth.notes: Open sea. Osor (Cres–Lošinj) is a narrow cut under a swing bridge opened at set times; plan the Lošinj channel accordingly.

rules.permit: Annual navigation safety fee (by length and engine power, enautika.pomorstvo.hr; certificate on board) and tourist tax for boats over 7 m with berths (lump sum by length and period, nautika.evisitor.hr); crew list for foreign nationals
rules.notes: NN 52/2025 (amended NN 40/2026), Art. 50: max 8 kn within 300 m of the coast, in narrow channels and harbour/anchorage approaches; jet skis and planing boats only beyond 300 m. Art. 49: keep ≥50 m off the coast (<15 m LOA), ≥150 m (15–30 m), ≥300 m (≥30 m); ≥50 m from a buoyed beach. Art. 53: no anchoring where charted or banned by the harbourmaster, near cables/outfalls, <50 m from a buoyed beach or <150 m from a natural beach; shore lines max 70 m. HTZ guide still quotes 5 kn inside 150 m: obey local harbour notices.

season.closures: Strongest bora of the Adriatic under Velebit: Senj, Velebit channel, Pag and Maslenica (gust 69 m/s at Maslenica bridge, 1998); it can rise suddenly on a clear calm day.

months.notes: Sea, no closures. Bora (NE, gusty, katabatic) most common in winter but summer bora of 1–3 days occurs; jugo (SE, warm, big seas) all year, stronger autumn–spring; maestral (NW sea breeze) is the regular summer afternoon wind. Bora is the danger here, worst Nov–Mar; Velebit channel can reach 9–10 Bf even in summer.

tides.notes: Microtidal, mixed semidiurnal/diurnal. HHI mean daily range at Bakar 0.30 m (other studies give ~0.6 m in Bakar bay); jugo and low pressure raise the sea more than the tide does.

notes: Weather: Rijeka Radio VHF 04/20/24/81 at 05:35, 14:35, 19:35 UTC; continuous forecast VHF 69 (Rijeka harbourmaster). Legs (charter NM): Punat–Cres 17, Mali Lošinj–Rab 23–25, Mali Lošinj–Silba 20–22, Rab–Krk ~21. Marinas: Punat, ACI Cres, ACI Rab, Mali Lošinj town quay.

name: Northern Dalmatia: Zadar archipelago (Silba, Olib, Premuda, Molat, Ugljan, Pašman, northern Dugi Otok)
reach: Zadar, Sukošan (D-Marin Dalmacija), Preko, the Zadar channel, Ugljan, Pašman and the Pašman channel, Iž, Molat, Ist, Premuda, Silba, Olib and Dugi Otok north of Sali (Božava, Veli Rat, Sakarun)

rules.permit: Annual navigation safety fee (by length and engine power, enautika.pomorstvo.hr; certificate on board) and tourist tax for boats over 7 m with berths (lump sum by length and period, nautika.evisitor.hr); crew list for foreign nationals
rules.notes: NN 52/2025 (amended NN 40/2026), Art. 50: max 8 kn within 300 m of the coast, in narrow channels and harbour/anchorage approaches; jet skis and planing boats only beyond 300 m. Art. 49: keep ≥50 m off the coast (<15 m LOA), ≥150 m (15–30 m), ≥300 m (≥30 m); ≥50 m from a buoyed beach. Art. 53: no anchoring where charted or banned by the harbourmaster, near cables/outfalls, <50 m from a buoyed beach or <150 m from a natural beach; shore lines max 70 m. Mali Ždrelac: no anchoring, sailing, stopping or fishing in the passage (Art. 57); Pašman channel: no anchoring or stopping in the fairways (Art. 64).

notes: Weather: Split Radio VHF 07/21/23/28/81 at 05:45, 12:45, 19:45 UTC (Rijeka Radio covers the north). Legs (charter NM): Sukošan–Biograd 10, Zadar–Murter 23, Silba–Olib 12, Veli Iž–Dugi Otok 11, Dugi Otok–Zadar 16. Telašćica tickets are also sold by agencies in Sali and Sukošan.

depth.notes: Open sea and island channels; many shoals in the Kornati, use the chart.

rules.permit: Annual navigation safety fee (by length and engine power, enautika.pomorstvo.hr; certificate on board) and tourist tax for boats over 7 m with berths (lump sum by length and period, nautika.evisitor.hr); crew list for foreign nationals; Kornati NP and Telašćica Nature Park tickets per vessel per day
rules.notes: NN 52/2025 (amended NN 40/2026), Art. 50: max 8 kn within 300 m of the coast, in narrow channels and harbour/anchorage approaches; jet skis and planing boats only beyond 300 m. Art. 49: keep ≥50 m off the coast (<15 m LOA), ≥150 m (15–30 m), ≥300 m (≥30 m); ≥50 m from a buoyed beach. Art. 53: no anchoring where charted or banned by the harbourmaster, near cables/outfalls, <50 m from a buoyed beach or <150 m from a natural beach; shore lines max 70 m. HTZ guide still quotes 5 kn inside 150 m: obey local harbour notices. St. Anthony channel (Šibenik): no anchoring in the channel or before its outer entrance; boats may anchor and swim only in its side bays (Art. 66).

season.closures: None; bora and jugo gales. Park tickets are priced by season: VI–IX high season, I–V and X–XII low.

months.notes: Sea, no closures. Bora (NE, gusty, katabatic) most common in winter but summer bora of 1–3 days occurs; jugo (SE, warm, big seas) all year, stronger autumn–spring; maestral (NW sea breeze) is the regular summer afternoon wind.

tides.notes: Microtidal, mixed semidiurnal/diurnal. HHI mean daily range at Zadar 0.25 m (nearest published station); jugo and low pressure raise the sea more than the tide does.

authority.name: Harbourmaster Šibenik; JU Nacionalni park Kornati (Murter); JU Park prirode Telašćica (Sali)

notes: Kornati NP 2026, ticket bought outside the park, 1 day low/high: <7 m €25/45, 7–11 m €30/65, 11–18 m €50/95 (on site 11–18 m €95/190); 3- and 5-day tickets; joint Kornati+Telašćica 3-day ticket. Telašćica (2025 list): 11–18 m €40/90 outside, €50/100 inside. Buy online (Parkovi Hrvatske webshop, mySea) at least a day ahead. Use park buoys; no anchoring on Posidonia or between buoys. Continuous forecast VHF 73 (Šibenik harbourmaster).

name: Krka estuary (Šibenik – Prokljan – Skradin)
reach: From the St. Anthony channel and Šibenik harbour up the drowned Krka estuary (Kanal sv. Josipa, Prokljansko jezero, Skradinski kanal) to ACI Marina Skradin; navigable for private boats only to Skradin

depth.notes: Deep channel to Skradin (ACI berths in up to 7 m). Raslina under 2 m; Zaton town quays shallow (~2.5 m off the north shore); two poorly charted shoals in north and NE Prokljan.

current.notes: River outflow; Art. 66 allows exceptions to the speed limit in strong downstream current.

locks.notes: No locks. Road bridge at Šibenik about 27 m clearance per SeaHelp (not confirmed officially).

rules.permit: Croatian navigation safety fee and tourist tax; Krka NP ticket to visit the falls (park boat from Skradin included)
rules.notes: Art. 66 NN 52/2025: max 8 kn on the Krka (SeaHelp says 5 kn); no anchoring in Kanal sv. Josipa or in the Skradin channel from Rt Oštrica (Prokljan) to Skradin; overtake only on the other vessel's port side; keep right. No private boats above Skradin: park boats run Skradin–Skradinski buk April–October.

season.closures: Park boats to Skradinski buk only April–October (weather and river level permitting).

months.notes: Tidal estuary, no closures for yachts to Skradin. Park boats to the falls do not run in winter.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea level as on the coast (~0.25 m); fresh outflow on the surface.

authority.name: Harbourmaster Šibenik; JU Nacionalni park Krka

notes: ACI Marina Skradin: 153 berths, water and power, open all year, often full in season; nearest fuel in Šibenik (~8 NM). Šibenik–Skradin about 8–10 NM (about 2 h). Legs: Murter–Skradin 26–27 NM, Skradin–Zlarin 11–15 NM, Skradin–Zaton 6 NM. Anchoring officially not allowed outside the marina.

name: Central Dalmatia (Trogir, Split, Šolta, Brač, Hvar, Pakleni, Vis)
reach: Trogir and Čiovo, Kaštela, Split, Šolta (Maslinica), Brač (Milna, Bol), Hvar (Hvar town, Stari Grad, Jelsa, Vrboska), the Pakleni islands (Palmižana), Vis (Vis town, Komiža), Biševo and the Makarska riviera

depth.notes: Open sea; harbour depths ample for 1 m draught.

rules.permit: Annual navigation safety fee (by length and engine power, enautika.pomorstvo.hr; certificate on board) and tourist tax for boats over 7 m with berths (lump sum by length and period, nautika.evisitor.hr); crew list for foreign nationals
rules.notes: NN 52/2025 (amended NN 40/2026), Art. 50: max 8 kn within 300 m of the coast, in narrow channels and harbour/anchorage approaches; jet skis and planing boats only beyond 300 m. Art. 49: keep ≥50 m off the coast (<15 m LOA), ≥150 m (15–30 m), ≥300 m (≥30 m); ≥50 m from a buoyed beach. Art. 53: no anchoring where charted or banned by the harbourmaster, near cables/outfalls, <50 m from a buoyed beach or <150 m from a natural beach; shore lines max 70 m. HTZ guide still quotes 5 kn inside 150 m: obey local harbour notices. Pakleni channel: closed to vessels ≥500 GT and yachts ≥1000 GT (exceptions); no anchoring within 0.6 NM of Galešnik (Art. 67).

season.closures: Summer bora off Split and the Brač channel can reach 9–10 Bf; jugo builds a heavy sea in the open Vis channel.

months.notes: Sea, no closures. Bora (NE, gusty, katabatic) most common in winter but summer bora of 1–3 days occurs; jugo (SE, warm, big seas) all year, stronger autumn–spring; maestral (NW sea breeze) is the regular summer afternoon wind. Storm bora at Split usually in winter, but about 30% of cases in spring in recent decades.

tides.notes: Microtidal, mixed semidiurnal/diurnal. HHI mean daily range at Split 0.23 m; jugo and low pressure raise the sea more than the tide does.

authority.name: Ministarstvo mora, prometa i infrastrukture / harbourmasters (lučke kapetanije); MRCC Rijeka (tel. 195, VHF 16)

notes: Weather: Split Radio VHF 07/21/23/28/81 at 05:45, 12:45, 19:45 UTC, NAVTEX Split 518 kHz (Q) and 490 kHz (F); continuous forecast VHF 67 (Split harbourmaster). Legs (charter NM): Trogir–Maslinica 14, Maslinica–Komiža 30, Komiža–Vis 11, Vis–Pakleni 17, Hvar–Stari Grad 12, Stari Grad–Bol 15, Bol–Milna 12, Milna–Trogir 20; Split–Bol ferry 19.

name: Southern Dalmatia (Korčula, Lastovo, Pelješac, Mljet, Elaphites, Dubrovnik)
reach: Korčula (Korčula town, Vela Luka), Lastovo, Pelješac and Ston, the Neretva channel, Mljet (Polače, Pomena, Okuklje), the Elaphite islands (Šipan, Lopud, Koločep), Dubrovnik (Gruž, ACI Komolac), Cavtat and Molunat to Prevlaka

depth.notes: Open sea; ACI Dubrovnik lies up the Rijeka dubrovačka (Ombla).

rules.permit: Annual navigation safety fee (by length and engine power, enautika.pomorstvo.hr; certificate on board) and tourist tax for boats over 7 m with berths (lump sum by length and period, nautika.evisitor.hr); crew list for foreign nationals; Mljet NP and Lastovo Nature Park tickets per vessel
rules.notes: NN 52/2025 (amended NN 40/2026), Art. 50: max 8 kn within 300 m of the coast, in narrow channels and harbour/anchorage approaches; jet skis and planing boats only beyond 300 m. Art. 49: keep ≥50 m off the coast (<15 m LOA), ≥150 m (15–30 m), ≥300 m (≥30 m); ≥50 m from a buoyed beach. Art. 53: no anchoring where charted or banned by the harbourmaster, near cables/outfalls, <50 m from a buoyed beach or <150 m from a natural beach; shore lines max 70 m. HTZ guide still quotes 5 kn inside 150 m: obey local harbour notices. Pelješac bridge: main passage between piers 7 and 8 (Art. 69). Neretva river: 7 kn, 5 kn within 300 m of ships, quays or settlements (Art. 68).

season.closures: Jugo is the main hazard: long fetch and heavy sea on the open coasts of Lastovo, Mljet and off Dubrovnik.

months.notes: Sea, no closures. Bora (NE, gusty, katabatic) most common in winter but summer bora of 1–3 days occurs; jugo (SE, warm, big seas) all year, stronger autumn–spring; maestral (NW sea breeze) is the regular summer afternoon wind.

tides.notes: Microtidal, mixed semidiurnal/diurnal. HHI mean daily range at Dubrovnik 0.22 m; jugo and low pressure raise the sea more than the tide does.

authority.name: Harbourmaster Dubrovnik; JU Nacionalni park Mljet; JU Park prirode Lastovsko otočje

notes: Mljet NP 2026, 1 day low/high season, bought at the park: 7–11 m €35/70, 11–18 m €50/100 (webshop €25/60, €40/90); valid to noon next day. Lastovo Nature Park 2026: 11–18 m €19/36 online, €23/45 on site; mooring paid to rangers. Weather: Dubrovnik Radio VHF 04/07/28/85 at 06:20, 13:20, 20:20 UTC; continuous VHF 73. Legs: Korčula–Pomena 14.5, Dubrovnik–Lopud 8–9, Šipanska Luka–Dubrovnik 15 NM.

name: Bay of Kotor and Montenegro coast (Herceg Novi – Tivat – Kotor – Budva)
reach: Boka Kotorska from the entrance (Oštra, Luštica) via Herceg Novi, Zelenika, Portonovi, Tivat (Porto Montenegro), the Verige strait, Perast and Risan to Kotor, plus the open coast to Budva

depth.notes: Deep fjord-like bay; harbour depths ample for 1 m draught.

rules.permit: Foreign yachts: vignette (cruising permit, from the Harbour Master; 1 week to 1 year) and tourist tax within 24 h of arrival; clear in at a port of entry (Kotor, Zelenika, Porto Montenegro/Tivat, Portonovi, Bar, Budva May–Oct)
rules.notes: Call the harbourmaster on VHF 16 before landing and go straight to the entry port's customs berth; anchoring before clearance is restricted at Kotor. No speed rule confirmed.

season.closures: Bora (NE, katabatic) strongest in the inner bay around Risan; cap cloud over the mountains is the warning.

months.notes: Sea, no closures. Bora mainly in winter, strongest in the inner bay (Risan, Kotor).

tides.notes: Microtidal as in southern Adriatic (Dubrovnik mean daily range 0.22 m); no Montenegrin figure found.

authority.name: Uprava pomorske sigurnosti i upravljanja lukama (Administration for Maritime Safety and Port Management), Bar

notes: Distances (charter NM): Tivat–Perast 4, Perast–Kotor 5, Tivat–Kotor ~8, Kotor–Herceg Novi 12–15, Herceg Novi–Budva 20, Cavtat–Herceg Novi ~25, Dubrovnik–Kotor ~42. Weather: Bar Radio VHF 20/24 (storm warnings and forecast) at 08:50, 14:20, 20:50 UTC. Tax-free diesel for foreign yachts again. Porto Montenegro tourism office does not sell vignettes: Harbour Master next door.

name: Saronic and Argolic gulfs (Athens – Aegina – Poros – Hydra – Spetses – Nafplio)
reach: Athens marinas (Alimos, Zea, Kalamaki) and Sounion, Aegina, Agistri, Methana, Poros, Hydra, Ermioni, Spetses, Porto Cheli, Argolic Gulf to Nafplio, Tolo and Leonidio

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Short hops; in meltemi season Athens (Alimos) is the recommended charter base. Anchoring and engine manoeuvring near bathing beaches is reported limited (500 m default unless a swim zone is buoyed): check local port police rules.

season.closures: No closures. Meltemi July–August.

months.notes: Meltemi (Etesians) mid-May to mid-September, strongest July–August: usually F4–5, often F5–7 by day, gusting F7–8; afternoon peak, eases at night; episodes 3–6 days, up to 10. NOA counts on average 17 strong-wind days in July and 19 in August (2025: 16 and 21).

authority.name: Hellenic Coast Guard (Λιμενικό Σώμα)

notes: Published legs (NM): Alimos–Aegina (Ag Marina) 14, Alimos–Hydra 36, Perdika–Poros 13, Poros–Ermioni 21, Ermioni–Hydra 11, Spetses–Hydra 16, Hydra–Nafplio 43, Leonidio–Nafplio 27, Poros–P. Epidavros 21. Town quays (Hydra, Poros, Aegina, Spetses) are stern-to with own anchor; Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Parnitha (Athens) ch 25.

name: Cyclades (Lavrio – Kea – Syros – Mykonos – Paros – Naxos – Santorini – Milos)
reach: Kea, Kythnos, Serifos, Sifnos, Milos, Kimolos, Folegandros, Ios, Santorini, Anafi, Amorgos, Naxos, Paros, Antiparos, Syros, Tinos, Mykonos, Andros; approaches from Lavrio and Sounion

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Meltemi rules the season: leave at dawn for upwind legs; dangerous acceleration and seas in the Kea, Kafireas (Andros–Evia, current up to 5 kn), Paros–Naxos and Mykonos–Tinos channels and gusts in the lee of high islands (Kea, Tinos, Andros, Serifos, Sifnos, Folegandros, Amorgos).

season.closures: No closures. Meltemi July–August: days of F6–7 can keep yachts in port; within six hours of a 30 kn wind waves can exceed 3 m.

months.notes: Meltemi (Etesians) mid-May to mid-September, strongest July–August: usually F4–5, often F5–7 by day, gusting F7–8; afternoon peak, eases at night; episodes 3–6 days, up to 10. NOA counts on average 17 strong-wind days in July and 19 in August (2025: 16 and 21).

authority.name: Hellenic Coast Guard (Λιμενικό Σώμα)

notes: Published legs (NM): Lavrio–Kythnos 25, Sounion–Kea 15, Syros–Tinos 12, Paros (Parikia)–Syros 25, Naxos–Naoussa 9, Folegandros–Santorini (Vlychada) 29, Folegandros–Ios 18, Serifos–Milos (Adamas) 28. Santorini: Vlychada marina on the south coast. Harbours are stern-to with own anchor. Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Syros ch 04.

name: Dodecanese (Patmos – Leros – Kalymnos – Kos – Nisyros – Symi – Rhodes)
reach: Agathonisi, Arki, Lipsi, Patmos, Leros, Kalymnos, Pserimos, Kos, Nisyros, Tilos, Symi, Chalki, Rhodes, Karpathos, Astypalaia

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Meltemi blows NW here, strongest in the open corridor towards the Cyclades (Kos–Astypalaia, Levitha) and funnelling west of Karpathos.

season.closures: No closures. July–August NW meltemi often F5–7, rough between Kos and Astypalaia and off Karpathos.

months.notes: Meltemi (Etesians) mid-May to mid-September, strongest July–August: usually F4–5, often F5–7 by day, gusting F7–8; afternoon peak, eases at night; episodes 3–6 days, up to 10. NOA counts on average 17 strong-wind days in July and 19 in August (2025: 16 and 21).

authority.name: Hellenic Coast Guard (Λιμενικό Σώμα)

notes: Published legs (NM): Kos–Kalymnos 17, Kalymnos–Leros (Lakki) 21, Lakki–Patmos 20, Patmos–Lipsi 11, Kos–Nisyros (Pali) 22, Rhodes–Symi 26–30, Symi–Panormitis 13, Rhodes–Lindos 24. The Turkish coast (Bodrum 10 NM from Kos) is a separate country: clear out of Greece before crossing. Quays stern-to; Kos and Rhodes have marinas. Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Astypalea ch 23, Rhodes ch 63.

name: Ionian islands (Corfu – Paxos – Lefkas – Meganisi – Kefalonia – Ithaca – Zakynthos)
reach: Corfu, Epirus coast (Sagiada, Syvota, Parga), Paxos and Antipaxos, Preveza, Lefkas, Meganisi, Kalamos, Kastos, Kefalonia, Ithaca, Zakynthos, Katakolo

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Zakynthos National Marine Park (Laganas Bay), 1 May–31 Oct: zone A (yellow buoys) no entry, mooring or anchoring; zone B max 6 kn (11 km/h), no mooring or anchoring (Marathonisi); zone C max 6 kn. Keep speed low for turtles; Strofades also protected. Navagio is a fair-weather day anchorage only.

season.closures: No closures. Etesian-type summer winds also blow in the Ionian (afternoon peak).

months.notes: Sea area, no closures. Laganas Bay marine park restrictions apply 1 May–31 October.

authority.name: Hellenic Coast Guard (Λιμενικό Σώμα)

notes: Published legs (NM): Gouvia–Kassiopi 12, Syvota–Parga 13–15, Parga–Gaios 12–14, Gaios–Gouvia 36, Lefkas–Parga 32, Meganisi (Vathy)–Lefkas 11, Lefkas–Kioni 25, Kioni–Fiskardo 10, Sami–Vathy (Ithaca) 17, Sami–Zakynthos 36, Zakynthos–Katakolo 25. Lefkas canal and floating bridge: see its own sheet. Town quays stern-to (Zakynthos port about €1/m/day at the Port Authority).Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Corfu ch 02, Kefalonia ch 27.

name: Northern Sporades and Pagasitic Gulf (Volos – Skiathos – Skopelos – Alonissos)
reach: Pagasitic Gulf (Volos, Agia Kyriaki/Trikeri), Oreoi channel and north Evia, Skiathos, Skopelos, Alonissos, the Alonissos marine park islands (Peristera, Kyra Panagia, Gioura, Psathoura, Piperi, Skantzoura) and Skyros

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Alonissos National Marine Park (NECCA): Zone A needs an online ticket (tickets.alonissos-park.gr; reported €33.50/vessel/day + €5.50/person, fine 20×). No approach within 3 NM of Piperi; max 10 kn within 0.5 NM of Zone A islands. Kyra Panagia: overnight only Planitis and Agios Petros, Monastiri by day; Psathoura (Mandraki), Skantzoura (Limani) by day only; Gioura closed except Megali Vala/Sykies by day. Zone B1 (Cape Kalamos–Cape Amoni, Alonissos): no overnight, max 10 kn within 200 m.

season.closures: No closures. Summer meltemi blows NE–N in the north Aegean.

months.notes: Meltemi (Etesians) mid-May to mid-September, strongest July–August: usually F4–5, often F5–7 by day, gusting F7–8; afternoon peak, eases at night; episodes 3–6 days, up to 10. NOA counts on average 17 strong-wind days in July and 19 in August (2025: 16 and 21).

authority.name: NECCA Management Unit of the Sporades National Park; Hellenic Coast Guard

notes: Published legs (NM): Volos–Skiathos 41 (ferry), Agios Konstantinos–Skiathos 38 (ferry), Volos–Agia Kyriaki 17–18, Skiathos–Loutraki (Skopelos) 6–7, Skopelos town–Skiathos 15, Patitiri–Skiathos 21.Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Pilio (Volos, Skiathos) ch 60.

name: North Aegean (Halkidiki – Thessaloniki – Kavala – Thassos – Lemnos)
reach: Thermaic Gulf (Thessaloniki), Halkidiki (Kassandra, Sithonia, Athos), Kavala, Thassos, Samothraki and Lemnos

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Long open crossings between Halkidiki, Thassos and Lemnos; few marinas. Check local beach and anchoring rules with the port police.

season.closures: No closures. Northerlies in summer; winter gales.

months.notes: Meltemi (Etesians) mid-May to mid-September, strongest July–August: usually F4–5, often F5–7 by day, gusting F7–8; afternoon peak, eases at night; episodes 3–6 days, up to 10. NOA counts on average 17 strong-wind days in July and 19 in August (2025: 16 and 21).

authority.name: Hellenic Coast Guard (Λιμενικό Σώμα)

notes: Published legs (NM): Kavala–Skala Prinos (Thassos) 17, Kavala–Myrina (Lemnos) 69, Thessaloniki–Myrina 138 (ferries). Few charter bases; Porto Koufo (Sithonia) is the best natural harbour: anchor with tripline, berths limited. Long open crossings; summer northerlies NE–N, strong winds common round Lemnos in August and winter. Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Sfendami (Thessaloniki) ch 23, Thasos ch 85, Lemnos ch 82.

name: Eastern Aegean islands (Lesvos – Chios – Samos – Ikaria)
reach: Lesvos (Mytilene), Chios, Oinousses, Psara (outside the box), Samos, Fournoi, Ikaria, along the Turkish coast

rules.permit: TEPAI cruising fee for private boats over 7 m, paid in advance via AADE eTEPAI per calendar month (min. 1 month): 7–8 m €16, 8–10 m €25, 10–12 m €33, over 12 m €8 per metre; carry the e-paravolo receipt
rules.notes: Meltemi N–NE; dangerous seas between Ikaria, Fournoi and Samos.

season.closures: No closures. July–August meltemi; strong funnelling in the Ikaria–Samos–Fournoi straits.

months.notes: Meltemi (Etesians) mid-May to mid-September, strongest July–August: usually F4–5, often F5–7 by day, gusting F7–8; afternoon peak, eases at night; episodes 3–6 days, up to 10. NOA counts on average 17 strong-wind days in July and 19 in August (2025: 16 and 21).

authority.name: Hellenic Coast Guard (Λιμενικό Σώμα)

notes: Published legs (NM): Mytilene–Chios 48, Çeşme (TR)–Chios 9 (ferries). Turkey is a few miles off: entering Turkish waters or ports needs clearance out of Greece and into Turkey. Strong funnelling in the Ikaria–Samos–Fournoi straits in meltemi. Non-EU boats need a customs transit log (digital since Aug 2024; also requires TEPAI); EU boats over 7 m a DEKPA. ICC accepted; carry a Greek translation of the insurance. VHF weather: Mytilene ch 01, Chios ch 85.

name: Corinth Canal (Isthmia – Poseidonia)
reach: Isthmia (Saronic Gulf, east) to Poseidonia (Gulf of Corinth, west), linking the Aegean and the Ionian without the 700 km trip round the Peloponnese

depth.notes: 8.00 m on the axis at mean low water; safe navigable width 24.6 m at the surface, 21 m on the bottom; beam limit 18.3 m.

current.notes: Current reverses about every 6 h, usually about 2.5 kn, seldom over 3 kn; north-westerlies prevail, gusty northerlies at Poseidonia.

locks.hours: 24 h except the weekly maintenance closure (Tuesdays 06:00–18:00 per noonsite; the regulation says one fixed day a week 06:00–20:00)
locks.notes: Submersible road bridges at both ends are lowered for each transit; one-way convoys only.

rules.permit: Transit toll to Corinth Canal S.A. (2026, private yachts by LOA): under 6 m €70, 6–9 m €100, 9–15 m €100 + €30 per m over 9 m, 15–25 m €100 + €34 per m over 9 m; plus VAT unless exempt
rules.notes: Max 6 kn. Call Corinth Canal Control on VHF 11 about 1 h before arrival and wait for permission and the light signals at each end; follow the convoy order. Pay at Customer Service at the Isthmia end (daily 08:00–22:00) or online by Pay by Link before arrival.

season.closures: Weekly maintenance closure (Tuesdays 06:00–18:00); check the canal notices before arrival.

months.notes: Open all year apart from the weekly maintenance closure.

tides.notes: High–low water difference about 60 cm; the tidal stream in the cut reverses about every 6 h and can reach 3 kn.

authority.name: Corinth Canal S.A. (ΑΕΔΙΚ)

notes: Waiting: Isthmia (east) quay, pay there; at Poseidonia (west) anchor or wait off and do paperwork in the control tower building. Short stays on the canal quays: first 3 h free, then €20 (to 9 m) / €30 (9–15 m) per day. Corinth city harbour is 1.25 NM from the west entrance. A 12 m yacht pays about €190 + VAT.

name: Lefkas Canal and floating bridge (Agia Mavra)
reach: Dredged channel along the east side of Lefkas town, from the floating (swing) bridge at the north entrance past Lefkas Marina to the south end towards Nidri and Meganisi

depth.notes: Dredged to a reported minimum of 4.5 m; about 6 m at the north entrance after dredging; keep to the buoyed channel.

locks.hours: Floating bridge openings (Port Authority schedule): 1 Jun–15 Sep 08:00, 10:00, 14:00, 17:00, 19:00, 21:00, 22:00; 16 Sep–31 May every 2 h 08:00–20:00
locks.notes: Closed to vessels from 14 July 2025 when its safety certificate expired (urgent passages only with Coast Guard permission); 2026 reopening not confirmed. Without it, the north end is reached round the west coast of Lefkas.

rules.notes: Pass the north end only at bridge openings; yachts queue on both sides and the bridge is not always punctual. Bridge reported on VHF 12. South part (Lefkas Marina – Nidri) is open water without the bridge.

season.closures: Floating bridge closed to vessels since 14 July 2025 (certificate expiry); check with Lefkada Port Authority before planning a north–south transit.

months.notes: Bridge status 2025–2026 uncertain; the south half of the canal is unaffected.

authority.name: Lefkada Port Authority (Λιμεναρχείο Λευκάδας)

notes: Lefkas Marina lies on the canal just south of the town; a waiting pontoon serves northbound yachts. Published legs: Lefkas–Parga 32 NM (north through the bridge), Meganisi (Vathy)–Lefkas 11 NM and Lefkas–Kioni 25 NM (south end).

name: Ligurian Riviera, Portofino and Cinque Terre
reach: Sanremo – Imperia – Savona – Genoa – Portofino – Sestri Levante – Cinque Terre – Portovenere – La Spezia – Lerici

depth.notes: Open sea; steep-to coast.

locks.notes: Published legs (NM): Genoa–Portofino 16.4, Portofino–Sestri Levante 9–10, Sestri–Portovenere 25, Lerici–Levanto 16.6, Levanto–Santa Margherita 20.5–20.9, Santa Margherita–Portofino 2.2, La Spezia–Lerici 4.5, Sanremo–Imperia ~15, Imperia–Savona ~37.

rules.notes: AMP Portofino: no mooring in zone A, no anchoring in zones A and B; anchoring in zone C except buoyed no-anchoring areas; motor navigation max 5 kn; boats not meeting the eco requirements enter B/C only on a perpendicular course to the mooring fields. AMP Cinque Terre zone B: displacement speed, max 5 kn within 300 m and 10 kn at 300–600 m; jet skis excluded; anchoring outside signed sensitive areas. Elsewhere bathing-ordinance strips (typ. 200 m from beaches, 100 m from cliffs), crossed only in 3 kn corridors.

season.closures: Gales: mistral most common in winter and spring (Gulf of Genoa lows); libeccio raises high seas.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Mistral most common Dec–May, strongest at the winter–spring transition; libeccio (SW) brings high seas and squalls.

tides.notes: Microtidal Mediterranean coast; no confirmed range found. Wind and pressure change levels more than the tide.

authority.name: Guardia Costiera (Capitanerie di porto Genova, La Spezia, Imperia, Savona); AMP Portofino; Parco Nazionale Cinque Terre

notes: Portofino mooring fields (San Fruttuoso, Punta Chiappa) booked via the AMP Portofino app; Cinque Terre buoy fields 3 kn when manoeuvring. Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: Tuscan archipelago (Elba, Capraia, Giglio, Giannutri, Pianosa, Montecristo)
reach: Livorno – Piombino – Elba (Portoferraio, Marina di Campo, Porto Azzurro, Cavo) – Punta Ala – Capraia – Giglio – Porto Santo Stefano – Giannutri

depth.notes: Open sea.

locks.notes: Published distances (NM): Piombino–Portoferraio 15, Livorno–Capraia 39, Porto Santo Stefano–Giglio ~12, Portoferraio–Marina di Campo 22, Marina di Campo–Porto Azzurro 13, Porto Azzurro–Punta Ala 16, Piombino–Cavo 8, Cavo–Portoferraio 7.

rules.permit: Parco Nazionale Arcipelago Toscano: zone 1 waters closed unless authorised by the park
rules.notes: DPR 22.07.1996 art. 4: in park zone 1 (the sea zones of Montecristo, Pianosa, Gorgona and parts of Capraia and Giannutri) navigation, access, stopping and anchoring are banned, except residents/house owners of Capraia, Gorgona and Giannutri with park authorisation; no swimming at Montecristo. Pianosa's landing is Cala Maestra. Sea zoning of Giannutri, Montecristo, Pianosa and Gorgona is being revised (2025 plan variant). Park fees not confirmed.

season.closures: Mistral and libeccio gales; check bulletins before the Capraia and Giglio crossings.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Mistral most frequent in winter and spring; libeccio (SW) raises high seas.

tides.notes: Microtidal Mediterranean coast; no confirmed range found. Wind and pressure change levels more than the tide.

authority.name: Parco Nazionale Arcipelago Toscano (Portoferraio); Capitanerie di porto Livorno and Portoferraio

notes: Ferries: Toremar to Capraia ~2 h 45 from Livorno. Strictly protected islands (Montecristo, Pianosa, Gorgona) need park-regulated access. Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: Bay of Naples, Ischia, Procida, Capri and the Amalfi coast
reach: Pozzuoli – Procida – Ischia – Naples – Sorrento – Capri – Nerano – Positano – Amalfi – Salerno

depth.notes: Open sea.
