rules.permit: AMP Regno di Nettuno (Ischia, Procida, Vivara): anchoring authorisation; non-residents €30/week (natanti), €40/week (imbarcazioni); yachts over 24 m only in zone C anchorages, €150–500/day
rules.notes: Regno di Nettuno: 5 zones (A, B n.t., B, C, D); no anchoring in A and B n.t.; zone B residents only, dawn to dusk; zone C with authorisation; yacht anchorages off Forio, Maronti and Lacco Ameno. AMP Punta Campanella (Sorrento peninsula) also restricts navigation; its limits were not confirmed here. Bathing-ordinance strips apply along the coast.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Sirocco most common in spring and autumn (peaks March and November).

tides.notes: Microtidal Mediterranean coast; no confirmed range found. Wind and pressure change levels more than the tide.

authority.name: Capitanerie di porto Napoli, Pozzuoli, Castellammare di Stabia, Salerno; AMP Regno di Nettuno; AMP Punta Campanella

notes: Busy ferry and hydrofoil traffic between Naples, Pozzuoli, Procida, Ischia, Sorrento and Capri. Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: Aeolian islands (Lipari, Vulcano, Salina, Panarea, Stromboli, Filicudi, Alicudi)
reach: Milazzo / Portorosa – Vulcano – Lipari – Salina – Panarea – Stromboli; Filicudi and Alicudi to the west

depth.notes: Deep water close to the islands; few sheltered harbours.

locks.notes: Published legs (NM): Portorosa–Vulcano 20, Vulcano–Filicudi 20–23, Filicudi–Alicudi 13, Filicudi–Salina 14, Alicudi–Salina 26, Salina–Stromboli 20–22, Stromboli–Lipari 24–25, Lipari–Portorosa 22, Milazzo–Lipari 20.

rules.notes: Stromboli: Capitaneria di Milazzo ordinance 81/2022 bans navigation within 2 NM off the Sciara del Fuoco (NW flank); further bans can be issued at higher alert levels (2024: navigation, anchoring and stopping banned during the red alert). INGV reports persistent Strombolian activity with lava flows on the Sciara in 2026 and blocks thrown a few hundred metres off the coast.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Mistral sometimes reaches Sicily with Gulf of Genoa lows; sirocco peaks March and November.

tides.notes: Microtidal Mediterranean coast; no confirmed range found. Wind and pressure change levels more than the tide.

authority.name: Capitaneria di porto di Milazzo; Comune di Lipari (civil protection, Stromboli)

notes: Check the Stromboli alert level and ordinances before passing the NW flank. Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: North Sardinia: Costa Smeralda, La Maddalena archipelago, Strait of Bonifacio
reach: Olbia / Porto Rotondo – Porto Cervo – Cannigione – Palau – La Maddalena / Caprera – Santa Teresa Gallura – Bonifacio

depth.notes: Open sea; many rocks and shoals in the archipelago passes.

locks.notes: Published legs (NM): Porto Rotondo–Porto Cervo 10, Porto Cervo–La Maddalena 11, La Maddalena–Santa Teresa 12.2, Santa Teresa–Bonifacio 9–11, Bonifacio–Palau 16.2, Palau–Cannigione 7, Cannigione–Porto Rotondo 16, Palau–La Maddalena 1.9.

rules.permit: La Maddalena National Park entry ticket (daily) to navigate, moor and anchor in the park; online 5% cheaper, sailing boats 40% off; overnight park buoys €100–150 depending on month
rules.notes: Regulation 33/2026 (in force 2 June 2026, trial for 2026–2027, 1 Jun–30 Sep): 7 kn within 500 m of the coast, 10 kn 500–1000 m (zone MB); anchoring banned in transit/emergency corridors at Cala Connari and Cala Corsara (Spargi), Cala Santa Maria, Porto Madonna; swimming only within 5 m of the boat; explicit night anchoring ban dropped. Zone MA: no navigation or stopping. Spiaggia Rosa (Budelli): no navigation or anchoring; Passo Cecca Morto, del Topo and degli Asinelli closed to pleasure craft. Anchor only on sand or mud, never on Posidonia.

season.closures: Mistral regularly affects Sardinia and funnels through the Strait of Bonifacio.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Park speed and corridor rules apply 1 Jun–30 Sep; ticket season reported 15 May–31 Oct. Mistral most common in winter and spring.

tides.notes: Microtidal Mediterranean coast; no confirmed range found. Wind and pressure change levels more than the tide.

authority.name: Ente Parco Nazionale Arcipelago di La Maddalena (authorisations 0789 790224, autorizzazioni@lamaddalenapark.it); Capitaneria di porto La Maddalena

notes: Speed limit field is the 7 kn (13 km/h) inshore limit. Tickets: autorizzazioni.lamaddalenapark.it or partner outlets. The French side (Bonifacio) has its own reserve rules (not covered). Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: West Sicily and the Egadi islands (Trapani, Favignana, Levanzo, Marettimo, Marsala)
reach: Marsala – Trapani – Levanzo – Favignana – Marettimo; San Vito Lo Capo

depth.notes: Open sea; shallow Stagnone lagoon north of Marsala.

locks.notes: Published legs (NM): Marsala–Trapani 15.4, Trapani–Levanzo 7.8, Trapani–Favignana 9–10, Levanzo–Marettimo 12–12.8, Favignana–Marettimo 13, Levanzo–San Vito Lo Capo 25.

rules.permit: AMP Isole Egadi: authorisation and fee (weekly/monthly/annual for anchoring; daily to annual for mooring) for non-residents
rules.notes: AMP Egadi (DM 1.6.2010): zones A–D. No jet skis or water-skiing in A, B, C (transit at 5 kn in B); no navigation in zone A of Maraone; zone B within 500 m: motor navigation, mooring and anchoring only for authorised residents' boats (Marettimo zone B: limited number of natanti); beyond 500 m and in C/D free navigation; anchoring allowed outside signed Posidonia/coralligenous seabeds; no anchoring in A. 181 buoys in 17 mooring fields; moor only to the assigned buoy.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Sirocco peaks March and November; mistral sometimes reaches Sicily.

tides.notes: Microtidal Mediterranean coast; no confirmed range found. Wind and pressure change levels more than the tide.

authority.name: AMP Isole Egadi (Comune di Favignana), info@ampisoleegadi.it, 0923 921659; Capitaneria di porto Trapani

notes: Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: Gulf of Venice and the northern Adriatic coast (Chioggia – Venice – Caorle – Lignano – Grado – Trieste)
reach: Po delta / Porto Levante – Chioggia – Venice (Lido, Malamocco and Chioggia inlets) – Jesolo – Caorle – Lignano – Grado – Trieste

depth.notes: Shallow sandy coast with shifting bars at river mouths; enter the lagoons by the marked inlets.

locks.notes: MOSE barriers close the Lido, Malamocco and Chioggia inlets during forecast high tides. Rotta dei Dogi Chioggia–Trieste about 110 miles (italia.it).

rules.notes: Bathing ordinances, e.g. Lignano 2026: swimmers' zone 400 m, 10 kn between 400 m and 1000 m from the beach; cross in launch corridors at 3 kn.

season.closures: Bora (NE) gales in winter, strongest at Trieste (gusts usually above 120 km/h); sirocco in spring and autumn drives acqua alta.

months.notes: Sea route, no closures. Bora most common in winter; sirocco peaks March and November; acqua alta mainly autumn to spring, many records in November.

tides.notes: The largest tides in the Mediterranean; semi-diurnal. Sirocco and bora hold water in the lagoon (acqua alta); range not confirmed here.

authority.name: Capitanerie di porto Chioggia, Venezia, Monfalcone, Trieste

notes: Italian rule (D.Lgs. 171/2005 art. 39): patente nautica beyond 6 NM from the coast, for jet skis, and within 6 NM for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV (or over the displacement limits); foreign boats follow their flag state's licence rules (not verified).

name: Po (Piacenza – Cremona – Pontelagoscuro – Volta Grimana – delta)
reach: Piacenza – Isola Serafini lock – Cremona – Foce Mincio (Governolo) – Pontelagoscuro (Ferrara) – Volta Grimana – Porto Tolle / delta

depth.notes: Free-flowing below Isola Serafini; the low-water channel between Pontelagoscuro and Foce Mincio is unstable and the hardest reach; Cremona–Foce Mincio regulated by groynes but bars still form. No direct exit to sea: bars at the mouths.

current.notes: Gradient about 18 cm/km Cremona–Mantova, about 4 cm/km in the lowest reach.

locks.notes: Isola Serafini (new lock completed 2017, the only lock on the Po) reopens Cremona–Piacenza (37 km). Exits: Volta Grimana lock 30 km above the mouth (Po di Levante, Po–Brondolo to Chioggia); Pontelagoscuro lock 90 km above the mouth (Idrovia Ferrarese).

season.closures: Low water and floods; sand bars shift. Headroom under bridges sufficient about 340 days in an average year.

months.notes: Low-water draft limits and floods vary by year; no month pattern confirmed from official sources.

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: AIPo (Agenzia Interregionale per il fiume Po); Regione Emilia-Romagna navigazione interna

notes: Distances (PRIT): Po Foce Ticino–sea 389 km; commercially usable Cremona–Porto Tolle 275 km; about 300 km Piacenza–sea; Cremona–Foce Mincio 130 km; Pontelagoscuro–Foce Mincio 68 km; Cremona port 300 km from the sea. Patente nautica on inland waters for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV.

name: Mincio (Mantova lakes – Governolo – Po)
reach: Mantova (Lago Superiore, di Mezzo, Inferiore, Valdaro port) – Governolo – confluence with the Po

locks.notes: Conca di Governolo and Conca di San Leone link the Po with the Mincio, Mantova port and the Fissero-Tartaro-Canalbianco.

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Lombardia – navigazione laghi, fiumi e navigli

notes: Mantova–Po 21 km (20 km via Governolo commercially usable). Mantova port is 150 km from the sea via the Fissero-Tartaro-Canalbianco.

name: Idrovia Fissero – Tartaro – Canalbianco – Po di Levante (Mantova – Porto Levante)
reach: Mantova (Valdaro) – Trevenzuolo – Torretta – Canda – Bussari – Baricetta – Po di Levante (Volta Grimana) – Porto Levante (Adriatic)

locks.hours: Trevenzuolo, Torretta, Canda, Bussari, Baricetta and Volta Grimana: 24 h all year, on booking (2023 schedule)
locks.notes: Operated by the Veneto inland navigation office at Cavanella d'Adige (041 8306862).

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Veneto – Uffici navigazione interna (Cavanella d'Adige); Infrastrutture Venete

notes: 135 km Mantova–sea (italia.it 130 km; 117 km to the Po di Levante incile, then 19 km of Po di Levante). Mantova–Venice open 365 days a year per the port of Venice. In the routing data the canal does not currently carry Mantova–Porto Levante traffic (routes go by the Po).

name: Idrovia Ferrarese (Pontelagoscuro – Ferrara – Migliarino – Porto Garibaldi)
reach: Pontelagoscuro lock on the Po – Canale Boicelli (5.5 km) – Po di Volano to Migliarino (km 41) – Valpagliaro lock (km 30) – Valle Lepri lock (km 58) – Porto Garibaldi (km 70)

depth.notes: Three levels: Pontelagoscuro–Valpagliaro 30 km at 4.60 m a.s.l., Valpagliaro–Valle Lepri 27 km at 1.50 m, last 13 km tidal. The Pontelagoscuro lock sill became too high as the Po bed sank, blocking passage for long periods (status not confirmed for 2026).

locks.chamber: Valle Lepri 97 × 12.30 m; Pontelagoscuro usable width 8.20 m
locks.notes: Pontelagoscuro (twin lock), Valpagliaro (3.10 m lift), Valle Lepri. Bookings with the Regione Emilia-Romagna navigation office in Ferrara.

rules.notes: Max 15 km/h for pleasure craft, 6 km/h for commercial vessels, also on straight reaches.

tides.notes: Below Valle Lepri the canal is open to the sea: levels normally up to +0.60 m a.s.l., maxima +0.90 m.

authority.name: Regione Emilia-Romagna – Agenzia per la sicurezza territoriale e la protezione civile, navigazione interna (Ferrara)

notes: Works to upgrade the idrovia to class V (bridges Bardella, Betto, Confortino, rail bridge on the Boicelli) ongoing; check headroom notices.

name: Idrovia Po – Brondolo (Volta Grimana – Cavanella – Chioggia)
reach: Volta Grimana lock on the Po – Cavanella d'Adige – Brondolo lock – Venetian lagoon at Chioggia

locks.hours: Volta Grimana, Cavanella Sx, Cavanella Dx, Brondolo: 24 h all year, on booking (2023 schedule)
locks.notes: Veneto navigation office, Cavanella d'Adige (041 8306862).

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Veneto – Uffici navigazione interna (Cavanella d'Adige)

notes: The usual link from the Po to Chioggia and Venice; Chioggia–Venice through the lagoon about 30 km.

name: Venetian lagoon (Chioggia – Pellestrina – Lido – Venice – Murano – Burano – Torcello)
reach: Chioggia – Pellestrina – Malamocco – Lido – Venice (Bacino di San Marco, Giudecca) – Murano – Burano – Torcello – Treporti/Cavallino

depth.notes: Shallow lagoon: keep to the marked channels (bricole).

locks.notes: MOSE barriers at the Lido, Malamocco and Chioggia inlets close during forecast high tides.

rules.notes: Max 20 km/h anywhere in the lagoon; 8 km/h in most channels across shoals or along islands; 5 km/h in small channels north of Torcello; Murano 7 (main inner canal), 5 (other inner), 8 (outer); Burano 8 outer, 11 Torcello–Burano, 5 inner. Average-speed cameras (barcavelox) on main canals. Pleasure boats may not use the Canal Grande and its side canals; jet skis banned.

months.notes: Acqua alta mainly autumn to spring (many record events in November); MOSE closures then.

tides.notes: Acqua alta 80–109 cm 'intense', 140 cm+ 'exceptional'; sirocco and bora raise levels. Forecasts: Centro Maree, +39 041 241 1996.

authority.name: Comune di Venezia (traffico acqueo, Testo Unico ord. 274/2015); Capitaneria di porto di Venezia; Provincia/Città metropolitana

notes: Motorboats over 10 hp need a registration; foreign-registered boats are accepted. Speed-limit maps are available at the marinas. Chioggia–Venice inside the lagoon about 26–30 km.

aliases: Canale dei Pantani (o Canal de Bevazzana)
reach: Portegrandi (Venetian lagoon) – Taglio del Sile – Cavallino – Cavetta (Jesolo, Cortellazzo/Piave) – Revedoli – Caorle – Lovi – Bevazzana (Tagliamento) – Marano and Grado lagoons – Foce Isonzo

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Veneto – navigazione interna; Infrastrutture Venete; Regione Friuli Venezia Giulia (Marano–Grado)

notes: 2026: dredging to restore depths between Sant'Andrea and the Aussa canal (FVG). Small pleasure craft; check bridge clearances locally (not confirmed).

name: Riviera del Brenta (Padova – Stra – Dolo – Mira – Fusina)
reach: Padova (Piovego) – Noventa – Stra – Dolo – Mira – Moranzani – Fusina (Venetian lagoon)

locks.hours: Summer 1 Apr–31 Oct 2023: Battaglia, Voltabarozzo, Noventa, Stra 08:00–19:00 Tue–Sun (closed Mondays unless a holiday); Dolo, Mira, Moranzani 24 h; all on booking
locks.notes: Locks Battaglia, Voltabarozzo, Noventa, Stra (348 0990296), Dolo, Mira, Moranzani (041 8306862). Swing bridges on the Riviera del Brenta on request (342 8056791).

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Veneto – navigazione interna; Infrastrutture Venete

notes: Winter lock hours differ: check the regional schedule before travelling.

name: Lago di Garda (Desenzano – Sirmione – Peschiera – Garda – Malcesine – Limone – Riva del Garda)
reach: Whole lake: Desenzano, Sirmione and Peschiera in the south to Riva del Garda and Torbole (Trentino) in the north

rules.permit: Trentino (northern) waters: motor navigation needs an authorisation from the Provincia di Trento
rules.notes: Lombardy shore: 300 m band for sail, oars and pedals only (150 m in parts of Salò and the Riviera), motorboats cross it only to land or leave, perpendicular, max 3 kn; elsewhere max 20 kn by day, 5 kn at night. From 1 Jan 2027 (Veneto L.R. 6/2026, interregional text; Lombardy approved a matching law) hulls and engines of boats coming from other waters must be sanitised before launching (quagga mussel, found 2022).

season.closures: Winds: Pelèr (N) from night to about noon, Ora (S) in the afternoon, strong in the upper lake.

months.notes: No closures. Pelèr/Ora daily cycle in fair weather.

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Lombardia, Regione Veneto, Provincia autonoma di Trento (shore by shore)

notes: Speed field: 20 kn by day (Lombardy rule). Patente nautica for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV. Rules differ by shore; check the local ordinance.

name: Lago Maggiore (Sesto Calende – Arona – Stresa – Verbania – Cannobio – Locarno)
reach: Whole lake from the Ticino outflow at Sesto Calende to Locarno/Tenero (Switzerland)

rules.notes: Piedmont shore (reg. 5/R 2009): 150 m shore band, motorboats only to land or leave at about 5 kn. Lombardy and Swiss (Ticino) shores have their own rules; Swiss rules differ for motor craft (not detailed here).

season.closures: Winds: morning N wind from the Monte Ceneri (moscendrino/tramontana), afternoon S breeze (inverna); the NE 'maggiore' is dangerous; strong in the narrow upper lake.

months.notes: No closures.

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Piemonte, Regione Lombardia, Canton Ticino

notes: Length 64.37 km, the longest Italian lake. Patente nautica for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV on the Italian part. The lake has no name in the routing data (legs show as unnamed), so the alias may not match until it does.

name: Lago di Como (Como – Bellagio – Menaggio – Varenna – Colico – Gera Lario; Lecco branch)
reach: Como to Gera Lario (45.7 km), with the Lecco branch and the Garlate/Olginate lakes on the Adda

season.closures: Storm winds such as the menaggino are dangerous for small boats.

months.notes: No closures.

tides.notes: Non-tidal inland water.

authority.name: Regione Lombardia; Autorità di bacino del Lario e dei laghi minori

notes: Max depth about 410–418 m (between Argegno and Nesso). Patente nautica for engines over 30 kW / 40.8 CV.

name: Canal du Nivernais (Auxerre – Clamecy – Baye summit – Decize)
aliases: Canal du Nivernais - Bief de Partage des Eaux
Canal du Nivernais Embranchement de Vermenton
Porte de Garde No 60 de Mailly-le-Chateau
Écluse de Garde de Cercy la Tour
reach: Auxerre, lock 81 VS du Batardeau (PK 173.8), up the Yonne valley (canal sections and canalised Yonne) via Mailly-la-Ville (PK ~145), Clamecy (PK ~114) and Tannay (PK ~98), the Sardy flight and La Collancelle tunnels to the Baye summit, down the Aron valley via Châtillon-en-Bazois (PK ~53) to the Loire at Decize (PK 0)

depth.notes: Mouillage 1.60 m (fr.wikipedia). Lock walls in poor condition in places.

current.notes: Canal with river sections on the canalised Yonne between Auxerre and Clamecy; current there after rain.

locks.chamber: 39 × 5.20 m on most of both sides; 30 × 5.20 m from lock 15 VS to 31 VL (central section); lock 1 VL Baye 40 × 5.20 m
locks.hours: High season daily 09:00–12:00, 13:00–19:00. Shoulder (17 Mar to the last Friday before summer time, and Monday after winter time to 10 Nov): weekdays 09:00–12:00, 13:30–17:00, weekends closed. Low season 1 Jan–16 Mar and 11 Nov–31 Dec: navigation interrompue. Closed 1 Jan, 1 May, 1 Nov, 11 Nov, 25 Dec.
locks.notes: All locks manual, worked by VNF or Nièvre éclusiers. Lock 81 VS–16 VS: VNF ST Nivernais-Yonne, Auxerre (03 58 43 21 64); 15 VS–30 VL: Conseil départemental de la Nièvre (03 86 93 57 66, canal.nivernais@nievre.fr); 31 VL–35 VL: VNF ST Val-de-Loire-Seine, Briare. Sardy flight (16 locks in ~3 km) and three tunnels at La Collancelle (758, 268, 212 m).

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: RPP voies touristiques de Centre-Bourgogne: 8 km/h on the whole canal.

season.closures: Navigation interrompue 1 Jan–16 Mar and 11 Nov–31 Dec (VNF avis à la batellerie n°1 2026); reduced weekday-only service in the shoulder months.

months.notes: Jan–mid-Mar and from 11 Nov: no lock service (official 2026 schedule). March and November are partly closed; shoulder months weekdays only.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: VNF DT Centre-Bourgogne (ST Nivernais-Yonne, Auxerre) and Conseil départemental de la Nièvre (central section)

notes: Lowest bridge 2.71 m (Mougny, PK 62); arches 3.5 m at centre only. Hire bases at Migennes, Auxerre, Tannay and elsewhere (Le Boat Migennes–Tannay one-way: 104 km, 46 locks, ~27 h). Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Canal de la Marne au Rhin, branche est (Frouard/Nancy – Lagarde – Arzviller – Saverne – Strasbourg)
aliases: Canal de la Marne au Rhin
Ancien Canal de la Marne au Rhin
reach: Moselle at Frouard (PK 154.5) via Nancy (164), Dombasle, Réchicourt (222), Gondrexange (228, junction with the Canal de la Sarre), the Saint-Louis–Arzviller inclined plane (255), Lutzelbourg (259), Saverne (269), Hochfelden (286) to Strasbourg (313; Ill at PK 311)

depth.notes: Mouillage normally 2.20–2.60 m; on 19 Nov 2026 limited to 1.80 m Frouard–Réchicourt and Réchicourt–plane, Henridorff–Lupstein, 2.20 m Ingenheim–Schiltigheim (water management, to 30 Nov 2026).

current.notes: Canal, no current.

locks.chamber: Freycinet, 38.50 × 5.05 m (max boat); Réchicourt lock 15.70 m fall; Saint-Louis–Arzviller inclined plane (44.5 m, replaced 17 locks in 1969)
locks.hours: Locks daily 09:00–17:00 at least, most 07:00–19:00 in peak season; closed 1 May. Inclined plane daily 07:00–18:00 (07:00–19:00 15 Jun–15 Jul), closed 1 May; ~15 min transit plus waits of 30 min–2 h in busy periods.
locks.notes: Locks towards Nancy by remote control (handed out at Réchicourt); towards Saverne automatic (triggered by perches/chains). Niderviller (475 m) and Arzviller (2,306 m) tunnels are one-way, light-controlled: enter on green only. 16 Nov–25 Nov 2026: navigation stopped at Réchicourt lock 2 (avarie, FR/2026/08954-0).

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: 8 km/h on the canal (Le Boat Alsace guide); lower in ports.

season.closures: Réchicourt lock 2 stopped 16–25 Nov 2026; draught limits in summer–autumn 2026 for water shortage.

months.notes: 2026: draught limited to 1.80 m on most of the branch from 24 Jul to 30 Nov (one year of data). Chômages announced by avis à la batellerie.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: VNF DT Nord-Est (Frouard–Réchicourt) and DT Strasbourg (Réchicourt–Strasbourg)

notes: Hire bases at Lagarde, Hesse, Niderviller, Lutzelbourg, Saverne. Le Boat Hesse–Lutzelbourg 19 km (2 tunnels, plane, 4 locks), Lutzelbourg–Saverne 10.3 km, 10 locks. Strasbourg: moor at the port de plaisance; the Ill through the city is used by tour boats. Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Canal de la Sarre (Gondrexange – Mittersheim – Sarralbe – Sarreguemines) and the French Sarre
aliases: Canal des Houillères de la Sarre
reach: Marne-Rhine canal at Gondrexange via Mittersheim, Harskirchen, Sarralbe and Wittring (lock 27) to Sarreguemines, then the canalised Sarre to Grosbliederstroff/Saarbrücken

depth.notes: Built for 38 × 5 m boats of 1.80 m draught. On 19 Nov 2026: closed Kerprich lock 1–Mittersheim lock 13 (water shortage, to 30 Nov 2026), draught limited to 1.60 m from lock 13 to Wittring lock 27 and 1.80 m from the junction to lock 1.

current.notes: Canal; some current on the canalised Sarre after rain.

locks.chamber: Freycinet (38 × 5 m boats)
locks.hours: Daily 09:00–17:00 at least, most 07:00–19:00 in peak season; closed 1 May (Le Boat Alsace guide).
locks.notes: Automated locks; remote control handed out on board (Sarreguemines direction). French Sarre adds 2–3 locks to Sarreguemines/Grosbliederstroff.

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: German Saar beyond Sarreguemines: German rules (BinSchStrO), Sportbootführerschein or ICC.

season.closures: 2026: Kerprich–Mittersheim closed from 19 Oct to 30 Nov for lack of water (FR/2026/08464-1).

months.notes: 2026: draught limits from 24 Jul and closure of the summit section from 19 Oct (one year of data). The Sarre loop (Sarre–Moselle–Marne-Rhine) is a classic week from Lagarde/Hesse.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: VNF DT Strasbourg

notes: Ports at Mittersheim, Harskirchen, Sarralbe, Wittring, Sarreguemines. Mittersheim lake feeds the summit. Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Lot (Luzech – Cahors – Saint-Cirq-Lapopie – Larnagol; lower Lot Aiguillon – Fumel)
reach: Upper (Quercy) section Luzech – Douelle – Cahors – Vers – Bouziès – Saint-Cirq-Lapopie – Larnagol (74 km, 17 locks); lower section from the Garonne/Canal de Garonne at Aiguillon to Fumel (85 km, 6 locks). The gap Fumel–Luzech is not navigable (transbordement at Montayral)

depth.notes: Upper Lot: draught 1.0 m (Cirkwi route sheet).

current.notes: River: flow rises quickly after storms; locks are next to weirs, keep clear of the weir side.

locks.chamber: Upper Lot ~30 × 5 m
locks.notes: Upper Lot: 17 locks, no lock-keepers, all manual and boater-operated (one exception); fit crew needed. Lower Lot: 6 locks Aiguillon–Fumel, including Villeneuve-sur-Lot (13 m).

rules.notes: Not on the VNF network: managed by the Départements (Lot, Lot-et-Garonne).

season.closures: Hire season April–October; navigation depends on river flow.

months.notes: Season April–October (tourism and hire sources); no lock service found outside it. Flow-dependent.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: Département du Lot (Luzech–Larnagol); Département de Lot-et-Garonne (lower Lot)

notes: Hire bases Douelle, Cahors, Bouziès, Luzech. Le Boat Douelle round trip via Saint-Cirq-Lapopie: 99 km, 28 locks, ~22.5 h. Air draught given as 3.7 m (another source 4.40 m). Moorings at Cahors, Vers, Bouziès, Saint-Cirq-Lapopie.

name: Charente (Angoulême – Jarnac – Cognac – Saintes – Saint-Savinien – Tonnay-Charente)
reach: Angoulême (pont Saint-Antoine, PK ~26) via Châteauneuf, Jarnac (PK ~71), Cognac (PK ~86), Saintes (PK ~120), the Saint-Savinien barrage-lock (PK 142.9) to Tonnay-Charente (PK 164) and on, tidal, past Rochefort to the sea

depth.notes: Shallower upstream of Cognac; maritime section below Saint-Savinien deep but tidal.

current.notes: River; tidal below Saint-Savinien, felt faintly to Saintes.

locks.chamber: Charente dept: 31.0–39.6 × 6.06–7.40 m (Crouin 49 × 6.50 m); La Baine (Chaniers) 34.80 × 6.50 m; Saint-Savinien barrage lock 51 × 8 m
locks.notes: 19 locks in Charente (Saint-Cybard to Crouin) and 2 in Charente-Maritime. Weir approach channels are closed to all navigation.

rules.notes: RPP Charente (Angoulême–Tonnay): 5 km/h zones in towns (Angoulême, Châteauneuf, Jarnac, Saint-Brice, Saintes, Tonnay), 45–60 km/h water-ski zones; anchoring banned in listed reaches (Angoulême, Saintes, Port d'Envaux–Taillebourg). Not on the VNF network.

months.notes: No recurring closures found.

tides.notes: Tidal range 6.50 m at the mouth, 5.40 m at Rochefort, 1.80 m at Saint-Savinien, 0.18 m at Saintes (1973 survey); the Saint-Savinien barrage damps it. Time the maritime Charente (Tonnay–Rochefort–sea) with the tide.

authority.name: Départements de la Charente and Charente-Maritime (fleuve Charente); police: DDT 16 / DDTM 17

notes: Lowest bridges at PHEN: Saint-Savinien barrage 2.80 m, new Saint-Savinien bridge 3.00 m, Chatenay (Cognac) 3.20 m, Jarnac 3.60 m. Hire base at Jarnac (Le Boat: Jarnac–Cognac 13.9 km/3 locks, Cognac–Saintes 33.6 km/2, Saintes–Saint-Savinien 22.4 km). Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Baïse (Canal de Garonne at Buzet – Nérac – Condom – Valence-sur-Baïse)
reach: Garonne/Canal de Garonne junctions at Buzet-sur-Baïse (double lock from the canal) via Vianne, Lavardac, Nérac, Moncrabeau and Condom to Valence-sur-Baïse (Moulin de Camarade, limit)

current.notes: Canalised river; flow after rain.

locks.notes: Buzet–Moncrabeau 45 km, 14 locks (Lot-et-Garonne); on to Condom and Valence-sur-Baïse (Gers). Double junction lock with the Canal de Garonne at Buzet.

months.notes: No closure data found.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: Département de Lot-et-Garonne (Lot-et-Garonne section)

notes: Ports at Buzet, Nérac, Condom. Distances (CanalPlan): Garonne junction 65 km to Valence-sur-Baïse, Nérac port 39.3 km from Valence, Condom quay 12.5 km. Pont-canal of the Canal de Garonne crosses the Baïse near Feugarolles.

name: Canal du Rhône à Sète (Beaucaire/Saint-Gilles – Aigues-Mortes – Palavas – Frontignan – Sète)
aliases: Canal du Rhône à Sète - Embranchement de Saint-Gilles
Canaux et port de plaisance de Sète
reach: Petit Rhône via the Saint-Gilles lock (VNF PK 0.4) along the Camargue lagoons via Gallician, the Aigues-Mortes branches, La Grande-Motte, Palavas (Lez crossing) and Frontignan to the port of Sète (PK 65.1); small-gauge Beaucaire–Saint-Gilles branch (Nourriguier lock)
class: Grand gabarit (1200 t convoys) on the main line; small gauge on the Beaucaire branch

depth.notes: Silting: mouillage limited to 2.30 m Saint-Gilles–Sète, 2.20 m in the Aigues-Mortes branch, 1.80 m at PK 1.4–1.9 of the Frontignan branch (avis to 31 Jan 2027).

current.notes: Canal through lagoons; wind sets up water level. Vidourle crossing with flood gates.

locks.notes: Saint-Gilles lock links the Petit Rhône; Beaucaire lock to the Rhône closed since the Vallabrègues dam. Nourriguier lock (Beaucaire branch) in chômage 26 Oct–4 Dec 2026.

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more
rules.notes: Frontignan lifting bridge opens at fixed times (Le Boat: usually 09:30 and 16:00; Jul–Aug 09:30, 13:00, 16:30; Nov–Mar 16:00 only).

season.closures: Floods: navigation stopped 12–15 Nov 2026 on the whole canal (Vidourle floods).

months.notes: Open all year; autumn Cévenol/Vidourle floods can stop navigation for days (Nov 2026).

tides.notes: Lagoon canal at sea level; wind and storm surge change levels slightly. Sea access at Sète, Palavas and Le Grau-du-Roi (Aigues-Mortes maritime canal).

authority.name: VNF DT Rhône-Saône

notes: Headroom 4.63 m in the Aigues-Mortes branch (Radelle rail bridge) at bief +70 cm NGF. Hire bases at Saint-Gilles, Gallician, Aigues-Mortes, Lattes, Port Cassafières. Distances (fr/en Wikipedia PK): Beaucaire 0, Saint-Gilles 24.5, Aigues-Mortes 51, Palavas 75.5, Frontignan 92–93, Sète 98–100. Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Petit Rhône (Arles/Fourques defluence – Saint-Gilles – sea)
reach: Defluence from the Rhône at Fourques/Arles (PK 279.3) past the Saint-Gilles lock junction to the sea west of Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer (PK 337.7)

depth.notes: Low water Nov 2026: mouillage close to the guaranteed depth (to 30 Nov). Shoal PK 295.8–296.2 (to 28 Feb 2027); silting at PK 293.2 right bank — keep to the left bank.

current.notes: Free-flowing river arm of the Rhône; current depends on Rhône flow.

locks.notes: No locks on the arm; the Saint-Gilles lock leads into the Canal du Rhône à Sète.

rules.permit: VNF vignette (péage plaisance) for boats over 5 m or with an engine of 9.9 CV (7.29 kW) or more

months.notes: Rhône floods can stop navigation (check CNR/VNF notices).

tides.notes: Mouth on the microtidal Mediterranean; sea entrance subject to silting.

authority.name: VNF DT Rhône-Saône

notes: Main large-gauge route from the Rhône to the Canal du Rhône à Sète. Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Canal de Nantes à Brest (Nantes – Erdre – Redon – Oust – Josselin – Pontivy; Finistère section)
aliases: Canal de Nantes à Brest - L'Oust Canalisé
Canal de Nantes à Brest (Bief de Partage)
reach: Nantes (Erdre, PK 2) via Nort-sur-Erdre, the Isac, Redon (95, crossing the Vilaine), the Oust (Malestroit 132, Josselin 157.5), Rohan (182) to Pontivy (205.9). Pontivy–Goariva interrupted by the Guerlédan dam; Finistère section Port-de-Carhaix – Châteaulin (Aulne, 81 km) then the tidal Aulne to the Rade de Brest

current.notes: Canalised rivers (Erdre, Isac, Oust, Aulne): current after rain.

locks.chamber: Max boat 25.70 × 4.65 m
locks.notes: 107 locks Nantes–Pontivy (206 km), 45 in Finistère. Dense flights on the summit approaches (Hilvern/Rohan side).

rules.notes: Breton section owned by the Région Bretagne (not VNF); short Loire-Atlantique part in Pays de la Loire.

months.notes: No closure dates found; ask the Région Bretagne / Loire-Atlantique for chômages.

tides.notes: Non-tidal except the Aulne maritime below Châteaulin/Port-Launay (tidal Rade de Brest).

authority.name: Région Bretagne (Breton section); Département de Loire-Atlantique (Nantes–Redon part)

notes: Le Boat Messac base: Malestroit–Saint-Martin-sur-Oust 14 km/3 locks, Saint-Martin–Redon 22 km/3 locks. Redon is the crossroads with the Vilaine (to Arzal and the sea, see the Vilaine sheet). Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Mayenne and Maine (Mayenne – Laval – Château-Gontier – Grez-Neuville – Angers – Loire)
reach: Mayenne town (lock 1) via Laval (35 km), Château-Gontier (70), Daon (83), Chenillé-Changé (89), Oudon junction (100), Grez-Neuville (101.5) to the Sarthe/Maine junction at Angers (122); Maine 11.3 km to the Loire at Bouchemaine

current.notes: Canalised river; current and closures in winter floods.

locks.chamber: 30 × 5.20 m (Becquey)
locks.hours: Basin of the Maine (2021 avis): locks usable 09:00–17:00 in winter and 09:00–20:00 from late March to 31 October; never at night or in thunderstorms. Boaters may work locks themselves within these hours when no keeper is present (disc signals).
locks.notes: 45 locks Mayenne–Angers (CanalPlan), 1 on the Maine (Bouchemaine). Laval lock fully automated. Keepers' hours vary by section and month.

rules.notes: Departmental rivers (Mayenne, Maine-et-Loire), not VNF.

season.closures: Partial chômages in autumn in Maine-et-Loire (e.g. 2021: Mayenne in Maine-et-Loire and Oudon 8 Sep–15 Dec).

months.notes: Open all year with shorter winter hours; autumn chômages on the Maine-et-Loire part in some years.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: Département de la Mayenne (02 43 59 93 60) and Département de Maine-et-Loire (02 41 81 41 39)

notes: Headroom 3.5 m except 2.7 m under the pont de l'Europe at Laval. Hire base at Chenillé-Changé, Château-Gontier and others. Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Sarthe (Le Mans – Malicorne – Sablé – Châteauneuf – Angers)
reach: Le Mans (head) via Spay, La Suze, Malicorne (47 km), Parcé, Juigné, Solesmes, Sablé-sur-Sarthe (73), Morannes, Châteauneuf-sur-Sarthe (103), Cheffes, Briollay (Loir junction 123) to the Mayenne/Maine junction at Angers (132)

depth.notes: Shoals in some reaches; keep to the marked channel.

current.notes: Canalised river; winter floods.

locks.hours: Basin of the Maine (2021 avis): 09:00–17:00 in winter, 09:00–20:00 late March–31 October; Sarthe dept locks staffed on set days, otherwise self-operated within hours; Sablé (15) automated.
locks.notes: 16 locks in Sarthe dept (Le Mans 1 – Beffes 16), 4 in Maine-et-Loire (Pendu 17 – Cheffes 20).

rules.notes: Departmental river (Sarthe, Maine-et-Loire), not VNF.

months.notes: Open all year with reduced winter service.

tides.notes: Inland canal/canalised river, non-tidal.

authority.name: Département de la Sarthe (02 43 54 72 71) and Département de Maine-et-Loire

notes: Hire bases at Sablé-sur-Sarthe and on the Mayenne (Anjou rivers). Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Canal de la Somme (Saint-Valery-sur-Somme – Abbeville – Amiens – Péronne)
reach: Sea lock at Saint-Valery-sur-Somme (PK 156) via the canal maritime to Abbeville (141), Amiens (92) to Péronne (34) where the Canal du Nord takes over; Voyennes–Saint-Simon closed

current.notes: Canalised river.

locks.notes: Saint-Valery–Abbeville 14.2 km, 1 lock (canal maritime); Abbeville–Péronne 105.3 km, 18 locks. Sea lock at Saint-Valery opens around high water.

rules.notes: Owned and run by the Département de la Somme (Direction du Fleuve et des Ports, 03 60 01 52 00), not VNF; travel times based on 6 km/h maximum.

months.notes: Season announced yearly by the Département (opening press release April 2026).

tides.notes: Canal non-tidal; the Baie de Somme outside the Saint-Valery sea lock is tidal and dries widely — time arrival/departure at high water.

authority.name: Département de la Somme – Direction du Fleuve et des Ports

notes: Moorings at Saint-Valery (130 m pontoon before the sea lock), Abbeville, Amiens, Corbie, Péronne. The Canal du Nord sheet covers the Péronne–Voyennes stretch. Permis plaisance option eaux intérieures (or recognised foreign licence/ICC) for engines over 4.5 kW (6 hp).

name: Calanques National Park (Marseille – Riou – Cassis – La Ciotat)
reach: Marseille (Pointe Rouge, Frioul) along the Calanques and the Riou archipelago to Cassis and La Ciotat

depth.notes: Open sea; check harbour depths and sills.

rules.notes: Parc national des Calanques: max 5 kn in the 300 m strip; no navigating, anchoring or landing in prohibited zones; do not tie up to yellow buoys; jet-skis, kitesurf, wing-foil and other motorised water toys banned; no fishing in non-take zones (zones de non-prélèvement); no noise, litter, drones; rental boats need park authorisation.

season.closures: Mistral (NW) can blow for days and raises steep seas off the Calanques; check Météo-France BMS.

months.notes: Mistral most frequent in winter and spring. Summer crowding in the calanques; anchoring zones regulated.

tides.notes: Microtidal (≈0.2–0.3 m); wind and pressure surges matter more.

authority.name: Préfecture maritime de la Méditerranée / CROSS MED La Garde (VHF 16)

notes: Weather VHF: Planier ch 80 (07:33, 13:33, 19:33), Toulon Mt-Coudon ch 63 (cycle). Harbours: Marseille Vieux-Port, Frioul, Pointe Rouge, Cassis (small, busy), La Ciotat. Sea: permis plaisance option côtière for engines over 4.5 kW; Division 240 equipment (basic < 2 NM from shelter, coastal 2–6 NM). Inland-only boats may not be fit for sea: check CE design category and insurance.

name: Îles d'Hyères (Porquerolles, Port-Cros) and Côte d'Azur to the Îles de Lérins
reach: Toulon – Giens – Porquerolles – Port-Cros – Le Lavandou – Cavalaire – Saint-Tropez – Estérel – Cannes and the Îles de Lérins (Sainte-Marguerite, Saint-Honorat) – Antibes

depth.notes: Open sea; check harbour depths and sills.

rules.notes: Port-Cros National Park: traffic, speed and anchoring zones around Port-Cros and Porquerolles set by prefectoral orders 2023_117 and 2023_116 (marked plans, ZMEL mooring buoys at Bagaud); the Bagaud island and Gabinière reef are integral reserves closed to access. General sea rules: 5 kn in the 300 m strip and channels; posidonia anchoring restrictions for large yachts.

season.closures: Mistral (NW, often violent between the Rhône and the Hyères islands); easterly gales with swell on the Var coast.

months.notes: Mistral mostly winter–spring, shorter in summer; ~81 mistral days/yr at Toulon (Wikipedia). July–August very crowded, book berths.

tides.notes: Microtidal (≈0.2–0.3 m); wind and pressure surges matter more.

authority.name: Préfecture maritime de la Méditerranée / CROSS MED La Garde (VHF 16)

notes: Weather VHF: Camarat ch 80 (07:46, 13:46, 19:46), Toulon ch 63, Cannes Pic de l'Ours ch 64 (cycle), Monaco Radio ch 23/25. Published legs: Hyères–Port-Cros 11 NM, Port-Cros–Porquerolles 6, Porquerolles–Saint-Tropez 24.5, Lérins–Saint-Tropez 26, Cannes–Sainte-Marguerite 2. Sea: permis plaisance option côtière for engines over 4.5 kW; Division 240 equipment (basic < 2 NM from shelter, coastal 2–6 NM). Inland-only boats may not be fit for sea: check CE design category and insurance.

name: Corsica coast (Calvi – Girolata – Ajaccio – Propriano – Bonifacio – Porto-Vecchio – Bastia)
reach: All Corsican coasts, including the Bouches de Bonifacio (strait to Sardinia), the Lavezzi and Cerbicale islands

depth.notes: Open sea; check harbour depths and sills.

rules.notes: Réserve naturelle des Bouches de Bonifacio (decree of 23 Sept 1999, ~79,000 ha of sea, managed by the Office de l'environnement de la Corse): fishing regulated (prefectoral orders 2004 underwater fishing, 2018 recreational), protected islands (Lavezzi, Cerbicale, Moines) with extra restrictions. Corsica is French territory: French sea rules (5 kn in the 300 m strip).

season.closures: Gales: mistral/libeccio (W) on the west coast, venturi in the Bouches de Bonifacio where wind is often about double the offshore value.

months.notes: Bouches de Bonifacio: wind accelerates (10 kn offshore ≈ 20 kn in the strait). Many coves are open to the wind; plan a sheltered harbour.

tides.notes: Microtidal (≈0.2–0.3 m); wind and pressure surges matter more.

authority.name: Préfecture maritime de la Méditerranée / CROSS MED La Garde (VHF 16)

notes: Weather VHF ch 79 every hour from CROSS MED Corse stations (Ersa, Serragia, Pigno, Punta, Conca, Piana); Monaco Radio ch 24. Published legs: Ajaccio–Sagone 23 NM, Sagone–Girolata 20, Girolata–L'Île-Rousse 36, L'Île-Rousse–Calvi 10, Propriano–Ajaccio 27 (20 by another guide), Bonifacio–Rondinara via Lavezzi 15. Bonifacio–Santa Teresa (Sardinia) about 9 NM. Sea: permis plaisance option côtière for engines over 4.5 kW; Division 240 equipment (basic < 2 NM from shelter, coastal 2–6 NM). Inland-only boats may not be fit for sea: check CE design category and insurance.

name: North Brittany coast (Saint-Malo – Bréhat – Perros-Guirec – Morlaix – Roscoff – L'Aber Wrac'h)
reach: Baie de Saint-Malo, Côte d'Émeraude, Baie de Saint-Brieuc, Paimpol/Bréhat, Trieux and Jaudy, Côte de Granit Rose (Sept-Îles), Baie de Morlaix, Île de Batz to L'Aber Wrac'h

depth.notes: Open sea; check harbour depths and sills.

current.notes: Streams to 6 kn off Bréhat and the Héaux, 6 kn in the Tréguier river at low water, 5 kn among the Sept-Îles and at Roscoff (also inside the marina), 3 kn in the Trieux; Île de Batz channel sets hard west. Navigate near slack in rivers.

rules.notes: Many harbours are behind sills or lock gates with tide windows (Saint-Malo Vauban lock from mid-tide; Paimpol lock ±2 h HW; Perros-Guirec open only at coefficients over 45; Trébeurden gate). Morlaix: arrive on the rising tide, follow the lights strictly.

season.closures: Spring–early summer: persistent easterlies under a Scandinavian high. Wind against tide raises dangerous seas at headlands and passages.

months.notes: Plan every passage on the tidal stream; neaps can shut sill harbours for days (Perros).

tides.notes: Macrotidal: range up to 13.6 m at Saint-Malo on the biggest springs (among the largest in Europe), decreasing westward. Approaches dry up to 7 m (Paimpol).

authority.name: Préfecture maritime de l'Atlantique / CROSS Corsen, Étel (VHF 16)

notes: Weather VHF ch 79 (CROSS Corsen: Fréhel, Bodic/Trieux, Batz) at 07:33–08:03, 13:33–14:03, 19:33–20:03; CROSS Jobourg ch 80 (Granville) to the east; Jersey Radio ch 25/82 for the Channel Islands. All-tide harbours: Saint-Cast, Saint-Quay-Portrieux, Roscoff, L'Aber Wrac'h. Charts: SHOM, Imray C33B/C34/C35. Sea: permis plaisance option côtière for engines over 4.5 kW; Division 240 equipment (basic < 2 NM from shelter, coastal 2–6 NM). Inland-only boats may not be fit for sea: check CE design category and insurance.

name: Iroise (Chenal du Four – Ouessant – Rade de Brest – Raz de Sein)
reach: From L'Aber Wrac'h through the Chenal du Four (Le Four to Pointe Saint-Mathieu) or the Chenal de la Helle, the Rade de Brest and Camaret, to the Raz de Sein and Audierne

depth.notes: Open sea; check harbour depths and sills.

current.notes: Raz de Sein ~6–7 kn at springs; Chenal du Four strong streams (marked by Saint-Mathieu and Kermorvan lights).

rules.notes: Chenal du Four and Raz de Sein are regulated by Atlantic prefectoral order; pass at slack water. Parc naturel marin d'Iroise covers the area.

season.closures: Avoid the Raz and the Four with wind against tide or in strong W–SW winds.

months.notes: Time the Four and the Raz together: carry the fair stream through both.

tides.notes: Large tides; Raz de Sein at spring tides (coef. 100): ~7 kn flood (NE) and ~6 kn ebb (SW); very rough seas with wind against tide even in moderate breeze. Inshore alternatives: Petit Raz, Trouz Yar.

authority.name: Préfecture maritime de l'Atlantique / CROSS Corsen, Étel (VHF 16)

notes: Weather VHF ch 79: Raz (04:45, 07:03, 13:03, 19:03), Stiff/Ouessant (05:03, 07:15, 13:15, 19:15) — CROSS Corsen. Brest roadstead harbours: Brest Moulin Blanc, Camaret. Sea: permis plaisance option côtière for engines over 4.5 kW; Division 240 equipment (basic < 2 NM from shelter, coastal 2–6 NM). Inland-only boats may not be fit for sea: check CE design category and insurance.

name: Pertuis charentais (La Rochelle – Île de Ré – Île d'Aix – Oléron – Charente estuary)
reach: Pertuis Breton and Pertuis d'Antioche: La Rochelle (Les Minimes), Île de Ré (Saint-Martin, Ars), Île d'Aix, Rochefort and the Charente estuary, Oléron

depth.notes: Open sea; check harbour depths and sills.

current.notes: Strong streams in the pertuis and the Charente estuary on springs.

rules.notes: Pont de l'île de Ré: 30 m clearance under four navigable spans. Saint-Martin-de-Ré is a tidal harbour with a gated basin (opening around HW). Charente river to Rochefort: tidal.

season.closures: W–NW gales raise breaking seas at the pertuis entrances on the ebb.

months.notes: Plan harbour entries on the tide (Saint-Martin, Rochefort).

tides.notes: Spring range about 6.5 m at the Charente mouth and 5.4 m at Rochefort (1973 survey); many harbours dry or are gated.

authority.name: Préfecture maritime de l'Atlantique / CROSS Corsen, Étel (VHF 16)

notes: Weather VHF: CROSS Étel ch 79 Royan (07:15, 13:15, 19:15), Chassiron ch 63 (cycle), ch 80 Les Sables (08:15, 14:15, 20:15). Sea: permis plaisance option côtière for engines over 4.5 kW; Division 240 equipment (basic < 2 NM from shelter, coastal 2–6 NM). Inland-only boats may not be fit for sea: check CE design category and insurance.

name: Balearic Islands (Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, Formentera, Cabrera)
reach: Mallorca (Palma, Andratx, Sóller, Pollença, Alcúdia, Cala Rajada, Cala d'Or), Cabrera, Menorca (Ciutadella, Maó), Ibiza (Eivissa, Sant Antoni, Santa Eulària, Portinatx) and Formentera (La Savina, Espalmador)

locks.notes: Typical legs (charter itineraries, NM): Palma–Andratx 17, Andratx–Sóller 25, Sóller–Pollença 35, Pollença–Cala Rajada 25, Cabrera–Palma 35; Ibiza: Sant Antoni–La Savina 23, Eivissa–Santa Eulària 8, Portinatx–Sant Antoni 16.

rules.permit: Cabrera National Park: navigation permit (online, valid 12 months) and a buoy reservation to stay; buoys €9.30/18.60 per day up to 12 m (winter/summer), €20/40 for 12–15 m, €35/90 for 15–20 m, €105/275 for 20–35 m
rules.notes: Posidonia: Balearic Decree 25/2018 and RD 191/2026 ban anchoring on Posidonia (and Cymodocea) meadows and on sand where chain or swing reaches them; inside buoy fields use the buoys; pumping bilges or dumping waste in a buoy field is an aggravating offence. Bathing zones (buoyed, or 200 m off beaches/50 m off other coast where unbuoyed) closed to boats; cross only perpendicular at max 3 kn; 3 kn in launch channels and port entrances; keep 50 m from swimmers and divers' flags.

season.closures: Cabrera: navigating, anchoring or diving inside the national park only with the park's authorisation; overnight only on a reserved buoy in the port. Posidonia meadows are no-anchoring all year.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures. Cabrera buoys: max 2 nights in July–August, 7 nights the rest of the year; summer buoy rates (1 May–30 Sep) double the winter rates.

authority.name: Capitanía Marítima de Palma / Govern de les Illes Balears (Posidonia, Cabrera National Park)

notes: Spain (RD 875/2014 as amended by RD 1188/2025): from 1 Oct 2026 no licence for motorboats up to 5 m and 15 CV (11.03 kW), sail up to 6 m, daylight, within 2 NM of port/beach; above that PNB (8 m, 5 NM), PER (15 m, 12 NM, inter-island Balearics), Patrón/Capitán de yate. Visitors: home licence/ICC. Cabrera: max 50 boats/day on the buoys, occupancy 18:00 first day to 17:00 last day; anchoring tel. 971 656 282, navigation/diving 971 17 76 41. Meadow maps: Govern balear anchoring viewer and LIFE Posidonia viewer. Passages (ferry figures): Barcelona–Palma ~112–130 NM, Barcelona–Maó 133, Alcúdia–Ciutadella 39, Palma–Ibiza 81, Ibiza–Formentera 10 NM.

name: Costa Brava and Barcelona (Barcelona – Blanes – Palamós – L'Estartit – Cadaqués)
reach: Barcelona (Port Vell, Port Olímpic) north along the Maresme and Costa Brava: Blanes, Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Palamós, Llafranc, L'Estartit and the Medes Islands, Empuriabrava, Cadaqués

rules.notes: RD 191/2026 (in force 2 Apr 2026): anchoring on Posidonia oceanica and Cymodocea nodosa banned in all Spanish Mediterranean waters, also on nearby sand if chain or swing reaches the meadow; only authorised buoys/buoy fields. Bathing zones (buoyed, or 200 m off beaches/50 m off other coast where unbuoyed) closed to boats; cross only perpendicular at max 3 kn; 3 kn in launch channels and port entrances; keep 50 m from swimmers and divers' flags.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures.

authority.name: Capitanía Marítima de Barcelona / Palamós (DGMM)

notes: Spain (RD 875/2014 as amended by RD 1188/2025): from 1 Oct 2026 no licence for motorboats up to 5 m and 15 CV (11.03 kW), sail up to 6 m, daylight, within 2 NM of port/beach; above that PNB (8 m, 5 NM), PER (15 m, 12 NM, inter-island Balearics), Patrón/Capitán de yate. Visitors: home licence/ICC. Legs (charter itineraries, NM): Blanes–Palamós 19.5, Palamós–L'Estartit 15.3, L'Estartit–Cadaqués 15.2, Empuriabrava–Cadaqués 9.4, Palamós–Sant Feliu 6.8. Crossings: Barcelona–Maó 133 NM, Barcelona–Ibiza 149 NM.

name: Valencia coast and the Dénia – Ibiza crossing
reach: Valencia, Dénia and the Costa Blanca north, with the crossings to Ibiza and Formentera (shortest mainland–Balearics passage from Dénia)

rules.notes: RD 191/2026 (in force 2 Apr 2026): anchoring on Posidonia oceanica and Cymodocea nodosa banned in all Spanish Mediterranean waters, also on nearby sand if chain or swing reaches the meadow; only authorised buoys/buoy fields. Bathing zones (buoyed, or 200 m off beaches/50 m off other coast where unbuoyed) closed to boats; cross only perpendicular at max 3 kn; 3 kn in launch channels and port entrances; keep 50 m from swimmers and divers' flags.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures.

authority.name: Capitanía Marítima de Valencia / Alicante (DGMM)

notes: Spain (RD 875/2014 as amended by RD 1188/2025): from 1 Oct 2026 no licence for motorboats up to 5 m and 15 CV (11.03 kW), sail up to 6 m, daylight, within 2 NM of port/beach; above that PNB (8 m, 5 NM), PER (15 m, 12 NM, inter-island Balearics), Patrón/Capitán de yate. Visitors: home licence/ICC. Crossings (ferry operators' figures): Dénia–Ibiza 57–67 NM, Dénia–Formentera ~61 NM, Valencia–Ibiza ~88 NM. The open-sea leg to Ibiza needs at least a PER-level licence for a Spanish skipper (more than 12 NM from shelter for a PNB).

name: Costa del Sol, Strait of Gibraltar and Bay of Cádiz approaches
reach: Málaga – Marbella – Estepona – Sotogrande – Gibraltar/La Línea – Algeciras – Tarifa – Barbate, with crossings to Ceuta, Tangier and Marina Smir

rules.notes: Orca interaction (MITECO/DGMM): avoid the mapped high-risk zones, plan routes close to the coast, do not stop the boat, head for the coast or shallower water, keep away from the sides; harmful deterrents are banned; report on VHF 16 to Salvamento Marítimo and send photos to orcas@sasemar.es. RD 191/2026 (in force 2 Apr 2026): anchoring on Posidonia oceanica and Cymodocea nodosa banned in all Spanish Mediterranean waters, also on nearby sand if chain or swing reaches the meadow; only authorised buoys/buoy fields. Bathing zones (buoyed, or 200 m off beaches/50 m off other coast where unbuoyed) closed to boats; cross only perpendicular at max 3 kn; 3 kn in launch channels and port entrances; keep 50 m from swimmers and divers' flags.

season.closures: Orca high-risk zones: avoid where possible, especially April–October.

months.notes: Orcas: extra caution April–October (MITECO); Strait encounters fell sharply by 2025 but the risk map for the Gulf of Cádiz–Strait stays in force. Easterly (Levante) is the favoured wind for Alcaidesa–Ceuta and westward runs to Barbate.

tides.notes: Tidal streams in the Strait run on top of a near-permanent east-going surface current (Atlantic inflow): it strengthens the east-going set and weakens the west-going one; plan on the net. Tidal effects largely die out east of Gibraltar.

authority.name: Capitanía Marítima de Algeciras / Málaga; Salvamento Marítimo (Tarifa)

notes: Spain (RD 875/2014 as amended by RD 1188/2025): from 1 Oct 2026 no licence for motorboats up to 5 m and 15 CV (11.03 kW), sail up to 6 m, daylight, within 2 NM of port/beach; above that PNB (8 m, 5 NM), PER (15 m, 12 NM, inter-island Balearics), Patrón/Capitán de yate. Visitors: home licence/ICC. Dangers: keep inside the Los Cabezos shoal (breaks even in calm weather), give the ridge ~2 NM SW of Cape Trafalgar a wide berth, keep 0.5 NM off Isla de Tarifa; fishing nets between Punta Almina and Smir. Marina Smir is a Moroccan port of entry; Gibraltar marinas assist with customs. Legs (NM): Alcaidesa–Estepona 25, Alcaidesa–Barbate 36, Alcaidesa–Ceuta 18, Alcaidesa–Smir 28, Algeciras–Ceuta ~15 (ferry), Tarifa–Tangier 17.

name: Galicia: Rías Baixas, Rías Altas and the Atlantic Islands National Park
reach: Baiona and the Ría de Vigo (Cíes), Ría de Pontevedra (Ons, Combarro, Sanxenxo), Ría de Arousa (Sálvora, Cortegada, A Pobra, Rianxo), Ría de Muros e Noia, north to A Coruña

rules.permit: Illas Atlánticas National Park (Cíes, Ons, Sálvora, Cortegada): written navigation authorisation (owner's form, valid 3 years) and a separate anchoring authorisation, requested online from the park (fondeos.iatlanticas@xunta.gal); same-day requests possible
rules.notes: Anchoring in the park only with authorisation; daily caps (about 235 private boats in high season across the four islands, 15–20 a day at Sálvora and Cortegada, Sálvora on one beach only). Orca protocol as in the Strait: do not stop, head for shallower water, report on VHF 16. Bathing zones (buoyed, or 200 m off beaches/50 m off other coast where unbuoyed) closed to boats; cross only perpendicular at max 3 kn; 3 kn in launch channels and port entrances; keep 50 m from swimmers and divers' flags.

season.best: Atlantic Islands: high season Easter and 15 May – 15 September
season.closures: Atlantic Islands National Park waters: no anchoring without the park's authorisation.

months.notes: Orcas: extra caution April–October; interactions rose slightly on the Galician and Cantabrian coasts in summer 2025 and MITECO drew a new high-risk map for Galicia.

tides.notes: Atlantic tides: plan entries to rías, bars and drying berths on the tide tables (Puertos del Estado); spring range not confirmed from an official source here.

authority.name: Parque Nacional Marítimo-Terrestre das Illas Atlánticas de Galicia (Xunta de Galicia); Capitanías Marítimas de Vigo, Vilagarcía, A Coruña

notes: Spain (RD 875/2014 as amended by RD 1188/2025): from 1 Oct 2026 no licence for motorboats up to 5 m and 15 CV (11.03 kW), sail up to 6 m, daylight, within 2 NM of port/beach; above that PNB (8 m, 5 NM), PER (15 m, 12 NM, inter-island Balearics), Patrón/Capitán de yate. Visitors: home licence/ICC. Legs (Rías Baixas rally, miles): Baiona–Combarro 30, Combarro–Rianxo 32, Rianxo–A Pobra 15, A Pobra–Muros 32.

name: Cantabrian / Bay of Biscay coast (Ribadeo – Gijón – Santander – Bilbao – San Sebastián – Hondarribia)
reach: Spanish north coast from the Ría de Ribadeo to the French border at the Bidasoa (Hondarribia)

rules.notes: Orca protocol (MITECO/DGMM): do not stop, head for the coast or shallower water, report on VHF 16. Bathing zones (buoyed, or 200 m off beaches/50 m off other coast where unbuoyed) closed to boats; cross only perpendicular at max 3 kn; 3 kn in launch channels and port entrances; keep 50 m from swimmers and divers' flags.

months.notes: Orcas: interactions rose slightly on the Galician and Cantabrian coasts in summer 2025; extra caution April–October.

tides.notes: Atlantic tides; harbour entrances and bars are tide-dependent. Spring range not confirmed from an official source here: use Puertos del Estado tide tables.

authority.name: Capitanías Marítimas de Gijón, Santander, Bilbao, Pasaia (DGMM)

notes: Spain (RD 875/2014 as amended by RD 1188/2025): from 1 Oct 2026 no licence for motorboats up to 5 m and 15 CV (11.03 kW), sail up to 6 m, daylight, within 2 NM of port/beach; above that PNB (8 m, 5 NM), PER (15 m, 12 NM, inter-island Balearics), Patrón/Capitán de yate. Visitors: home licence/ICC. No leg distances from a guide could be confirmed for this coast in this pass.

name: Portugal west coast (Viana do Castelo – Porto/Leixões – Nazaré – Cascais – Lisbon – Sesimbra – Setúbal – Sines)
reach: Portuguese Atlantic coast from the Minho to Sines, with the Tejo and Sado estuaries' approaches

rules.permit: Every boat needs a skipper with a carta de navegador de recreio (DL 93/2018); EU licences recognised. Foreign boats pay the taxa de farolagem e balizagem once at the first Portuguese port
rules.notes: Local Capitania editais set speeds: Cascais (Edital 5/2021) under 3 kn in anchorages and the access channel, 5 kn on final approach, 3 kn inside the marina. Motor craft off-limits at bathing beaches. Jet skis may not run between sunset and sunrise.

months.notes: Orcas also interact with yachts off Portugal; authorities in Portugal, Spain and Morocco issue advice to recreational sailors.

tides.notes: Atlantic tides; the Douro bar and estuary depths depend on the tide (Crestuma lock approach: 4.35 m only with tides of 1.25 m, 3.6 m at low water springs with the power station stopped).

authority.name: Autoridade Marítima Nacional (Capitanias) / DGRM

notes: Legs (charter itinerary, NM): Doca de Belém–Oeiras 5.7, Oeiras–Cascais 5.7, Cascais–Setúbal 37, Setúbal–Sines 36.9, Sines–Tróia 35.2, Tróia–Sesimbra 11, Sesimbra–Doca de Belém 25.3. Lisbon's 25 de Abril bridge: 70 m clearance at mean high water.

name: Algarve (Sagres – Lagos – Portimão – Albufeira – Vilamoura – Culatra – Vila Real de Santo António)
reach: Portuguese south coast from Cabo de São Vicente / Sagres to the Guadiana mouth (Vila Real de Santo António / Ayamonte)

rules.permit: Carta de navegador de recreio (DL 93/2018); taxa de farolagem e balizagem at the first Portuguese port
rules.notes: Anchor only where charts and Capitania editais allow; protected-area portarias can restrict navigation and anchoring (DL 93/2018 art. 44). Albufeira marina: a footbridge must be retracted to enter, call VHF 9. Vilamoura Radio VHF 9.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures.

tides.notes: Atlantic tides: the Ria Formosa channels (Faro, Olhão, Culatra, Tavira) and the Guadiana bar are tide-dependent; deep-draught boats anchor outside the barrier islands. VRSA marina 2–3 m at MLW.

authority.name: Autoridade Marítima Nacional (Capitanias de Lagos, Portimão, Faro, Olhão, Tavira, Vila Real de Santo António)

notes: Legs (NM, Noonsite/itineraries): VRSA–Culatra 26, Culatra–Vilamoura 20, Vilamoura–Albufeira 6, Albufeira–Portimão 14, Portimão–Alvor 4, Lagos–Sagres 15, Lagos–Albufeira 21.5, Quarteira–Portimão 21.8, Portimão–Sagres 21.3. Culatra is a popular safe anchorage. Last anchorage before Cabo de São Vicente: Sagres/Baleeira.

name: Guadalquivir (Sanlúcar de Barrameda / Bonanza – Seville)
reach: Ría del Guadalquivir from the mouth (Sanlúcar/Bonanza, buoy no. 1 'Juan Sebastián Elcano') up the Eurovía E 60.02 channel to the 'Puerta del Mar' lock and the Seville dock; the Brazo de San Juan to Puerto Gelves; maritime waters up to the Alcalá del Río dam

depth.notes: Seagoing channel; outside it, depths fall with the tide, silting and submerged pipes (Capitanía de Sevilla 2026).

current.notes: Tidal river: strong flood and ebb streams; a yacht can carry the flood upriver for at least 9 hours (Imray).

locks.notes: 'Puerta del Mar' lock and the lifting Puente de las Delicias give access to the Seville dock; yachts have low priority and openings are limited: request through a Seville marina 24 h ahead and meet the set time. Port Control (port, lock, bridge) VHF 12.

rules.notes: Max 10 kn in the channel between buoys 13/14 and Bonanza and between Puebla del Río (58) and Coria (69-B); 6 kn on the channel margins inside buoys 13/14; 4 kn in ports. Merchant ships have right of way; cross the channel at right angles, no anchoring in it. At night: channel only (10 kn), no side arms; no navigation north of Puerto Gelves. Jet skis banned at night. Watch VHF 16, and VHF 12 within 2 NM of buoy 1. No anchoring at 'El Pozo' without permission.

tides.notes: Tidal up to the Alcalá del Río dam; the Seville dock is behind the lock and free of tide. About 55 NM mouth–Seville: start an hour before the flood and most yachts reach Seville on one tide (Imray). Spring range not confirmed here.

authority.name: Capitanía Marítima de Sevilla; Autoridad Portuaria de Sevilla

notes: Air draught: Seville dock max 42 m; power lines across the river are charted (chart 4425, derrotero 5); Brazo de San Juan 16.5 m under the lines 1,750 m N of Punta de D. Isaías. Stop at Chipiona first for fuel and advice. Licence as at sea (Spain).

name: Douro (Porto – Pocinho – Barca d'Alva, Via Navegável do Douro)
reach: Douro bar at Porto/Foz to Barca d'Alva at the Spanish border (Via Navegável do Douro, VND), through Crestuma-Lever, Carrapatelo, Régua (Bagaúste), Valeira and Pocinho

depth.notes: Lock limit 3.8 m draught; Régua and Valeira sills 0.5 m higher than the downstream channel (3.7 m in the worst case). Crestuma from downstream: 4.35 m only with a 1.25 m tide, as little as 3.6 m at low water springs with the power station stopped.

current.notes: Flow is set by the dams; unannounced releases from upstream Spanish dams occasionally disturb navigation.

locks.chamber: Lengths Crestuma-Lever 88 m, Carrapatelo 84 m, Régua 86 m, Valeira 87 m, Pocinho 86.5 m; beam 11.4 m
locks.hours: Set by APDL notice (avisos on douro.apdl.pt)
locks.notes: Book each lockage via the APDL Balcão Virtual (douro.apdl.pt) by 17:00 the day before; slots appear in the RIS Douro lock plan; late boats wait — lockage goes 10 min after the booked time. Carrapatelo lift about 35 m. Max 0.2 m/s (~0.4 kn) in locks and approaches. Lock fees per APDL tariff.

rules.permit: Leisure boats exempt from the CUV use certificate but must follow APDL scheduling (Planos de Escala); lock bookings through the APDL Balcão Virtual / JUP
rules.notes: Max 10 kn in the channel; leisure boats max 5 kn within 50 m of banks, bathing areas or anchored boats and within 100 m of ports and quays. No navigation in reduced visibility. Night navigation by leisure boats only exceptionally, by JUP request (radar, ECDIS, AIS required). Commercial vessels have priority. VHF 12/16 with VTS Leixões / VND control.

season.closures: Floods: in Feb 2026 the Capitania and APDL restricted and considered banning navigation during red flood alerts; night navigation within 5 km of dams has been banned in flood periods.

months.notes: High-water restrictions during winter flood alerts (e.g. Feb 2026); APDL publishes closures as avisos.

tides.notes: Tidal below Crestuma-Lever (the first lock); depth at the Crestuma approach depends on the tide.

authority.name: APDL – Administração dos Portos do Douro, Leixões e Viana do Castelo (Via Navegável do Douro)

notes: Air draught 7.2 m under the Mosteirô and Ferradosa bridges (can drop to 6.6 m outside the dry season). Carta de navegador de recreio needed (no power exemption). The river is busy with cruise ships (about 17,000 lockages in 2025).

name: Tejo / Tagus estuary (Cascais – Lisbon – Mar da Palha)
reach: Tejo estuary from the bar off Cascais/São Julião past Belém and Lisbon into the Mar da Palha

depth.notes: The inner estuary is a wide lagoon with shallow sandbanks that dry at low tide; keep to buoyed channels.

current.notes: Strong tidal streams at the narrow (about 2 km) estuary mouth.

rules.permit: Carta de navegador de recreio (DL 93/2018)
rules.notes: Lisbon port and Capitania rules not verified for this sheet.

months.notes: Upstream river floods usually January–April, lowest flow July–October (Tagus basin).

tides.notes: Tidal estuary; banks dry at low water. Spring range not confirmed here.

authority.name: APL – Administração do Porto de Lisboa; Capitania do Porto de Lisboa

notes: 25 de Abril bridge: 70 m clearance at mean high water. Doca de Belém – Oeiras 5.7 NM, Oeiras – Cascais 5.7 NM.

name: Guadiana (Vila Real de Santo António / Ayamonte – Alcoutim – Pomarão)
reach: Border river from the mouth at Vila Real de Santo António / Ayamonte upstream to Alcoutim / Sanlúcar de Guadiana (about 20 NM) and Pomarão; Pomarão–Mértola Portuguese only

depth.notes: VRSA–Alcoutim channel dredged to -2.00 m ZH, min. 30 m wide, design boat 70 × 10 m, 1.8 m draught (POCTEP phase 1); Alcoutim–Pomarão works under POCTEP 2014-2020 (status not confirmed); Pomarão–Mértola design 1.0 m, not financed. Deep mid-channel and on the outside of bends.

current.notes: Tidal; yachts ride the flood upriver after low water.

locks.notes: Guadiana International Bridge just above VRSA/Ayamonte (clearance not confirmed; yachts with tall masts pass), the next bridge about 40 km upriver.

rules.notes: Border waters: Portuguese (Capitania VRSA) and Spanish (Capitanía de Huelva) rules on each side; not verified in detail.

months.notes: Alcoutim is a popular wintering anchorage.

tides.notes: Tidal to Alcoutim and beyond; time the passage under the bridge and upriver on the flood.

authority.name: DGRM / Capitania do Porto de Vila Real de Santo António; Capitanía Marítima de Huelva

notes: Lit beacons along the channel (visible 2 NM). Anchorages south of Alcoutim/Sanlúcar de Guadiana and below the bridge. VRSA marina 2–3 m at MLW.

name: Malta, Gozo and Comino
reach: Grand Harbour and Marsamxett (Valletta, Msida, Ta' Xbiex, Birgu/Kalkara) – Marsaxlokk – St Paul's Bay – Mellieħa – Comino (Blue Lagoon) – Mġarr (Gozo)

depth.notes: Open sea; marinas and the main bays deep enough for 1–2 m draught.

locks.notes: Distances (NM, itineraries): Kalkara–Mġarr 15.2, Comino–Golden Bay 6.7, Golden Bay–Mellieħa 8.5, Mellieħa–St Paul's Bay 4.3, St Paul's Bay–Kalkara 8.8; Valletta–Pozzallo (Sicily) ~50; Port El Kantaoui (TN)–Valletta 194.

rules.permit: Nautical Licence from Transport Malta for 30 HP (about 22 kW) or more; third-party insurance compulsory
rules.notes: Max 10 kn (18 km/h) in harbours, within 300 m of sandy beaches and 200 m of other shore; 5 kn zones in busy bays (Blue Lagoon, Mġarr ix-Xini, Mellieħa, St Paul's Islands, Xemxija); 3 kn near marinas and mooring areas. Buoyed swimmer zones (Blue Lagoon: LNTM 059/2026) are closed to boats; no anchoring or mooring in launch lanes, fairways or the safety strip next to swimmer zones (LNTM 061/2025, 130/2026: keep 20 m, 5 m at Blue Lagoon).

season.closures: Seasonal swimmer zones and launch lanes June–October; Gregale (strong N–NE wind) makes north-east facing harbours and bays, including the Grand Harbour approach, uncomfortable or dangerous.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures. Gregale = strong N–NE wind (season not confirmed). Blue Lagoon swimmer zone and 5 kn buoys in the summer season.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea; wind and pressure change the level more than the tide.

authority.name: Transport Malta (Ports and Yachting Directorate); Valletta VTS

notes: Schengen/EU. Arriving from outside Schengen: go straight to a port of entry (Grand Harbour/Msida–Ta' Xbiex; customs at Msida marina weekdays 09:00–17:00, otherwise Grand Harbour); mooring elsewhere first risks a fine. Call Valletta VTS/Port Control on VHF 12 before entering, marina on VHF 13; notify Mġarr (Gozo) on VHF before entering or anchoring off. No cruising tax.

name: Turkish Aegean: Bodrum, Gökova, Datça and Marmaris
reach: Çeşme and the Bodrum peninsula (Yalıkavak, Turgutreis, Bodrum) – Gulf of Gökova (Çökertme, Mersincik, English Harbour) – Knidos – Datça – Hisarönü and Symi bays (Bozburun, Selimiye) – Marmaris, with the crossings to Chios, Kos, Symi and Rhodes

depth.notes: Open sea; deep water close inshore, most anchorages are steep-to (stern lines ashore common).

locks.notes: Distances (NM, itineraries/ferries): Bodrum–Knidos 20, Bodrum–Çökertme 20, Yalıkavak–Knidos 34, Knidos–Datça 15, Datça–Bozburun 20.5–25, Bozburun–Selimiye 12, Marmaris–Çiftlik 12; crossings Bodrum–Kos ~10, Datça–Symi 9.9, Marmaris–Rhodes 22–25, Çeşme–Chios ~9.

rules.permit: Transit Log (Yat Kayıt Belgesi), done at the port of entry (usually through an agent); electronic transit log being introduced (expected fully in 2026); yacht noted in the owner's/skipper's passport
rules.notes: Discharging grey or black water is banned and fined; waste is tracked through the digital Maritime Waste Application (formerly Blue Card). Special Environmental Protection Areas (Gökova, Datça–Bozburun) have anchoring, fishing and waste rules. Clear out of Turkey before crossing to a Greek island and clear in there (non-Schengen → Schengen).

season.closures: Meltemi (N–NW) in July–August, often Force 5–7 in the afternoon, gusting more round capes and in the Kos–Bodrum and Knidos/Datça channels; the Bodrum area itself is somewhat gentler.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures. Meltemi June–September, peak mid-July to mid-August, usually light in the morning and strongest in the afternoon; plan long legs early. Winter brings southerly gales and rain.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea; wind and pressure change the level more than the tide.

authority.name: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism (yacht entry) / Harbour masters (Liman Başkanlığı), Ministry of Transport

notes: Not EU/Schengen: enter and leave only at designated frontier ports (e.g. Çeşme, Bodrum, Datça, Marmaris) under the Q flag; arrival from or departure to Greece means full clearance each way. Ports of entry per the Ministry list; Turgutreis is not on the extract seen. Fuel and marinas widely available (Yalıkavak, Bodrum, Netsel Marmaris).

name: Turquoise coast: Göcek, Fethiye, Kaş and Kekova
reach: Ekincik and Dalyan – Gulf of Fethiye/Göcek (Twelve Islands, Sarsala, Wall Bay, Kapı Creek) – Fethiye – Gemiler – Ölüdeniz – Kalkan – Kaş – Kastellorizo (GR) – Kekova Roads (Üçağız, Kaleköy/Simena) – Gökkaya – Kemer/Antalya

depth.notes: Open sea; bays deep and steep-to, stern lines ashore usual; Göcek bays partly on paid buoys.

locks.notes: Distances (NM, charter itineraries): Göcek–Twelve Islands 8, Göcek–Wall Bay 8, Wall Bay–Kapı Creek 2.5, Kapı Creek–Fethiye 12, Fethiye–Gemiler 15, Kalkan–Kaş 15, Kaş–Kekova 18–22, Ekincik–Twelve Islands 25; Kaş–Kastellorizo about 4 (ferry).

rules.permit: Transit Log at a port of entry (Fethiye, Kaş, Kemer, Antalya, Marmaris); paid mooring buoys in Göcek's no-anchoring zones (booked by app/web, operated by TÜÇA/ÇEYAŞ)
rules.notes: From the 2026 season anchoring is banned in designated Göcek bays (incl. Atbükü, Boynuzbükü, Kille, Bedri Rahmi, Büyük and Küçük Sarsala, Martı, Yassıca Islands); use the ~200 paid GPS/AIS buoys (fees reported from ~€20 a night; official tariff not seen). Kekova Special Environmental Protection Area: no swimming, diving or anchoring over the Sunken City, boats may pass slowly; fishing restricted. No grey/black-water discharge (digital waste log).

season.closures: Kaş–Kalkan is the longest, most exposed leg of a Göcek/Fethiye week; plan it for the morning. Wind climate not confirmed from an official source.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures. July–August: crowded Göcek bays, buoys in demand (estimates 1,000–1,500 yachts vs ~880 buoy places). Spring and autumn quieter and cooler.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea; wind and pressure change the level more than the tide.

authority.name: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (entry); Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change / Turkish Environment Agency TÜÇA (protected areas, Göcek buoys)

notes: Göcek and Fethiye are the charter hubs (Göcek itself is not on the Ministry's port-of-entry list seen; Fethiye and Kaş are). Kastellorizo (Meis, GR) is a Schengen entry: clear out of Kaş first. Buoy fees are paid online and not included in charter prices.

name: Cyprus (Republic): Larnaca, Limassol, Paphos and Latsi
reach: Ayia Napa – Larnaca – Zygi – Limassol (Limassol Marina, St Raphael, old port) – Cape Gata – Paphos – Cape Akamas – Latsi (Polis), the coast controlled by the Republic of Cyprus

depth.notes: Open sea. Larnaca Marina usable depth ~1.5–3 m; Limassol Marina 3.5–9 m; Ayia Napa basin 7 m; St Raphael up to 4 m.

locks.notes: Distances (NM, Deputy Ministry of Tourism): Limassol–Larnaca 38 (Limassol Marina says 35), Limassol–Paphos 42, Paphos–Latsi 33, Limassol–Latsi 75, Paphos–Larnaca 75, Larnaca–Latsi 108. Offshore: Larnaca–Lebanon 110, Limassol–Rhodes 255.

rules.permit: Operator licence for motorboats (Shipping Deputy Ministry); visitors carry ICC/home licence (acceptance not confirmed)
rules.notes: Yellow-buoyed swimming zones (about 100 m off beaches) closed to motorboats under power; 3–5 kn in marinas (secondary source). Do not anchor before clearing in (a €100 fine reported). New Recreational Navigation Law 4(I)/2026 passed, not yet in force in August 2026.

season.closures: Marinas are crowded and booked well ahead (Larnaca usually full of local yachts). Wind climate not confirmed from an official source.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures; sailing year-round, Limassol a winter base.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea; wind and pressure change the level more than the tide.

authority.name: Shipping Deputy Ministry / Cyprus Ports Authority; Customs and Excise Department

notes: EU but not Schengen: every yacht clears customs and immigration on arrival, even from the EU. Ports of entry: Larnaca Marina (VHF 16, works 8, 24 h), Limassol Marina (VHF 12, 24 h), Paphos, Latsi. Entering through the north (Kyrenia, Famagusta) is illegal under Republic law and penalised later. Russian-flag yachts barred (2022 notice).

name: Slovenian coast and Gulf of Trieste (bora)
reach: Piran – Portorož – Izola – Koper – Ankaran – Muggia – Trieste – Miramare – Sistiana/Portopiccolo

depth.notes: Open sea, shallow gulf (mostly 15–25 m); harbours fine for 2 m draught.

locks.notes: Distances: Piran–Trieste 14.1 NM (ferry); straight-line Portorož–Piran 1.2, Portorož–Izola 3.2, Izola–Trieste 8.3, Koper–Izola 2.9 NM.

rules.permit: Slovenian boat licence (voditelj čolna) for boats over 7.35 kW or over 7 m; foreign equivalents/ICC
rules.notes: Koper port anchorage area: max 6 kn (11 km/h). No mooring or anchoring in port areas without the port authority's approval; Slovenian anchor berths have set swinging circles (from 5 Aug 2025). Strunjan Nature Park between Izola and Piran (shellfish farm buoys). Koper VTS VHF 69 (backup 72); harbour master VHF 08/16.

season.closures: Bora (NE) mainly in winter, stronger in Trieste than in Koper Bay (up to 6–7 stormy days a month in winter); summer squalls from Tramontana (N–NNW) or Lebič (SW) at 40–60 kn for 1–3 h with thunderstorms; winter fog.

months.notes: Sea area. Long Jugo (SE) in December–January can raise the sea level up to 1.2 m and flood Koper's quays; long bora lowers it up to 0.6 m.

tides.notes: Largest tides in the Mediterranean: about 1.1 m at springs at Koper (MLWS/MHWS), mixed semidiurnal; storm surge adds to it.

authority.name: Uprava RS za pomorstvo (Slovenian Maritime Administration), Koper; Capitaneria di porto di Trieste

notes: Schengen: no clearance between Slovenia, Italy and Croatia; from a non-Schengen port clear in at Koper, Izola (seasonal) or Piran. Marinas: Portorož, Izola, Koper; Piran town quay on lines, fills by early afternoon. Trieste Marina San Giusto VHF 77. Weather warnings via Koper VTS on VHF 69 and AIS; ARSO forecasts.

name: Montenegro: Bay of Kotor, Budva and Bar
reach: Herceg Novi/Zelenika – Portonovi – Tivat (Porto Montenegro) – Verige strait – Perast – Kotor – Luštica (Bigova) – Budva – Sveti Stefan – Petrovac – Bar

depth.notes: Open sea and a deep fjord-like bay; marinas take large yachts.

locks.notes: Distances (NM, itineraries): Kotor–Perast 5.3, Perast–Bigova 17.8, Bigova–Petrovac 15.9, Petrovac–Bar 9.5, Bar–Budva 15.8, Budva–Tivat 24.3, Tivat–Kotor 8–8.5, Kotor–Herceg Novi 15; Dubrovnik (Gruž)–Kotor about 42.

rules.permit: Vignette (cruising permit) for foreign yachts, bought on clearance at the harbour master; valid 1 week, 1 month, 3, 6 or 12 months, priced by length (no official 2026 tariff found); tourist tax per person
rules.notes: Kotor: no anchoring or mooring within 450 m of the Luža breakwater light (port order; check current). Illegal chartering by foreign yachts is actively prosecuted.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures. Kotor very busy with cruise ships in summer.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea; wind and pressure change the level more than the tide.

authority.name: Uprava pomorske sigurnosti i upravljanja lukama (Maritime Safety and Port Management Administration); harbour masters Bar and Kotor

notes: Not EU/Schengen: clear in at a port of entry (Bar, Kotor, Zelenika, Porto Montenegro/Tivat, Portonovi; lists differ), calling the harbour master on VHF 16 before landing. From Croatia clear out at Cavtat or Dubrovnik. Tax-free diesel for foreign-flag yachts at Porto Montenegro, Portonovi and Marina Bar (vignette needed; 72 h minimum stay dropped 29 Aug 2025).

name: Albania: Riviera, Vlorë and Durrës
reach: Corfu channel – Sarandë – Porto Palermo – Himarë – Palasë/Dhërmi – Karaburun peninsula and Sazan island – Vlorë/Orikum – Durrës – Shëngjin – Velipojë

depth.notes: Open sea; north of Vlorë the coast is shallow far out (Durrës bay 2–2.5 m well offshore), the Riviera is deep.

locks.notes: Distances (NM): Corfu–Sarandë ~15 (ferry), Sarandë–Himarë 20, Himarë–Vlorë 40 (round Karaburun), Vlorë–Durrës 58, Durrës–Montenegro border 37; whole coast ~155.

rules.permit: Cruising permit issued by customs at the port of entry (about €20–50 by size, secondary source); agent in practice essential
rules.notes: Karaburun–Sazan National Marine Park: entry by private boat needs a permit, fishing banned, mooring buoys instead of anchoring at some sites, Posidonia meadows. Police may ask boats to anchor farther off beaches (Himarë). Anchoring in Sarandë bay with the harbour master's permission.
