season.closures: Summer afternoon northerly (maestral), calm nights; bora (NE) can arrive suddenly in autumn and winter; Sarandë exposed to S and W winds and swell; the north coast less sheltered.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures.

tides.notes: Microtidal sea; wind and pressure change the level more than the tide.

authority.name: Albanian harbour masters (Kapitenerija) and customs at ports of entry; National Agency of Protected Areas (AKZM)

notes: Not EU/Schengen: clear in only at a port of entry (Sarandë, Vlorë, Durrës, Shëngjin; Himarë in summer) under the Q flag; going straight to a beach or anchorage first is illegal. Agent (~€50) handles papers: passports, registration, insurance, crew list. Fuel mostly by tanker except Sarandë and Vlorë.

name: Tunisia north and east coast: Tabarka to Monastir
reach: Tabarka – Cap Serrat – Bizerte – Ghar el-Melh – Sidi Bou Saïd/La Goulette (Gulf of Tunis) – Cap Bon (Kélibia) – Yasmine Hammamet – Port El Kantaoui – Monastir

depth.notes: Open sea. Bizerte marina 3.5–12 m; Port El Kantaoui 1.6–3 m; Cap Monastir 3.5–5.5 m. Sandbar and silting near Sidi Bou Saïd entrance.

locks.notes: Distances (NM, ONTT): Tabarka–Bizerte 64, Bizerte–Sidi Bou Saïd 33, Sidi Bou Saïd–Monastir 116, Sidi Bou Saïd–Pantelleria 76, Sidi Bou Saïd–Trapani 123, Bizerte–Trapani 135, Port El Kantaoui–Valletta 194, La Galite 36 from Tabarka.

rules.permit: Cruising permit issued by customs on first arrival, handed back on departure
rules.notes: Present at a customs port first: Tabarka, Bizerte, Sidi Bou Saïd, La Goulette, Kélibia, Yasmine Hammamet, Port El Kantaoui, Marina Monastir, Mahdia, Houmt Souk. Watch for poorly marked fish farms. Zembra island is a nature reserve.

season.closures: Cap Bon: strong winds, confused seas and currents; round it only in settled weather (good lee anchorage near the cape).

months.notes: Sea area. Monastir and El Kantaoui are popular wintering marinas.

tides.notes: North coast microtidal; tides become significant only further south in the Gulf of Gabès.

authority.name: Office National du Tourisme Tunisien (marinas); Tunisian Customs and Garde nationale maritime

notes: Not Schengen/EU: at the first port, clear customs, police and port; before leaving notify the Coast Guard the day before and clear with police and customs (Monastir). Officials may ask for 'gifts' (reported). Tunisian customs has an online service for pleasure-boat entries/exits (2023).

name: Bulgarian Black Sea coast
reach: Romanian border – Shabla – Kavarna – Balchik – Golden Sands – Varna – Cape Emine – Sveti Vlas – Nesebar – Pomorie – Burgas – Sozopol – Tsarevo – Ahtopol (Turkish border)

depth.notes: Open sea, non-tidal; Marina Dinevi (Sveti Vlas) max 3.5 m; Pomorie entrance shallow with rocks.

locks.notes: Distances (NM): Varna–Sveti Vlas 36, Balchik–Sveti Vlas 54, Sveti Vlas–Tsarevo 32, Sveti Vlas–Burgas 20, Sveti Vlas–Bosporus 110; direct line from Nesebar: Pomorie 7.3, Sozopol 14, Burgas 14, Tsarevo 29, Varna 33; Sozopol–Varna ~50.

rules.notes: Jets and motor craft max 5 kn (9 km/h) in water-sport corridors; jets at least 300 m off unguarded coasts and 200 m seaward of bathing-zone buoys. Marina Dinevi max 3 kn, VHF 73; Sozopol VHF 88. No restricted areas for visiting yachts any more.

season.closures: Prevailing NE winds in summer with a daily alternation of land and sea breezes; winter storm climate not confirmed.

months.notes: Sea area; most yacht traffic June–September. Late summer reported calmest.

tides.notes: Black Sea practically tideless; wind changes the level.

authority.name: Executive Agency Maritime Administration (ИАМА), Varna and Burgas

notes: Schengen at sea since 31 March 2024 (EU since 2007): from a Schengen port no border check; from Türkiye (non-Schengen) clear in with health, border police, customs and Maritime Administration, best at Tsarevo; from Romania Balchik; Varna and Burgas also. After clearing in no check-in at intermediate ports.

name: Romanian Black Sea coast and Danube mouths
reach: Vama Veche – Mangalia – Eforie – Constanța (Port Tomis) – Midia – Danube delta coast – Sulina (Sulina branch mouth) – Sfântu Gheorghe

depth.notes: Open sea, shallow off the delta; Sulina channel is the maintained deep-water mouth (safe-water buoy 45°08.075'N 29°47.613'E, then ~301° M into the breakwaters).

locks.notes: Distances (NM): Mangalia–Constanța 20 (direct line), Constanța–Sulina branch 85, Constanța–Bosporus 179, Mangalia–Balchik 30, Mangalia–Varna 46; Tulcea is ~40 NM up the Sulina branch.

rules.permit: Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve (ARBDD) access permit for people and a separate permit for vessels, issued in Tulcea or online (tourist day permit about €1.05 + VAT in 2026)
rules.notes: Inside the delta reserve, private boats visiting the nature areas need the ARBDD permit; some channels and strictly protected zones are closed. Port Tomis control on VHF 67 (report).

season.closures: Summer: onshore breeze from around midday dying at dusk, land breeze at night. Danube outflow off Sulina.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures known.

tides.notes: Black Sea practically tideless.

authority.name: Autoritatea Navală Română (ANR), Constanța; Administrația Rezervației Biosferei Delta Dunării (ARBDD), Tulcea

notes: Schengen since 2025 (sea borders since March 2024): from a non-Schengen port (Türkiye, Ukraine) clear in with border police, customs and health at a port of entry (Constanța/Tomis, Mangalia, Sulina), crew list in duplicate. Weather on VHF 25 at 04:04, 10:04, 16:04, 20:04 local; Navtex from Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye.

name: Istanbul Strait (Bosporus)
reach: Sea of Marmara (Sarayburnu/Kadıköy) – Bosporus – Black Sea entrance (Rumeli Feneri / Anadolu Feneri, Poyrazköy)

depth.notes: Deep-water strait, 700 m wide at its narrowest.

current.notes: Surface current south, up to ~4 kn, 7–8 kn at Kandilli; northbound undercurrent.

locks.notes: Strait ~31 km (17 NM) long. Constanța–Istanbul ~200 NM; Istanbul–Sozopol ~120 NM (blog); Bosporus–Sveti Vlas (BG) 110 NM.

rules.permit: No separate strait permit for a yacht; Turkish entry formalities and Transit Log apply when stopping in Türkiye
rules.notes: Turkish Straits Maritime Traffic Regulations: max 10 kn over ground; sailing under sail or oars, swimming and fishing banned inside the traffic separation scheme (motor through); no overtaking; vessels 20 m LOA and over report to the VTS (SP1/SP2, position and calling-point reports). Anchoring within 2.5 cables of the shore prohibited.

season.closures: Strong N winds (poyraz) against the south-going current make the northbound transit hard without a strong engine; heavy ship and ferry traffic day and night.

months.notes: Open all year. Large ships wait when the surface current exceeds 4–6 kn.

tides.notes: No tide; surface current runs south from the Black Sea, typically up to about 4 kn and 7–8 kn at Kandilli–Aşiyan, with a northbound undercurrent; strong southerlies can weaken or reverse it.

authority.name: Directorate General of Coastal Safety (KEGM) / Turkish Straits VTS (TBGTH), Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure

notes: Motor through, outside the shipping lanes where possible; ferries and local craft must give way to transiting vessels. Istanbul is a frontier port for clearing in/out of Türkiye (Transit Log). Not advisable to go north to Poyrazköy in strong N winds unless the engine is very powerful.

name: Çanakkale Strait (Dardanelles)
reach: Aegean entrance (Kumkale/Seddülbahir) – Kilitbahir/Çanakkale narrows – Gelibolu/Lapseki (Sea of Marmara)

depth.notes: Deep-water strait, 1.2–6 km wide.

locks.notes: Strait 61 km long. Istanbul–Antalya via the Dardanelles ~560 NM.

rules.permit: No separate strait permit for a yacht; Çanakkale is a Turkish port of entry
rules.notes: Same Turkish Straits rules as the Bosporus: 10 kn max over ground, no sailing, swimming or fishing inside the traffic separation scheme, no overtaking, VTS reporting for 20 m LOA and over, no anchoring within 2.5 cables of shore.

months.notes: Open all year. Hazardous-cargo and slow vessels wait when the current exceeds 4 kn.

tides.notes: No tide; surface current flows from the Marmara towards the Aegean with a saltier undercurrent beneath; northbound yachts keep close inshore (10–15 m contour) where it is weaker.

authority.name: Directorate General of Coastal Safety (KEGM) / Çanakkale VTS (TBGTH)

notes: Çanakkale is a frontier port for clearing in/out of Türkiye. Heavy ship traffic in the traffic separation scheme.

name: Göta kanal (Mem – Roxen – Boren – Motala; Karlsborg – Viken – Sjötorp)
reach: Mem on Slätbaken (Baltic) via Söderköping, Norsholm, Lake Roxen, Berg, Borensberg, Lake Boren and Motala to Lake Vättern (Östergötland section); Karlsborg via Bottensjön, Forsvik, Lake Viken, Töreboda to Sjötorp on Lake Vänern (Västergötland section)

depth.notes: TSFS 2019:140: max draught 2.82 m; the canal company may impose a lower temporary limit.

current.notes: Canal and lakes; no current of note.

locks.chamber: vessels max 30 m LOA × 7 m beam × 2.82 m draught × 22 m height (larger by approval; over 24 m notify in advance)
locks.hours: High season daily 09:00–18:00 (last locking earlier at some locks). Pre/post-season: convoys on a fixed itinerary with a lock keeper (Mem–Sjötorp 5 days; Express 3 days).
locks.notes: Per stage (official itinerary): Mem–Berg 15 locks/55 km; Berg–Borenshult 16/34 km; Borenshult–Motala 6; Vättern 32.5 km; Karlsborg–Forsvik 7.4 km; Forsvik–Töreboda 2/39 km; Töreboda–Sjötorp 19/19 km. Staircases: Carl Johan (7), Borenshult (5), Riksberg (3).

rules.permit: Canal ticket (AB Göta kanalbolag), priced by boat size, distance and season; includes 5 marina nights per marina on the booked distance in high season
rules.notes: 5 kn over ground on dug and blasted sections; no sailing, anchoring or mooring there except at jetties/harbours; no overtaking without consent; pleasure craft give way to all other vessels. Boats >15 m: AIS + VHF, watch ch 16 (10). Berg canal: meet only at the 9 marked places.

season.best: June – mid-August (high season); May/September in convoy
season.closures: 2026 season 5/6 May – 27 Sep (high season 16 Jun – 12 Aug). 2027: pre-season 4 May – 14 Jun, high season 15 Jun – 19 Aug, post-season 20 Aug – 30 Sep. No locking October–April.

months.notes: Closed for navigation outside the May–September season (official season dates 2026/2027). Ice dates not published.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: AB Göta kanalbolag, Motala (+46 141 20 20 50, info@gotakanal.se)

notes: Fees: Mini trip SEK 1,025 incl. 3 nights (Sjötorp–Lyrestad, Karlsborg–Vassbacken, Motala–Borensberg, Mem–Söderköping); extra night SEK 285 or SEK 1,500/week; 25 % off high-season tickets booked before 3 Apr 2027. Full canal ~5 days in convoy, 6–8 days in high season. Summit 91.5 m. Trollhätte kanal is ticketed separately by Sjöfartsverket.

name: Trollhätte kanal and Göta älv (Göteborg – Lilla Edet – Trollhättan – Vänersborg)
reach: Göteborg (Älvsborgsbron) up the Göta älv via Lilla Edet (Ströms sluss), the four Trollhättan locks and Brinkebergskulle to Vänersborg (Gropbron) on Lake Vänern

depth.notes: Fairway at least 6.3 m; lock sills 5.7 m at lowest water. 5.4 m draught only with a Sjöfartsverket permit.

current.notes: River fairway (Göta älv) for most of the 82 km; only ~10 km is dug canal. Current speed not published by the authority.

locks.chamber: vessels max 87 × 12.7 × 4.7 m (permit 89 × 13.4 × 5.4 m)
locks.hours: Pleasure craft daily 09:00–19:00 between Ströms sluss (Lilla Edet) and Gropbron (Vänersborg); extra spring 2026 openings 06:00–22:00 on 30/4–3/5 and 14–17/5. Merchant ships 24/7 all year, with priority.
locks.notes: Lilla Edet 1 lock (~6 m), Trollhättan 4 locks (~32 m), Brinkebergskulle 1 (~6 m); total lift 44 m. 12 bridges, 3 fixed: Stallbackabron 28 m (not openable), power lines 27 m. Openable: Klaffbron 3.5 m, Trollhättan rail 2.8 m, Gropbron 4.0 m, Vänersborg rail 2.0 m. VHF 9.

rules.permit: Lock fee SEK 1,200 one way for all locks (2026), card only at Kanalcentralen Trollhättan, incl. one night at Åkersjö guest harbour; 2027 proposal SEK 1,370 (+14.4 %); season passes sold
rules.notes: TSFS 2019:97 traffic rules. Commercial traffic has priority at locks and bridges; pleasure craft strongly advised not to transit in darkness or poor visibility.

season.closures: Planned lock maintenance closures published yearly (2026 PDF v12, e.g. Trollhättan and Brinkebergskulle in September); new larger locks are being planned by Sjöfartsverket/Trafikverket.

months.notes: Open all year for commercial traffic; pleasure-craft service 09:00–19:00 daily. Check the yearly planned-closure PDF.

tides.notes: River regulated by Vänern outflow; no tide information published by the authority.

authority.name: Sjöfartsverket (Swedish Maritime Administration), service tel. +46 10 478 6331 (09–19)

notes: Göteborg bridges (clearance): Älvsborgsbron 45 m, Hisingsbron 12 m (openable), Marieholmsbron 5.9 m, Angeredsbron 47 m, Jordfallsbron 11 m, Lilla Edetbron 10 m. Nordre älv alternative: Kungälv and Ytterby fixed 12.5 m. Göta kanal is 190 km further from Sjötorp across Vänern (118 km).

name: Dalslands kanal (Köpmannebro – Håverud – Bengtsfors – Töcksfors/Östervallskog)
reach: Köpmannebro on Lake Vänern north through Upperud, Håverud (aqueduct), Långed, Billingsfors, Bengtsfors, Lennartsfors and Töcksfors to Östervallskog (Värmland) and the Norwegian border lakes

depth.notes: Max draught 1.80 m above Upperud; Köpmannebro lock alone takes 3.0 m (2024 terms).

current.notes: Lakes linked by 12 km of dug canal.

locks.chamber: boats max 22.75 m × 4.05 m × 1.80 m (Köpmannebro only: 32 × 7.0 × 3.0 m)
locks.hours: Main season 2026: 11 Jun – 16 Aug. 2025 hours: late June/mid-Aug ~10:00–16/17:00, 30 Jun – 3 Aug ~09/10:00–18/19:00 (varies per station). Pre/post season (2026: 4 May – 10 Jun, 17 Aug – 30 Sep): openings by booking, 3 days ahead, SEK 425 per station (2025).
locks.notes: 31 locks at 17 stations, lift 66 m. Air draught: 17 m beyond Lennartsfors, 5 m beyond Töcksfors, 14.5 m beyond Ed, Snäcke canal 14 m, Silarna (above Gustavsfors) 11.75 m. No locking if it cannot finish before closing time.

rules.permit: Canal ticket from Dalslands Kanal AB (online); 2025 return ticket SEK 2,420 (<5 m) to 6,820 (≥14 m), or per-station single tickets
rules.notes: 3 kn in the dug canal sections; lakes per chart 956. Third-party liability insurance compulsory. Lifejackets compulsory while locking; no open fire, smoking, cooking or fuelling in locks; no swimming within 50 m of locks/bridges.

season.closures: Locks unmanned outside the main season (bookable openings May–September); closed October–April.

months.notes: Official season dates (2025, 2026). Ice not documented.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Dalslands Kanal AB, +46 530 44750, info@dalslandskanal.se

notes: Köpmannebro E45 road bridge opens only at set times in season (2026: 11–28 Jun 11:30/14:00; 29 Jun–26 Jul 10:00/13:30/17:30; 27 Jul–16 Aug 11:30/14:00). Chart 956 sold at Köpmannebro, Upperud, Lennartsfors, Töcksfors (SEK 560). Carry 2 boathooks and 4–5 fenders.

name: Södertälje kanal (Mälaren – Södertälje sluss – Baltic)
reach: Lake Mälaren (Mälarbron) through the Södertälje lock and the canal to the southern canal bridges and Igelstaviken towards the Baltic

depth.notes: Mon–Thu (11/7–19:00) from 27 Apr 2026 the Mälarhamnen–Igelstaviken fairway is closed to vessels over 70 m, 14 m beam or 4.5 m draught (NtM 20035(T)).

locks.chamber: 135 × 19.6 m (largest ship lock in the Nordics)
locks.hours: Pleasure craft southbound Mon–Fri 09:15, 11:15 … 21:15 (every 2 h), weekends/holidays hourly 08:15–22:15; northbound at :30 (Mon–Fri 09:30–21:30 every 2 h; weekends 08:30–22:30 hourly). Mon–Thu works periods: lock closed to boats over 24 m.
locks.notes: Mälarbron (bascule) 15.0 m between marks/13.8 m full width; pleasure openings Mon–Thu 09,11,13,15,18,19,21; Fri also 20; weekends hourly 08–21. Southern canal bridges 26.0 m closed, 41.5 m lift span open, fixed opening times (pre-notify 4 h, VHF 68).

rules.permit: Lock fee SEK 320 for pleasure craft, charged southbound
rules.notes: 6 kn throughout the canal. Contact VHF 14 or 68, tel. +46 771 630 655. Canal camera-monitored; signals per chart 6181.

season.closures: Weekday works restrictions from 27 Apr 2026 (see depth notes).

months.notes: Year-round service; schedule identical Jun–Aug and Sep–May per Sjöfartsverket.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Sjöfartsverket, Södertälje kanal

notes: Sailing yachts over 15 m air draught northbound must time Mälarbron openings. Southern bridges: winter/summer timetables (summer 19 Jun – 16 Aug 2026).

name: Strömsholms kanal (Mälaren/Strömsholm – Hallstahammar – Virsbo – Smedjebacken)
reach: Lake Mälaren at Strömsholm up the Kolbäcksån valley through Hallstahammar, Virsbo, Västanfors (Fagersta) and the Barken lakes to Smedjebacken

depth.notes: Boats max draught 1.35 m (1.5 m by dispensation from the canal office).

current.notes: 14 lakes linked by 14.4 km of cuts.

locks.chamber: boats max 18 m × 5 m × 1.35 m, height 2.5 m
locks.hours: Locking by timetable: low season one locking per direction per day, high season on average two; extra lockings until all waiting boats pass.
locks.notes: Lift about 100 m. Sites include Strömsholm, Västerkvarn (2), Prästforsen, Sörkvarn (3), Skantzen, Trångfors (2), Ålsätra, Seglingsberg, Virsbo, Västanfors, Semla (3).

rules.permit: Canal fee; season pass for the six locks Barken–Västanfors SEK 1,280 (operator FAQ, 2023)

season.closures: Usually opens the first Monday after Midsummer and closes on a Sunday in the 2nd week of August (2023: 26 Jun – 13 Aug). The canal bridge at Strömsholm was closed for repairs until spring 2026 (Trafikverket). 2026 dates not confirmed: operator website offline in Nov 2026.

months.notes: Short summer season (late June to mid-August) per operator FAQ; June before Midsummer also closed.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: AB Strömsholms kanal (tel. +46 220 100 11)

notes: Very small locks: check dimensions (18 × 5 m, 2.5 m height) before planning; most cruising yachts cannot pass with mast up. Confirm 2027 timetable with the canal office.

name: Vänern (Vänersborg – Sjötorp – Mariestad – Karlstad – Köpmannebro)
reach: Sweden's largest lake, linking the Trollhätte kanal (Vänersborg), Göta kanal (Sjötorp), Dalslands kanal (Köpmannebro) and Säffle kanal

depth.notes: Sea-going traffic limited by the Trollhätte locks (Vänermax 4.7 m).

locks.notes: Göta kanalbolag gives the Vänersborg – Sjötorp crossing as 118 km. Vänersborg bridges: Gropbron 4.0 m and rail bridge 2.0 m (opening), Dalbobron 15.5–17 m.

rules.notes: No general speed limit in Sweden; local limits by sign. Alcohol: 0.2 ‰ for boats ≥10 m or ≥15 kn.

months.notes: Lake open all year; canal connections are seasonal. Ice not documented in sources used.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Sjöfartsverket (fairways, Lotsområde Vänern); Transportstyrelsen (traffic rules)

notes: Large open lake: plan crossings for the weather. Göta kanal starts at Sjötorp (Mariestad side), Dalslands kanal at Köpmannebro.

name: Vättern (Motala – Karlsborg crossing of the Göta kanal)
reach: Lake Vättern, crossed by the Göta kanal between Motala (east) and Karlsborg (west)

depth.notes: Through traffic limited by Göta kanal draught 2.82 m.

locks.hours: Karlsborg road bridge opened remotely from Forsvik (in convoy season at set times)
locks.notes: Motala harbour – Karlsborg crossing 32.5 km (Göta kanalbolag).

rules.notes: In pre/post-season the Vättern crossing is free-sailing ('at your own pace') between convoy legs. Alcohol 0.2 ‰ for boats ≥10 m or ≥15 kn.

months.notes: Göta kanal locks at both ends closed October–April.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: AB Göta kanalbolag (canal ends); Transportstyrelsen (rules)

notes: Night harbours used by the canal itineraries: Motala marina, Karlsborg outer marina (outside the road bridge) or inner marina, Forsvik.

name: Mälaren (Stockholm Hammarby/Slussen – Västerås – Södertälje)
reach: Lake Mälaren from Stockholm (Hammarby lock / Slussen to the Baltic) west to Västerås and Köping, with the Södertälje canal to the south and Strömsholms kanal at Strömsholm

locks.hours: Stockholm locks (Ports of Stockholm), boats <50 m: 27 Apr – 27 Sep 2026 on demand 07:00–23:30, plus 00:00, 01:00, 02:00, 04:30; 28 Sep – 26 Apr 07:00–18:00 on demand, night lockings 19/22/00/01/02/04:30 on request (5 h notice).
locks.notes: Exits to the Baltic: Stockholm (Hammarby lock/Slussen, Ports of Stockholm, VHF 12/16) and Södertälje lock (Sjöfartsverket).

rules.permit: Stockholm lock: Mälaren → Baltic SEK 339, Baltic → Mälaren free; season pass 2026 SEK 1,479 (card only). Södertälje: SEK 320 southbound
rules.notes: No general speed limit; local limits by sign (Södertälje canal 6 kn). Alcohol 0.2 ‰ for boats ≥10 m or ≥15 kn.

months.notes: Locks operate all year with reduced winter hours.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Ports of Stockholm, Port and Traffic Control (BTC), +46 8 670 28 10, VHF 12/16

notes: Every passage between Mälaren and the sea is through a lock (Stockholm or Södertälje). Strömsholms kanal (small boats only) leaves from Strömsholm.

name: Telemarkskanalen (Skien – Norsjø – Ulefoss – Dalen; Notodden branch)
reach: Skien (Skien sluse) via Løveid to Norsjø; Ulefoss – Eidsfoss – Vrangfoss – Lunde – Kjeldal – Hogga (Bandak-Norsjøkanalen) and the lakes Flåvatn, Kviteseidvatn and Bandak to Dalen; branch Norsjø – Notodden without locks

depth.notes: Max keel depth 2.5 m; chambers 2.4 m. At Ulefoss sailing boats should use the outer guest pier for depth.

current.notes: River sections (Skienselva, Ulefoss–Strengen); strong current at Skien Langbrygga, quieter above the lock at Hjellebrygga.

locks.chamber: 31.4 × 6.6 m, 2.4 m depth (boats max 31.4 m × 6.6 m × 2.5 m keel; mast 16 m, 12.8 m Ulefoss–Dalen)
locks.hours: 2026: 26 Jun – 20 Aug, all locks staffed 09:00–18:00 (escorted locking only 17–20 Aug). Off season: Skien and Løveid on Fridays 09:00–12:00 (last 2 Oct 2026). Locking outside hours on request at cost.
locks.notes: 8 lock sites, 18 chambers, 72 m lift: Skien, Løveid (hydraulic), Ulefoss, Eidsfoss, Vrangfoss (5 chambers, 23 m), Lunde, Kjeldal, Hogga (hand-operated). Ulefoss–Strengen 17 km has 14 locks. First come, first served; passenger boats have priority. VHF 9.

rules.permit: Lock fee per lock site, paid by card at the first lock (2022 list: NOK 230–500 per site by length; Skien–Hogga one way NOK 2,090–3,100)
rules.notes: 5 kn in harbours and leads; 5 kn within 100 m of shore in Skien, Nome and Sauherad (incl. Årnes bird sanctuary). The canal is a drinking-water source: no emptying of septic/waste — pump-out at Skien, Ulefoss, Kviteseid, Dalen, Akkerhaugen.

season.closures: Upper locks (Ulefoss–Hogga) only staffed in the main season; outside it only Friday lockings at Skien and Løveid.

months.notes: Season 26 Jun – 20 Aug 2026; June before the opening also closed. Lower part (Skien, Løveid) has Friday lockings in spring/autumn.

tides.notes: Inland canal above Skien sluse; the Porsgrunnselva below is the approach from the coast.

authority.name: Telemarkskanalen (Vestfold og Telemark fylkeskommune), tel. +47 409 20 000

notes: Bridges: Porsgrunn (Frednes 13 m, Porsgrunn bru 8 m) open every half hour except weekdays 07–09 and 15–17 (VHF 12, +47 35 93 16 08); Elstrømbrua 16 m; Sundkilen swing bridge 4 m (09–11, 16–18). Skien–Notodden 80 km, 2 lock sites. Fuel: Ulefoss, Norsjø Ferieland, Dalen.

name: Saimaa lake system (Lappeenranta – Puumala – Savonlinna – Varkaus – Kuopio)
reach: Greater Saimaa and the connected lakes of the Vuoksi system: Lappeenranta, Puumala, Savonlinna, Haukivesi, Varkaus (Taipale and Konnus canals) to Kallavesi/Kuopio

depth.notes: Deep-channel network (≥4.2 m) of about 814 km reaching Kuopio; Taipale canal takes 4.35 m.

locks.chamber: Taipale canal (Varkaus): vessels 160.0 × 12.2 × 4.35 m, height 24.5 m; lift 4.6–6.0 m
locks.hours: Taipale: 24 h in season (bookings by 15:00 the previous business day in the shoulder season); Konnus: self-service, 24 h.
locks.notes: Mast over 12 m seriously limits routes off the main channels; some canal routes have 5.5 m bridges. Heinävesi route: see separate sheet. No access from the sea: Saimaa canal closed to pleasure craft.

rules.permit: No permit on Finnish inland waters; eastern border-zone waters need a Border Guard permit
rules.notes: No general speed limit; local limits and no-wake zones by sign. Alcohol limit 1.0 ‰ (rowing boats exempt). Mooring in natural harbours generally allowed, not near cottages or at private jetties.

season.closures: Ice in winter; locks have seasonal hours (vayla.fi).

months.notes: Peak season Midsummer – mid-August; ice in winter (dates not sourced). Saimaa is covered by the official marine weather forecast.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Väylävirasto / Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency (canals); Traficom (rules)

notes: Lake steamers link Savonlinna–Kuopio (12 h via the Heinävesi canals). Charter: Savonlinna–Puumala–Lappeenranta–Puumala–Savonlinna loop itineraries ~540 km in 14 days. Weather forecasts cover Saimaa; small-craft warning at 11 m/s.

name: Heinävesi route (Oravi – Pilppa – Vihovuonne – Kerma – Karvio; Varistaipale branch)
reach: From Haukivesi (Oravi) north through the Pilppa, Vihovuonne, Kerma and Karvio canals and Lake Kermajärvi to Heinävesi and on towards Kuopio; branch via Varistaipale and Taivallahti canals to Juojärvi

depth.notes: Karvio canal: max draught 1.8 m.

current.notes: Kermanvirta and canal reaches; Karvio lock fall 1.8 m.

locks.chamber: Karvio: vessels max 31.2 × 7.1 × 1.8 m, height 9.5 m
locks.hours: Karvio (self-service): May 07–21, Jun–Aug 07–24, Sep 07–18, Oct weekdays 07–17.
locks.notes: Pilppa, Vihovuonne, Kerma and Karvio: one self-service lock each; passenger boats have priority. Varistaipale branch: 4 chambers at Varistaipale + 2 at Taivallahti (height limit 12.5 m).

rules.notes: Self-service locks with Finnish/English instructions. Finnish inland rules (no CEVNI). Alcohol 1.0 ‰.

season.closures: Lock service roughly May – October (Karvio hours).

months.notes: Karvio lock operates May–October per vayla.fi; winter ice.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Väylävirasto / Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency

notes: Karvio canal (1895–96) opened the Kuopio–Heinävesi steamer route; Kerma, Vihovuonne and Pilppa (1903–06) opened it to Savonlinna. s/s Heinävesi: Savonlinna–Kuopio 12 h. Valamo monastery is on the Varistaipale/Juojärvi branch. Kermajärvi nature reserve on the route.

name: Saimaa canal (Lappeenranta – Vyborg) — closed to pleasure craft
reach: Lappeenranta (Lake Saimaa) to the Vyborg Bay, Gulf of Finland; 23.3 km in Finland, 19.6 km in Russia (leased)

locks.chamber: vessels up to 82 m long (Wikipedia)
locks.notes: Present alignment opened 1968.

rules.notes: Pleasure-craft traffic suspended since 15 Apr 2024; Nuijamaa, Santio and Haapasaari border crossing points closed for leisure craft. In 2026 the canal opened only for cargo and passenger ships. Saimaa cannot be reached from the sea by yacht.

season.closures: Closed to pleasure craft until further notice (checked 21 Nov 2026).

months.notes: Closed all year to pleasure craft since April 2024.

tides.notes: Inland lake/canal, non-tidal.

authority.name: Väylävirasto / Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency

notes: Route planning: treat Saimaa as reachable only by road/trailer or charter. Eastern border zone waters need a Border Guard permit.

name: Stockholm archipelago (Furusund – Vaxholm – Sandhamn – Dalarö – Utö)
reach: Stockholm (Saltsjön) and the archipelago from Furusund/Norrtälje in the north through Vaxholm, Grinda, Möja and Sandhamn to Dalarö, Utö and Landsort

depth.notes: Short cuts: Baggensstäket (Saltsjöbaden–Stockholm) max draught 2.6 m, air 30 m; Strömma kanal (to Sandhamn) max draught 1.4 m, air 11.5 m.

locks.notes: Sjöfartsverket (ship routes to Skeppsbron): Sandhamn via Stavsnäs 37 M; Furusund and Möja via Vaxholm 38.2 M; Dalarö via Stavsnäs/Vaxholm 49.8 M; Utö via Stavsnäs 61.1 M; Norrtälje 59 M; Saltsjöbaden via Baggensstäket 11 M; Saltsjöbaden–Sandhamn via Strömma kanal 19.8 M.

rules.notes: No general speed limit; local limits by sign (e.g. 5 kn within 100 m of land in Nämdöskärgården NP, which also bans motorboats/anchoring in listed zones, 01FS 2026:22). Old SJÖFS 2008:97 archipelago rules repealed 1 Jul 2026. Alcohol 0.2 ‰ (≥10 m or ≥15 kn).

season.closures: Seal and bird sanctuaries: seasonal no-access zones, often incl. water within 100 m (typically 1 Apr–31 Jul or 1 Feb–15 Aug), marked on charts and by yellow signs. Right of public access: mooring/one night on uninhabited shores away from houses, not in garden areas.

months.notes: Sea area, no closures; sanctuaries closed in spring/early summer. Ice in hard winters not sourced.

tides.notes: Baltic: no tides; water level varies with wind and air pressure (rarely more than 1 m).

authority.name: Sjöfartsverket (fairways, Stockholm pilot area VHF 13); Länsstyrelsen Stockholm (protected areas); Transportstyrelsen (rules)

notes: Classic stops: Vaxholm, Grinda, Möja, Sandhamn (KSSS guest harbours), Dalarö, Utö (guest harbour), Landsort (Sweden's oldest lighthouse). Charter legs: Vaxholm–Grinda 9 NM, Grinda–Möja 12, Möja–Sandhamn 9, Sandhamn–Utö 30, Utö–Dalarö 19. Busy ferry traffic in the main fairways.

name: Bohuslän coast (Göteborg – Marstrand – Orust/Tjörn – Lysekil – Smögen – Strömstad/Koster)
reach: Swedish west coast from the Göta älv mouth at Göteborg north through Öckerö, Marstrand, the inner route behind Tjörn and Orust, Lysekil, Smögen/Kungshamn, Hunnebostrand, Fjällbacka to Strömstad and the Koster islands

locks.notes: Legs (boote-magazin): Göteborg Lilla Bommen–Öckerö 11 nm; Öckerö–Marstrand just under 24 nm (via the Kattegat); Marstrand–Uddevalla ~37 nm inner route (Älgöfjorden, Hakefjorden/Tjörnbron, Havstensfjorden). Sotekanalen ~3 nm cuts behind Smögen/Sotenäs.

rules.notes: Local speed limits by sign in harbours and sounds; no general limit. Seal/bird sanctuaries with seasonal access bans (charted, yellow signs). Kosterhavet national park off Strömstad. Alcohol 0.2 ‰ (≥10 m or ≥15 kn).

season.closures: Inner fairways are narrow in places (two boats barely pass). The skerry belt shelters most legs, but the Skagerrak builds steep seas outside it; Kattegat legs uncomfortable in F6–7.

months.notes: Sea area; no closures.

tides.notes: Tide information not found in the sources used.

authority.name: Sjöfartsverket; Länsstyrelsen Västra Götaland (protected areas)

notes: Göteborg bridges: Älvsborgsbron 45 m, Hisingsbron 12 m (opens). Harbours: Marstrand (floating pontoons, rope ferry), Uddevalla (Bäveån), Grundsund (sheltered, fills up), Koster, Väderöarna. Right of public access lets you moor to the rocks away from houses.

name: Oslofjord and Norwegian Skagerrak coast (Oslo – Færder – Kragerø – Arendal – Kristiansand – Farsund)
reach: Inner and outer Oslofjord (Oslo, Drøbaksundet, Moss, Son, Tønsberg, Tjøme/Færder) and the Sørlandet coast west via Langesund, Kragerø, Risør, Lyngør, Arendal, Grimstad, Lillesand (Blindleia) and Kristiansand to Farsund

depth.notes: Depths drop fast at skerries; shoals at river mouths and between close islands. Blindleia: sections 6.5 m wide with little water.

current.notes: Currents up to about 3 kn reported on the Sørlandet coast; jet effects between islands.

locks.notes: Distances: Arendal–Kristiansand 40.5 nm; Farsund–Kristiansand 52 nm; Blindleia (Kristiansand–Lillesand inside route) 12 miles; Koster–Oslo ~70 nm; outer fjord mouth ~12 nm wide; Drøbaksundet ~7 cables.

rules.notes: Speed limits set by each municipality (commonly 5 kn near land/harbours). Lifejacket must be worn on boats under 8 m. Alcohol 0.8 ‰ (<15 m). Strict fishing rules in the Oslofjord (cod banned all year). Færder national park.

season.best: June and September (Oslofjord); mid-June – end of August (Sørlandet)
season.closures: Prevailing W–SW wind, rarely E, often parallel to the coast; outer fjord calm mornings with afternoon sea breeze; short steep seas in SW winds against the current; thundery showers after hot days. Busy high season.

months.notes: Sea area; no closures.

tides.notes: Tidal range not quantified in the sources used; local guides note no tide in the Sørlandet anchorages.

authority.name: Kystverket (fairways); Sjøfartsdirektoratet (boating rules); municipalities (speed limits)

notes: Oslo: Aker Brygge Marina (~50 guest berths, VHF 72), Kongen Marina, KNS Dronningen. Tønsberg bridges open 10:05, 13:05, 19:05 in summer (VHF 12). Moss canal bridge ~4.5 m. Tjøme ~100 guest berths. Guest berths ~€30–70/night (40 ft). Norway is outside the EU: alcohol/tobacco quotas.

name: Archipelago Sea and Åland (Mariehamn – Kökar – Utö – Nagu – Turku – Naantali)
reach: Åland islands and the Archipelago Sea from the Sea of Åland east to Hanko/Kimitoön and north to Uusikaupunki, including Turku, Naantali, Nagu, Korpo, Houtskär, Iniö, Utö and Jurmo

depth.notes: Many guest piers shallow (Jurmo too shallow for 2.4 m); 900 NM of official fairways, cardinal marks dominate.

locks.notes: Port of Turku: Turku–Mariehamn 92 NM, Turku–Helsinki via Hanko 147 NM, via Utö 187 NM. Naantali not accessible above 16.5 m air draught. Mariehamn has two marinas (west and east harbour).

rules.notes: No general limit; local limits/no-wake zones by sign. Alcohol 1.0 ‰ (Finland). Landing banned on many bird islands; approach banned to some seal islands; military areas. Åland: own boat law; outside the EU tax area (alcohol/tobacco limits to mainland). Archipelago VTS VHF 71.

season.closures: Winds mostly SW–W; strong early-summer sea breezes with short steep seas between outer skerries; first autumn storms end of September. Night navigation between skerries not recommended.

months.notes: Sea area; ice in winter (Baltic), boating mainly May–September.

tides.notes: Baltic: no tides; level varies with wind and pressure, rarely over 1 m.

authority.name: Traficom (rules); Fintraffic Archipelago VTS; Metsähallitus (protected islands); Åland government

notes: Everyman's right: mooring on skerries generally allowed, not at private jetties or close to cottages/saunas. Guest harbours €5 (small islands) to €15–40; Turku guest marina €35 for 15 m incl. sauna. Classics: Utö, Jurmo, Nötö, Nagu Kyrkbacken, Korpoström, Kökar, Föglö.

name: Gulf of Finland coast (Hanko – Helsinki – Porvoo – Loviisa – Kotka)
reach: Finnish south coast and archipelago from Hanko east via Ekenäs, Porkkala, Helsinki, Sipoo, Porvoo, Loviisa and Kotka to the Russian border (Virolahti)

locks.notes: Hanko–St Petersburg ~220 NM; Helsinki–Tallinn <50 NM (42 NM to the Old City Marina). Porvoo old town 2 km up the Porvoo river, 12 M from the main inner west–east fairway; Loviisa 6 M off the inner fairway.

rules.permit: Border-zone permit (Border Guard) in the eastern border area
rules.notes: Alcohol 1.0 ‰. Bird/seal islands with landing or approach bans; military restricted areas. Defence Forces often close sea areas off Kotka (drone measures) — check Fintraffic warnings and VHF 16. Border stations Nuijamaa, Santio, Haapasaari closed to leisure craft.

season.closures: Afternoon sea breeze on sunny days, light land breeze at night; SW winds most common. Very busy Helsinki–Tallinn ferry lanes (20+ departures each way daily). Small-craft notice at 11 m/s forecast, gale 14, storm 21.

months.notes: Sea area; winter ice. Season peaks late June – mid-August.

tides.notes: Baltic: no tides; wind/pressure-driven level changes, rarely over 1 m.

authority.name: Traficom; Fintraffic VTS; Finnish Border Guard; Metsähallitus (Gulf of Finland national park)

notes: Saimaa cannot be reached from here (Saimaa canal closed to pleasure craft). Gulf of Finland national park off Kotka: outer-archipelago harbours safe only in calm weather. Sipoo inner route has a low bridge.

name: South Funen archipelago and the Belts (Faaborg – Lyø – Avernakø – Svendborg – Ærø – Lillebælt)
reach: Det Sydfynske Øhav (Faaborg, Bjørnø, Lyø, Avernakø, Svendborg, Tåsinge, Ærø/Ærøskøbing/Marstal) with the southern Lillebælt and the western approaches of Storebælt

depth.notes: Shallow archipelago; buoyed channels such as Mørkedyb to Marstal. Lyø entrance unmarked.

locks.notes: Visit Faaborg legs: Faaborg–Bjørnø ~3 NM, Bjørnø–Lyø ~6 NM, Lyø–Avernakø ~5 NM, Avernakø–Faaborg ~9 NM via Svelmø. Ferries: Svendborg–Ærøskøbing 75 min; Faaborg–Avernakø 35 min, –Lyø 1 h 20.

rules.notes: Most police districts: 5 kn within 300 m of the shore for motorboats in summer; many harbours 3 kn. Jet skis banned within 300 m (cross at right angles <5 kn) and in reserves. Alcohol 0.5 ‰ for craft that need a certificate. Svelmø private: no landing.

season.closures: Harbours fill up in high season: arrive before 14:00 (Faaborg, Avernakø, Lyø).

months.notes: Sea area; no closures.

tides.notes: Tide information not found in the sources used.

authority.name: Søfartsstyrelsen (Danish Maritime Authority); Fyns Politi (local sailing rules)

notes: Harbours: Faaborg ~75 guest berths, sheltered from all directions (MarinaBooking); Bjørnø 4–5 keelboats, DKK 75 self-service; Lyø ~85 berths (anchor at Revkrogen if full); Avernakø ~25 berths (or Korshavn). Denmark does not take part in the ICC scheme.

name: Limfjord (Aalborg – Løgstør – Livø – Mors/Nykøbing – Struer – Thyborøn)
reach: The Limfjord across North Jutland from Hals/Aalborg (Kattegat) via Løgstør, Livø, Nykøbing Mors, Sallingsund and Struer to Thyborøn (North Sea)

depth.notes: Through route Kattegat–North Sea fine for deep-draught yachts; outlying bays and sounds: max ~1.8 m. Deepest at Hvalpsund (24 m).

current.notes: Westerly gales raise the level by about 1.5 m, easterlies lower it by almost 1 m.

locks.hours: Bascule bridges: opening times on large displays at each bridge; request with flag 'N' or VHF 16.
locks.notes: Sallingsund high bridge (south of Nykøbing) 26 m fixed; several opening bridges, including Aalborg.

rules.notes: Danish coastal rules: 5 kn within 300 m of shore for motorboats in summer in most police districts, harbours often 3 kn. Dogs on a lead on Livø.

season.best: June – September (Limfjorden Rundt regatta in September)
season.closures: Prevailing NW winds; short steep chop in strong winds, worst entering harbours. Easterly 'Øster' spells bring weeks of warm weather.

months.notes: Sea-connected fjord; no closures.

tides.notes: Tidal range plays no role; wind set-up dominates (+1.5 m W gales, −1 m E winds).

authority.name: Søfartsstyrelsen; Vejdirektoratet (bridges)

notes: Aalborg: Skudehavn and Vestre Bådehavn near the centre; Løgstør guest harbour in the old canal; Livø harbour busy, many anchorages round the island; Hanklit cliffs (Mors). Harbour info: havneguide.dk.

name: Nord-Ostsee-Kanal / Kiel Canal (Brunsbüttel – Kiel-Holtenau)
reach: Brunsbüttel locks (canal km 1.5) to Kiel-Holtenau locks (km 98.0), with the Gieselau junction (km 40.5), Obereidersee/Rendsburg (km 66), Borgstedter See (km 67.5/70) and Flemhuder See (km 85.4)

depth.notes: Seaway 11 m deep. Recreational craft drawing more than 3.1 m need a pilot. Gieselau and Dückerswisch berths: max draught 2.40 m.

locks.chamber: Large locks 310 × 42 m (both ends); small locks 125 × 22 m (Brunsbüttel only)
locks.hours: Locks work round the clock, but pleasure craft may transit only within the daylight hours (CET; +1 h in summer time): 07:30–17:00 in early January and December, 02:30–22:00 in June and early July
locks.notes: Kiel-Holtenau small locks permanently closed: yachts lock through the large chambers after the ships (one interrupted white light = enter). VHF 13 Kiel Canal I (Brunsbüttel), 2 Kiel Canal II (to Breiholz), 3 Kiel Canal III (to Holtenau), 12 Kiel Canal IV (Holtenau). Lockmaster Kiel +49 431 3603-152, Brunsbüttel +49 4852 885-252.

rules.permit: Transit fee for recreational craft until 31 Dec 2026 (about €12–43 by length; online at wsv.webshop.bund.de, pay machine west of Tiessenkai in Kiel, or at Gieselau lock); free for recreational craft from 1 Jan 2027
rules.notes: Transit only, daylight only, never in reduced visibility; plan to reach a recreational berth before dark. 12 km/h over ground. No sailing, except motor-sailing with a black cone point down. No water-skiing, jet skis, windsurfing or SUP. AIS class A/B for boats ≥20 m. No self-steering gear. Towing: one boat <15 m, min 9 km/h.

season.closures: Daylight-hours table in the WSA leaflet (April 2026). In May 2026 the Brunsbüttel small locks closed by day on 29–30 May for crane work (yachts used the large locks).

months.notes: Open all year; the daylight transit window is shortest in December–January (07:30–17:00 CET).

tides.notes: The canal is not tidal, but the Elbe off Brunsbüttel is: the Alter Vorhafen waiting area depends on the tide, the inner Binnenhafen is reachable at any time.

authority.name: WSA Nord-Ostsee-Kanal (Brunsbüttel / Kiel)

notes: Recreational berths: Brunsbüttel km 1.8 (max 72 h), Dückerswisch km 20.7, Gieselau km 40.5, Obereidersee km 66 (Rendsburg), Borgstedter See km 67.5/70 (bridge 22.5 m), Flemhuder See km 85.4 (10 dolphin berths, 2–4.5 m), Kiel-Holtenau km 98.5; all others max 24 h. About 8–10 h for a full transit.

name: Schlei (Schleimünde – Kappeln – Schleswig)
reach: Schleimünde (Baltic entrance) – Maasholm – Kappeln (bascule bridge) – Arnis – Lindaunis (rail/road bridge) – Missunde – Schleswig

depth.notes: Average depth about 3 m, average width 1.3 km; keep to the buoyed channel in the narrows (Stexwiger Enge 280 m wide).

locks.notes: No locks. Kappeln bascule bridge (2025 timetable): opens 20 min before each hour for 15 min. Lindaunis bridge (2026): openings at 10:30, 11:30 … 17:30, max 10 km/h through the opening, Schleswig-bound boats first; special openings must be requested from Deutsche Bahn 10 working days ahead.

rules.notes: 10 km/h through the Lindaunis bridge opening. The Schleimündung nature reserve is covered by the Ostsee-SH-NSG-Befahrensverordnung (restricted navigation); Hestholm island is protected.

season.closures: Lindaunis bridge closed to shipping 3 Nov 2025 – 25 Mar 2026 (construction of the replacement bridge; the road bridge closes for good in 2027), so the upper Schlei (Lindaunis – Schleswig) was cut off over winter.

months.notes: Upper Schlei above Lindaunis: no bridge openings Nov–March in 2025/26 because of the bridge works.

authority.name: WSA Ostsee (federal waterway); Deutsche Bahn (Lindaunis bridge)

notes: Harbours: Maasholm, Kappeln, Arnis, Lindaunis, Schleswig Stadthafen. Laboe – Maasholm about 20 NM.

name: Vorpommern Bodden waters (Darß-Zingst, Hiddensee, West Rügen, Strelasund)
reach: Ribnitz-Damgarten – Saaler/Bodstedter Bodden – Zingster Strom (Meiningen bridge) – Barth – Grabow – Barhöft – Hiddensee fairway (Neuendorf, Vitte, Kloster) – Schaproder and Wieker Bodden (Wiek) – Strelasund (Stralsund) – Jasmunder Bodden

depth.notes: Narrow buoyed fairways with very shallow water either side, especially west of the Meiningen bridge to Ribnitz and at the Bülten bank; sandbanks off Bock and SW Hiddensee (stay in the fairway Stralsund – Barhöft). Dabitz harbour: unbuoyed approach, daylight only.

locks.notes: Meiningen bridge (Zingster Strom) is the only bridge in the Darß-Zingst Bodden; Ziegelgraben bridge at Stralsund (Rügen side).

rules.notes: NPBefVMVK (national parks Vorpommersche Boddenlandschaft, Jasmund, Südost-Rügen zones I/II): 12 kn in buoyed fairways, 8 kn outside; 16 kn north of buoys 5/6 (Hiddensee fairway) and 10/11 (Stralsund north fairway). Motorboats banned outside fairways in the mapped areas; jet skis, hovercraft, water-skiing and parasailing banned. Bird islands Oie and Kirr: landing only with permit.

season.closures: Ice in cold winters: in late Jan–Feb 2026 ice up to 25 cm stopped the Hiddensee ferries (icebreaker service only) and a night-navigation ban (17:30–07:30) applied around Stralsund and the Bodden and Peenestrom harbours.

months.notes: Ice in cold winters only (e.g. late January – February 2026); no regular closure.

authority.name: WSA Ostsee (federal waterways); Nationalparkamt Vorpommern

notes: Day legs (South Coast Baltic): Barth – Neuendorf 26 NM, Neuendorf – Wiek 11, Wiek – Stralsund 22.4, Stralsund – Barhöft 8.9, Barhöft – Zingst 24, Zingst – Ribnitz 21 NM. The Hiddensee fairway is narrow and shared with the ferries. Stralsund Citymarina next to the old town.

name: Peenestrom, Achterwasser and Greifswalder Bodden south shore
reach: Greifswald (Ryck) – Freest/Kröslin – Peenemünde – Wolgast (Peene bridge) – Krummin – Achterwasser (Zinnowitz) – Lassan – Zecherin bridge – Karnin – Kleines Haff (buoy Peenestrom Süd/H1)

depth.notes: Keep strictly to the channel after the Wolgast bridge (shallow both sides) and in the narrow channel south of Zecherin. Achterwasser: enter at buoy PN 76 between Lieper Winkel and Gnitz, cardinal-marked shoals, keep clear of Görmitz; no buoyage to Zinnowitz (2–2.5 m), daylight only. Freesendorfer Haken shallow.

locks.notes: Bridges: Wolgast Peene bridge (bascule, timed openings; waits common), Zecherin bascule bridge (6 m closed, three openings a day), Karnin lift bridge (monument, fixed open span), Wieck wooden bascule bridge on the Ryck (manual).

rules.notes: Many set nets (Stellnetze) on the Greifswalder Bodden, e.g. at Gahlkower Haken. Ruden island is a nature reserve; its small harbour can no longer be used. Night-navigation ban in ice periods (Feb 2026).

season.closures: Ice in cold winters (Jan–Feb 2026: night-navigation ban 17:30–07:30 at the Bodden and Peenestrom harbours).

months.notes: Ice in cold winters only.

authority.name: WSA Ostsee

notes: Day legs: Greifswald – Lubmin 14 NM, Lubmin – Kröslin 12, Kröslin – Krummin 13–14, Krummin – Zecherin bridge 15 (about 3 h), Krummin – Ueckermünde 28–29, Rankwitz – Zinnowitz 11 NM. Marina Kröslin (South Coast Baltic info lounge), Horn shipyard at Wolgast.

name: Szczecin Lagoon / Stettiner Haff, Świna and the Świnoujście – Szczecin fairway
reach: Kleines Haff (Ueckermünde, Mönkebude, Altwarp) and Wielki Zalew (Nowe Warpno, Trzebież, Stepnica); Świnoujście – Kanał Piastowski – Szczecin fairway; Dziwna and Zalew Kamieński to Wolin, Kamień Pomorski and Dziwnów

depth.notes: Świnoujście – Szczecin fairway deepened to 12.5 m (in use since 9 May 2022); outside it the lagoon is shallow – very shallow on the north edge before Zatoka Skoszewska and at the Głęboki Nurt entrance to the Dziwna (stay in the buoyage). Wolin harbour 3.5 m.

rules.notes: No border control or clearance between Germany and Poland (Schengen), but random checks happen well inside the border. Share the Szczecin fairway with ships: keep to its right-hand edge; the quiet Kanał Skolwiński passes west of Wyspa Żurawia.

authority.name: Urząd Morski w Szczecinie (PL); WSA Ostsee (DE)

notes: Day legs: Ueckermünde – Szczecin 37 NM, Świnoujście – Ueckermünde 24, Stepnica – Świnoujście 22, Szczecin – Stepnica 15–16, Nowe Warpno – Świnoujście 14, Świnoujście – Wolin 21. Kanał Piastowski (Kaiserfahrt, 12 km) bypasses the old Świna. Marina Świnoujście (Basen Północny), Szczecin North East Marina; Dąbie lake marinas can step masts for boats from Berlin.

name: Martwa Wisła, Motława and Szkarpawa (Gdańsk – Vistula Lagoon, E70)
reach: Gdańsk Old Town (Motława) – Martwa Wisła (Sobieszewo bridge km 8.93) – Przegalina lock (km 0.55) – across the Wisła – Szkarpawa (Gdańska Głowa lock, km 0.2) – Vistula Lagoon; Wisła Śmiała to the sea at Górki

locks.hours: 2026: Przegalina Południowa and Gdańska Głowa until 23 Apr Mon–Fri 07:00–15:00 (weekends closed); 24 Apr – 4 Oct daily 07:00–19:00; otherwise by arrangement two working days ahead (by 13:00)
locks.notes: Both locks may close without notice when the Baltic/lagoon level is high and strong northerly winds push water in (cofka): phone first. Przegalina (58) 323 93 76 / 786 876 453; Gdańska Głowa (55) 247 17 07 / 735 094 723.

rules.permit: Lock dues per the Minister of Infrastructure notice of 25 July 2025 (rates from 1 Jan 2026)
rules.notes: Sobieszewo bascule bridge (season 25 Apr – 4 Oct): 08:30, 10:30, 13:00, 14:30, 17:00, 19:00 (+21:00 weekends); off season 08:30, 10:30, 13:00, 17:00, 19:00 except ice; VHF 09; dawn to dusk only. Motława: Stągiewny bridge lifts at 08:10–20:10 every 2 h Apr–Oct (10:10, 12:10, 14:10 Nov–Mar), book 1 h ahead, VHF 15/14.

season.closures: Reduced lock hours outside 24 Apr – 4 Oct; lock closures at high water with northerly winds.

authority.name: PGW Wody Polskie RZGW Gdańsk (Zarząd Zlewni w Tczewie)

notes: Day legs (South Coast Baltic): Gdańsk – Błotnik 11.9 NM, Gdańsk – Rybina 21.6, Rybina – Elbląg 14.6 NM. Gdynia – Gdańsk 13 NM by sea and the Martwa Wisła. Footbridges to Ołowianka and Wyspa Spichrzów open on a half-hourly/hourly cycle.

name: Vistula Lagoon (Polish part) and the Vistula Spit canal (Nowy Świat)
reach: Gulf of Gdańsk – outer port and lock at Nowy Świat (Vistula Spit) – lagoon fairway – Elbląg river to Elbląg; lagoon harbours Krynica Morska, Kąty Rybackie, Tolkmicko, Frombork, Nowa Pasłęka. The Russian part (Kaliningrad Bay) is not open to EU yachts.

depth.notes: Waterway designed for 5 m (2.5 m before the project). The last stretch of the Elbląg river to the port turning basin was still unfinished (planned by late 2026). Lagoon outside the fairway shallow.

locks.chamber: 269 × 25 m (canal 1,536 m long)
locks.notes: Canal opened 17 Sep 2022; two swing road bridges (DW 501, spans 19.5 m and 40 m). Passages: 1,589 (2023), 1,909 (2024), 1,340 (2025), mostly leisure craft.

rules.notes: Stay on the Polish side of the state border across the lagoon. Entry into Russia via the Vistula or Curonian lagoon was never allowed (Baltiysk was the only port of entry); Germany warns against all travel to Russia and individual boat trips in Kaliningrad coastal waters need a special permit.

authority.name: Urząd Morski w Gdyni (canal and lagoon fairway)

notes: Waterway 22.88 km: 2.32 km spit cut with outer port and lock, 10.18 km lagoon, 10.38 km Elbląg river. Day legs: Elbląg – Tolkmicko 15.1 NM, Tolkmicko – Frombork 10.2, Krynica Morska – Kąty Rybackie 14 NM.

name: Kanał Elbląski / Elbląg Canal (Ostróda – Miłomłyn – Elbląg, inclined planes)
reach: Ostróda – Miłomłyn – five inclined planes (Buczyniec, Kąty, Oleśnica, Jelenie, Całuny) – Lake Drużno – Elbląg river; branches to Iława and Lake Jeziorak (151.7 km with branches)

depth.notes: Design craft 24.48 × 2.98 m, 1.1 m draught (about 50 t).

locks.hours: 2026 season 25 Apr – 4 Oct: inclined planes 08:00–19:00 daily; locks Miłomłyn (km 0), Zielona (km 4.62), Ostróda (km 15.4), Mała Ruś (km 19.13) 09:00–20:00 daily
locks.notes: Boats ride the inclined planes on rail cars (rises: Buczyniec 20.4 m, Kąty 18.83 m, Oleśnica 21.97 m, Jelenie 21.97 m, Całuny 13.72 m; nearly 100 m in all). Kąty was under repair in 2026, its opening to be announced separately. Off season the locks can work Mon–Fri 07:00–15:00 if booked the day before.

rules.permit: Lock and inclined-plane dues per the Minister of Infrastructure notice of 25 July 2025
rules.notes: On the rail cars: lift centreboard, rudder and outboard, lash the mast, crew member at the gong, nobody leaves the car; fixed propellers must overhang the car floor (about 3.5 m at Buczyniec and Całuny, 1.5 m on the middle planes). Planes: (55) 248 70 92, +48 510 043 037.

season.closures: Inclined planes and locks open only 25 Apr – 4 Oct (2026).

months.notes: Inclined planes closed outside the 25 April – 4 October season (2026 dates).

authority.name: PGW Wody Polskie RZGW Gdańsk, Zarząd Zlewni w Elblągu

notes: Polish Historic Monument; passenger boats since 1927. Renovated 2011–2015. Check the daily Informacja żeglugowa for Kąty before setting out.

name: Curonian Lagoon, Lithuanian part (Klaipėda – Nida, Nemunas delta)
reach: Klaipėda (Smiltynė yacht club, Castle harbour on the Danė) – Juodkrantė – Nida; Nemunas delta: Atmata, Minija (Mingė), Šyša (Šilutė), Uostadvaris; Dreverna. The lagoon south of Nida is Russian.

depth.notes: Buoyed channel Klaipėda – Nida silts up in the last third: stay inside the buoys. Pass Kiaulės Nugara island only on its west side. Harbours: Šilutė 1.5–1.8 m, Uostadvaris 1.6–1.8 m (silting), Minija 2.4–3 m to Mingė, Dreverna max 1.2 m.

locks.notes: Klaipėda Castle harbour swing bridge opens hourly (manual). King Wilhelm canal (Mingė – Dreverna – Klaipėda) only partly passable for small boats; Lankupiai lock for small craft only.

rules.notes: Curonian Spit national park: sailing, mooring and anchoring restricted in core zones. Register arrival in Klaipėda with the harbour office on VHF; Lithuanian border police may stop yachts. Nida is about 2 km from the Russian border: do not cross it; Germany warns against travel to Russia.

authority.name: Klaipėda harbour office; Curonian Spit National Park

notes: Day legs: Klaipėda – Nida 26 NM, Nida – Mingė 11 NM, Mingė – Klaipėda 36 NM, Dreverna – Klaipėda 14.7 NM. Nida's south basin has lit pier heads. NE winds build a short steep sea along the whole lagoon; the Juodkrantė quay is exposed to NE.

name: German Baltic coast west (Flensburg Fjord, Kiel Bay, Fehmarn, Lübeck Bay)
reach: Flensburg Fjord – Schleimünde – Eckernförde – Kiel Fjord (Laboe, Kiel-Holtenau) – Hohwacht Bay – Heiligenhafen – Fehmarn (Fehmarnsund, Burgtiefe) – Lübeck Bay (Neustadt, Travemünde)

rules.notes: Putlos/Todendorf firing ranges, Hohwacht Bay (sea danger area about 486 km²): beacon SW of Heiligenhafen flashes red for Putlos, yellow for Todendorf, both alternately; guard boats, VHF 11/16; times on ELWIS. Nature reserves with navigation rules (OstseeSHNSGBefV): Geltinger Birk, Holnis, Schleimündung, Schwansener See, Bottsand, Graswarder, Krummsteert/Fehmarn, Grüner Brink, Dassower See.

tides.notes: Practically non-tidal; water level changes with wind (storm surges and wind-driven low water).

authority.name: WSA Ostsee / GDWS

notes: Kalkgrund light (outer Flensburg Fjord) in emergency mode, unreliable (2026). Fehmarnsund tunnel opening now 2032. Legs: Heiligenhafen – Laboe 33 NM, Laboe – Maasholm 20, Marstal – Heiligenhafen 37 NM. Charter bases Heiligenhafen and Fehmarn.

name: Mecklenburg coast (Wismar Bay – Rostock – Darß)
reach: Wismar Bay (Boltenhagen, Poel/Timmendorf, Kirchdorf, Wismar) – Salzhaff (Rerik) – Kühlungsborn – Warnemünde/Rostock – Fischland-Darß outer coast

rules.notes: Wismar Bay: Walfisch island is a nature reserve, no landing; local clubs ask for 8 kn in bird-sensitive zones (voluntary). Salzhaff entrance about 80 m wide, unbuoyed, variable depths: avoid in strong northerlies and swell.

tides.notes: Non-tidal; wind-driven level changes.

authority.name: WSA Ostsee

notes: Westerlies dominate April–September, about 12–13 kn on average in summer. Travemünde – Timmendorf about 20 NM, Timmendorf – Wismar 8, Kühlungsborn – Warnemünde 10, Rerik – Rostock about 25 NM. Timmendorf (~30 guest berths) uneasy in SW swell; Kirchdorf in southerlies; Boltenhagen Weiße Wiek ~350 berths, fuel. Rostock approach: patches under 1.5 m. Kühlungsborn east jetty closed for works (2026).

name: Rügen, Hiddensee, Greifswalder Bodden and the Usedom coast (incl. Arkona wind farms)
reach: Darß/Zingst outer coast – Hiddensee – Kap Arkona – Sassnitz – Prorer Wiek – Greifswalder Bodden (Lauterbach, Gager, Greifswald) – Peenemünde – Usedom outer coast to the Polish border

rules.notes: Wind farms: navigation, anchoring and fishing banned in the safety zones (EnBW Baltic 1 off Darß/Zingst: 500 m round the park; Wikinger, Arkona-Becken Südost, Windanker, Baltic Eagle, EnBW Baltic 2, Arcadis Ost 1 by GDWS general orders). Jasmund NP: no navigation outside fairways in zone I; Südost-Rügen zones I/II: fairways only (sail/paddle on Having, Zickersee 100 m off shore). NP speed rules 12 kn in fairways, 8 kn outside.

season.closures: Ice in cold winters on the Greifswalder Bodden (up to 25 cm in Feb 2026; Hiddensee ferry stopped).

months.notes: Bodden ice in cold winters only (Jan–Feb 2026).

authority.name: WSA Ostsee / GDWS (wind farm orders)

notes: Sassnitz: 2.6 km mole, harbour usable in heavy weather, fairway starts 0.5 NM south of the mole head. Legs: Lauterbach – Sassnitz 25 NM, Sassnitz – Rønne 50–55, Sassnitz – Świnoujście 42, Świnoujście – Lubmin 34, Greifswald – Neuhof 12. Set nets on the Bodden; Ruden harbour closed.

name: Pomeranian Bay and the Polish coast (Świnoujście – Kołobrzeg – Łeba)
reach: Świnoujście – Międzyzdroje – Dziwnów – Mrzeżyno – Kołobrzeg – Darłowo – Ustka – Łeba

rules.notes: Military exercise areas are closed by navigational warnings of the Polish Navy Hydrographic Office (BHMW, bhmw.gov.pl/pl/warnings); harbour masters give current warnings and forecasts. Port regulations set speeds and reporting in each port. Foreign skipper certificates are recognised in Poland.

authority.name: Urząd Morski w Szczecinie (west) / Urząd Morski w Gdyni (east); BHMW (warnings)

notes: Harbours in river mouths, often about a day apart: Świnoujście – Dziwnów 19 NM (approach buoy DZ1), Dziwnów – Mrzeżyno 22, Mrzeżyno – Kołobrzeg 10, Kołobrzeg – Darłowo 33–34, Darłowo – Łeba 53 NM. Bornholm crossings: Łeba – Svaneke 88, Svaneke – Darłowo 60 NM.

name: Gulf of Gdańsk (Hel – Gdynia – Gdańsk – Vistula Spit)
reach: Władysławowo – Hel peninsula (Jastarnia, Hel) – Puck Bay – Gdynia – Sopot – Gdańsk (Górki, Westerplatte) – Vistula Spit (Nowy Świat canal)

rules.notes: Exercise areas closed by BHMW warnings; VTS Zatoka Gdańska controls ship traffic. The Russian border meets the Vistula Spit just east of this box: keep out of Russian waters (Germany warns against all travel to Russia; boat trips in Kaliningrad coastal waters need a permit).

authority.name: Urząd Morski w Gdyni

notes: Gdynia – Gdańsk 13 NM, Sopot – Gdynia 6 NM, Gdynia – Hel about 23 km (fast catamaran half an hour), Gdańsk – Nowy Świat canal for the lagoon. Gdynia – Klaipėda 120 NM overnight, outside Russian territorial waters.

name: Lithuanian and Latvian Baltic coast (Klaipėda – Liepāja – Ventspils – Cape Kolka)
reach: Klaipėda – Šventoji – Liepāja – Pāvilosta – Ventspils – Cape Kolka (Irbe Strait); Kaliningrad waters south of 55.27° N excluded

rules.notes: Schengen: no clearance from other Schengen states. Klaipėda: register arrival with the harbour office on VHF; Lithuanian border police may stop yachts at sea. Boats over 10 m should call the harbour master before entering. Passages south pass the Russian EEZ: keep out of Russian territorial waters (German travel warning for Russia).

tides.notes: Tidal currents only 0.02–0.04 kn; sea level varies about +1.3/−1.0 m with wind and pressure.

authority.name: MRCC Riga (phone 115); Klaipėda harbour office

notes: SW and N winds dominate, westerly storms to 22–23 m/s; frequent coastal fog; summer mostly calm. Marinas in river mouths about 50 NM apart (Klaipėda – Liepāja 50 NM, Ventspils – Riga 120 NM); small basins, 2 m draught often the limit, some harbours shut in heavy seas. VHF 16 / DSC 70.

name: Gulf of Riga (Riga, Jūrmala, Pärnu, Kuressaare, Kihnu, Ruhnu)
reach: Irbe Strait – Roja, Mērsrags, Engure, Jūrmala (Lielupe), Riga (Daugava), Skulte, Salacgrīva; Estonian side Ruhnu, Kihnu, Manilaid, Munalaid, Pärnu, Kuressaare/Roomassaare, Abruka

rules.notes: Estonian sailing directions are updated monthly (Transpordiamet); harbour masters expect a call by phone or VHF before arrival.

months.notes: Freezing is common in winter and the gulf is sometimes iced over completely; the ice usually melts in March–April. Not every winter.

tides.notes: Tides 5–7 cm; wind-driven currents 0.2–0.3 kn in the gulfs.

authority.name: Transpordiamet (EE); Latvian Maritime Administration

notes: About 50 × 50 NM, average depth 26 m. The Irbe Strait is the main entrance and uncomfortable in swell. Kuressaare – Riga almost 100 NM. Official fairways: Roomassaare approach 5.8 NM, Pärnu fairway about 19 NM from the gulf to the river mouth, Kihnu strait 21 NM. Pärnu Yacht Club 220 berths (30 guest).

name: Estonian west coast and islands (Väinameri, Hiiumaa, Haapsalu, Muhu)
reach: Väinameri (Moonsund) between the mainland, Muhu, Saaremaa and Hiiumaa: Haapsalu, Rohuküla, Vormsi (Sviby), Virtsu, Kuivastu, Heltermaa, Orjaku, Kärdla, Sõru, Triigi, Soela strait, Dirhami

depth.notes: Shallow inner sea: follow the official fairways (Väinameri fairway Hari kurk – Väinameri S about 52 NM; Voosi kurk and Hobulaiu fairways to Haapsalu; Soela strait). Much shallower than the Irbe Strait route.

rules.notes: EU/Schengen: arrival from EU states is simple; call the harbour master by phone or VHF before arrival. Sailing directions, notices to mariners and navigational warnings from Transpordiamet.

tides.notes: Tides 5–7 cm; sea breeze onshore by day, offshore at night.

authority.name: Transpordiamet (Estonian Transport Administration)

notes: Almost 30 marinas a few hours apart. Virtsu – Kuivastu 4 NM (ferry). Tallinn – Helsinki 42–45 NM. Average wind 6–7 m/s in the archipelago, stronger in spring and autumn.

name: River Thames, non-tidal (Lechlade – Oxford – Reading – Windsor – Teddington)
reach: St John's Lock, Lechlade to Teddington Lock (EA navigation; Cricklade–Inglesham small boats only)
class: Broad river locks (smallest St John's/Buscot ~33.5 × 4.5 m)

depth.notes: Approx. max draught by reach: Lechlade–Oxford 0.9 m, Oxford–Reading 1.2 m, Reading–Windsor 1.3 m, Windsor–Staines 1.7 m, Staines–Teddington 2.0 m.

current.notes: Stream warning boards at locks: yellow 'stream increasing/decreasing' (unpowered boats stop, powered moor up or go with caution), red 'strong stream' = do not navigate. Updated daily by 11:00 on gov.uk. 22 Nov 2026: yellow St John's–Osney.

locks.chamber: St John's 33.60 × 4.52 m, Buscot 33.47 × 4.47 m (smallest main chambers); Boulters tail gates limited to 4.8 m wide
locks.hours: Keepers 2026: Jan–Mar & Nov–Dec 09:15–13:00, 14:00–16:00; Apr & Oct 09:00–13:00, 14:00–17:00; May–Jun & Sep to 18:00; Jul–Aug to 18:30. Self-service outside (blue signs). Teddington normally 24 h.
locks.notes: 44 locks St John's–Teddington. Teddington launch lock closed since 1 Oct 2023.

rules.permit: EA River Thames registration (visitor daily/weekly/monthly by boat area, e.g. 21–25 m²: £34.90/£63.00/£178.80 in 2026) or CRT Gold licence
rules.notes: Visitor registration can be bought at staffed locks on the EA form. Electric boats pay 75%.

season.closures: Now: Benson Lock closed 9 Nov–21 Dec 2026; Old Windsor Lock closed (electrical fault) from 11 Nov 2026 until further notice; Marsh 23 Nov–18 Dec; Hambleden 30 Nov–17 Dec 2026. 2027: Abingdon 4 Jan–22 Mar, Temple and Cookham 11 Jan–22 Mar.

months.notes: Winter lock works Nov–Mar each year. Drought restrictions Penton Hook–Teddington from 3–24 Aug 2026 (still listed in Nov 2026). Stream warnings any time after heavy rain.

tides.notes: Tidal below Teddington Lock (see tidal Thames sheet).

authority.name: Environment Agency (River Thames waterways)

notes: Lowest bridge Osney 2.28 m (above Oxford); below Folly Bridge the lowest is Folly 3.12 m. Through-navigation is blocked at Old Windsor and Benson in Nov 2026. Speed limit 8 km/h (EA distance table basis). Moorings at Hurley, Oxford East Street and Marlow closed.

name: Tidal Thames (Teddington – London – Thames Barrier – estuary)
reach: Teddington Lock (tidal limit) through central London (Brentford, Limehouse) to the Thames Barrier and the estuary off Southend

current.notes: Tidal streams up to 4 kn and waves to 1.2 m can be met (PLA); PLA ebb-tide flag warning for fluvial flow updated daily 06:00.
