months.notes: Lake level varies 4–5 ft a year: lowest Sept–Oct, highest April–May. Canal months as for the NY canal system.

authority.name: New York State Canal Corporation

notes: Ports: Whitehall, Port Henry, Burlington VT, Plattsburgh, Rouses Point (CBP/Canada border; the Richelieu and Chambly Canal continue north). Fort Ticonderoga cable ferry: never pass close. Special anchorages Deep Bay and south of the ferry.

name: Atlantic ICW: Norfolk – Beaufort NC (Albemarle & Chesapeake route)
reach: ICW Mile 0 (Norfolk) via Great Bridge Lock, the Albemarle & Chesapeake Canal, Currituck and Albemarle Sounds, the Alligator–Pungo Canal, Pamlico Sound and Neuse River to Beaufort/Morehead City (about Mile 204)

depth.notes: Federal project 12 ft Norfolk–Fort Pierce; actual controlling depths in USCG LNM/USACE surveys and often less (wind-driven levels in the sounds).

current.notes: No periodic tide south of Great Bridge Lock: water level depends on wind direction and strength; open sounds (Albemarle, Pamlico) get steep short seas.

locks.chamber: Great Bridge Lock (Mile 11.5) 600 × 72 ft (usable 530 ft), 16 ft over sills, lift 2.7 ft
locks.hours: Lock operator reachable 24 h on VHF 13
locks.notes: Only lock on the ICW Norfolk–Key West via this route. Several low lift/bascule bridges in Norfolk (e.g. Mile 5.8 bascule 7 ft) open on request or schedule.

rules.notes: 6 kn from Eastern Branch to the railroad bridge at Mile 2.6 (Norfolk); drawbridges per 33 CFR 117; bridges work VHF 13 (Virginia/NC).

months.notes: Hurricane season June–November; strong winds can raise or lower sound levels by several feet.

tides.notes: Elizabeth River tidal; south of Great Bridge essentially non-tidal (wind tides).

authority.name: USACE Norfolk and Wilmington Districts; U.S. Coast Guard District 5

notes: Fixed bridges 65 ft standard; Wilkerson Bridge (Mile 125.8, Alligator–Pungo Canal) 64 ft is the lowest on this reach. Wait for settled weather to cross Albemarle Sound and the Alligator River. Alternate route: Dismal Swamp Canal.

name: Dismal Swamp Canal (ICW alternate route)
reach: Deep Creek (ICW Mile 7.6 off the Southern Branch, Elizabeth River) through the 19-mile summit canal to the Pasquotank River and Elizabeth City (Norfolk–Elizabeth City 51 sm)

depth.notes: Project 10 ft Deep Creek, 9 ft canal, 10 ft Pasquotank, but the canal is maintained to only 6 ft (1.8 m); Deep Creek north of the lock reported 5.5 ft MLLW. Shoals build at the Lake Drummond feeder ditch.

current.notes: Non-tidal summit; wind changes level 1–2 ft. Submerged logs and stumps common.

locks.chamber: Deep Creek and South Mills: 300 × 52 ft, 12 ft over sills, lift about 12 ft
locks.hours: Normally 08:30, 11:00, 13:30, 15:30 daily (USACE; may change in drought or bad weather)
locks.notes: Call Deep Creek lock/bridge 757-487-0831 and South Mills 252-771-5906 before transit; both on VHF 13. Lockings tied to the Deep Creek and South Mills bridge openings.

rules.notes: No-wake canal; free Dismal Swamp Welcome Center dock (Mile 28).

season.closures: Closed periodically for gate and bridge work (e.g. 2020, 2024 Deep Creek lock, early 2025 Deep Creek bridge); can close in drought.

months.notes: Lock schedules reduced when Lake Drummond is low (drought).

tides.notes: Pasquotank and Deep Creek wind-driven.

authority.name: USACE Norfolk District

notes: Slow, scenic alternative to the A&C route for boats drawing under 6 ft (1.8 m). Fixed bridge 65 ft at Mile 31.5; overhead cables 91 ft at Deep Creek. Check status before going: closures are announced by USCG/USACE.

name: Atlantic ICW: Beaufort NC – Savannah River (the Carolinas)
reach: About ICW Mile 204 (Beaufort/Morehead City NC) via Wrightsville, Cape Fear, Little River, Georgetown, Charleston and Beaufort SC to the Savannah River (about Mile 575)

depth.notes: Project 12 ft but inlets cause shoaling: Lockwoods Folly and Shallotte crossings (NC), Mile 347 area reported 8 ft (2012); transit the problem spots on a rising tide and check USACE surveys.

current.notes: Strong cross-currents at inlet crossings (Masonboro, Lockwoods Folly, Shallotte, Little River) and in the Cape Fear River; tidal range grows southward.

locks.notes: Several swing/bascule bridges with schedules (e.g. Mile 353.3 swing); fixed bridges 65 ft except 64 ft at Mile 252.3; Snows Cut overhead cable 68 ft (Mile 295.8).

rules.notes: Drawbridge rules 33 CFR 117; no-wake zones by marinas.

season.closures: Hurricane season June–November

months.notes: Hurricanes Aug–Oct can raise water 10 ft or more.

tides.notes: Mean range from non-tidal (NC sounds) to about 7 ft (2.1 m) on the waterway further south (Coast Pilot); plan shoal spots and inlet crossings by the tide.

authority.name: USACE Wilmington and Charleston Districts; U.S. Coast Guard Districts 5 and 7

notes: Waccamaw River (Mile 375–403) is a scenic cypress stretch with anchorages; Charleston (Mile 469) has strong Ashley/Cooper currents and city marinas; Beaufort SC (Mile 536). Bridges monitor VHF 09 or 13 depending on state.

name: Atlantic ICW: Georgia (Savannah – St. Marys)
reach: Savannah River (about ICW Mile 575) through the Georgia rivers and sounds to Cumberland Sound/St. Marys (about Mile 714), about 160 miles

depth.notes: Authorised 12 ft, rarely funded: user soundings Little Mud River 4.0 ft MLLW (2023), Jekyll Creek 5.4 ft MLLW (2024, historically the shallowest point), Hell Gate shoals; pass the hot spots near half tide rising.

current.notes: Strong tidal streams in the sounds and at river junctions; about 1 kn in Skidaway Narrows.

locks.notes: Most bridges now fixed 65 ft; former Skidaway bascule (22 ft) and Causton Bluff bascule (21 ft) replaced by fixed spans.

months.notes: Hurricane season June–November.

tides.notes: Largest tides of the US southeast coast; the alternate routes and creeks dry or shoal (e.g. 4 ft at low tide near Mile 623). Use current USACE Savannah District surveys.

authority.name: USACE Savannah District; U.S. Coast Guard District 7

notes: Remote marshland: plan fuel (Thunderbolt, Kilkenny, Brunswick, St. Simons, Jekyll). Many skippers go outside from Savannah to St. Marys in settled weather to skip the shallow sounds. Cumberland Island NS anchorages.

name: Atlantic ICW: Florida east coast (Fernandina – Miami)
reach: Fernandina Beach (about Mile 716) via St. Augustine, Daytona, Titusville, Fort Pierce (Mile 965.6) and Palm Beach to Miami (Mile 1089)

depth.notes: Federal project 12 ft to Fort Pierce, then 10 ft (3.0 m) to Miami; shoaling at inlet crossings (Matanzas, Ponce de Leon, St. Lucie, Jupiter) — see LNM.

current.notes: Strong currents at inlets and at the St. Johns River crossing; Indian River and Mosquito Lagoon almost tideless.

locks.notes: Bascule bridges open on demand or on schedule (33 CFR 117); fixed bridges 65 ft except Julia Tuttle Causeway 56 ft (Mile 1087.1): taller boats go outside from Port Everglades.

rules.notes: Regulated manatee speed zones (e.g. from Mile 880.5) and local no-wake zones.

season.closures: Hurricane season June–November

months.notes: Hurricane season June–November.

tides.notes: Tidal near inlets; Mosquito Lagoon and Indian River mostly wind-driven.

authority.name: USACE Jacksonville District; Florida Inland Navigation District; U.S. Coast Guard District 7

notes: Mile 987.8 at St. Lucie Inlet is the junction with the Okeechobee Waterway. Haulover Canal links Mosquito Lagoon and the Indian River near Titusville (Kennedy Space Center restricted area nearby).

name: Okeechobee Waterway (Stuart – Fort Myers)
reach: St. Lucie Inlet/Stuart (ICW Mile 987.8) via the St. Lucie Canal, Lake Okeechobee (Route 1 across, Route 2 rim) and the Caloosahatchee to Fort Myers and Punta Rassa (about 155 mi)

depth.notes: Controlling depth 8 ft Route 1, 6 ft Route 2 (rim) at lake level 12.5 ft; depth changes foot-for-foot with the lake. Below 12 ft NGVD some north-shore locks close. Check USACE daily lake level.

current.notes: Strong currents and turbulence near St. Lucie and Port Mayaca locks when water is released from the lake; depth over St. Lucie lock sill falls from 13.5 to 8 ft during releases.

locks.chamber: St. Lucie, Moore Haven, Ortona: 250 × 50 ft, 10 ft over sills; Port Mayaca 400 × 56 ft, 16 ft; W.P. Franklin 400 × 56 ft, 14 ft
locks.hours: USACE 2022 notice: 07:00–17:00, last lockage 16:30 (Coast Pilot lists 06:00–21:30); extended hours before tropical storms
locks.notes: Planned: W.P. Franklin closed 3 May – 30 Jun 2027 (moved from Jan–Mar 2027); Ortona closed 1 Mar – 30 Apr 2027. Clewiston lock gives access to the town basin.

rules.notes: Manatee zones on the St. Lucie and Caloosahatchee; Route 2 Torry Island swing bridge closed 12 Oct – 22 Dec 2026 (8 ft clearance; Route 1 open).

season.closures: Lock closures for maintenance; low-lake closures in droughts; Route 2 Torry Island bridge works to 22 Dec 2026

months.notes: Lake usually lowest in late spring before the rainy season; hurricanes June–November.

tides.notes: Tidal only below the St. Lucie and Franklin locks (diurnal range 1.2 ft at Fort Myers).

authority.name: USACE Jacksonville District

notes: Port Mayaca railroad lift bridge (Mile 38) limits air draft to about 49 ft (15 m): taller boats go round the Keys. Government slips at Moore Haven and below Ortona; tie-up dolphins at each lock.

name: Chesapeake and Delaware Canal
reach: Reedy Point on the Delaware River to Back Creek and the Elk River at the head of Chesapeake Bay (14 mi)

depth.notes: Federal project 35 ft × 400 ft; sea-level canal, no locks. Small-craft anchorage basin at Chesapeake City (south side).

current.notes: Tidal: 2.6 kn flood, 2.1 kn ebb at Reedy Point, about 2 kn at Chesapeake City; flood sets east. Storms raise it to 3 kn+. Plan with the current.

locks.notes: Bridges: lowest fixed 131 ft MHW (Summit); Conrail vertical lift 45 ft down / 129 ft up, normally raised.

rules.notes: No sailing (engine required) and no water-skiing between Reedy Point and Welch Point; no stopping or anchoring in the channel; no racing; vessels with the current have right of way. Dispatcher at Chesapeake City VHF 13/16 (24 h).

season.closures: Ice possible December–April, worst January–February

tides.notes: High and low water in the Delaware about 2 h later than in the Elk River; NE storms raise, westerlies lower the level.

authority.name: USACE Philadelphia District

notes: Heavy ship traffic day and night; keep to the side. Chesapeake City has free basin anchorage, town dock and fuel. Delaware Bay is rough in wind against tide: time the bay leg with the ebb toward Cape May.

name: Chesapeake Bay
reach: Chesapeake Bay from the Virginia Capes (Cape Charles–Cape Henry) to the Susquehanna Flats and the C&D Canal approach, with Annapolis, Baltimore, St. Michaels, Solomons, Norfolk

depth.notes: Deep main channel, but wide shallow flats along both shores and in the Eastern Shore rivers; crab-pot floats everywhere outside the channels.

current.notes: Tidal currents strongest at the entrance and in the narrow upper bay.

rules.notes: State boating laws (MD/VA) apply; local no-wake zones in the creeks.

months.notes: Gales Sep–Mar; dense fog mostly Jan–Apr; spring/summer thunderstorms 6–9 days a month with gale-force gusts (squall lines up to 70–90 kn).

tides.notes: Small tides in most of the bay; strong winds pile up or drain water by a foot or more. Predictions at tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard Sector Maryland–NCR and Sector Virginia (District 5)

notes: Summer: light southerlies with afternoon thunderstorms – watch the sky. Popular: Annapolis, St. Michaels, Oxford, Solomons, Baltimore Inner Harbor, Norfolk. NOAA Weather Radio 162.55 MHz; VHF 16. Superstructure icing risk Nov–Mar.

name: Delaware Bay and River
reach: Cape May–Cape Henlopen entrance up Delaware Bay and River to the C&D Canal and Philadelphia

depth.notes: Ship channel deep; extensive shoals either side of the bay with few harbors of refuge between the entrance and the C&D Canal.

current.notes: 1.8 kn at the bay entrance; strong in the river; wind against tide makes a steep short sea.

rules.notes: Heavy commercial traffic: monitor VHF 13/16; Delaware pilots on VHF 14.

months.notes: Strong NW winds Nov–Mar (gales 1–3 %), seas 10 ft+ about 1 % then; fog April–June; ice usually from January to early March.

tides.notes: Strong E/SE winds raise tides and flood lowlands; long NW blows give lower than predicted lows.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard Sector Delaware Bay (District 5)

notes: Small craft shelter behind the Cape Henlopen breakwaters; Cape May Harbor via the Cape May Canal. Run the bay with the tide (ebb down, flood up).

name: Long Island Sound
reach: Throgs Neck/Hell Gate (East River) to The Race and Block Island Sound, between Connecticut, New York and the north shore of Long Island

depth.notes: Deep and well marked, but boulders and broken ground: take care where charted depths are within 6–8 ft of your draft. Oyster stakes are hazards.

current.notes: 1.8 kn off Cornfield Point, about 1 kn off New Haven, weak in the west; very strong in The Race, Plum Gut and Hell Gate – time passages.

rules.notes: No-Discharge Zone for all sewage throughout the Sound from Hell Gate to Block Island Sound. Submarine operating areas off New London.

months.notes: Best mid-May–mid-Oct (20–25 ideal days a month in summer); fog in spring and early summer; winter winds W–N; ice mostly in the western Sound in cold winters.

tides.notes: Mean range about 2.5 ft at the east end rising to 7.3 ft (2.2 m) at the west end; strong winds can drop water several feet below chart datum.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard Sector Long Island Sound (District 1)

notes: Summer SW sea breeze builds in the afternoon; squall lines ahead of cold fronts. Harbors: City Island, Oyster Bay, Port Jefferson, Stamford, New Haven, Essex/Connecticut River, Mystic, Greenport, Shelter Island. New London is the main refuge in the east.

name: Lake Ontario (US shore)
reach: US south and east shore from the Niagara River to Cape Vincent and the St. Lawrence (Olcott, Rochester, Sodus Bay, Oswego, Sackets Harbor)

depth.notes: Deep lake (average 283 ft, max 802 ft); few offshore shoals except Niagara Bar and the NE end toward the St. Lawrence. Chart datum: Low Water Datum 243.3 ft IGLD85.

current.notes: Less seiche than Lake Erie; currents at the Niagara and St. Lawrence outflows.

locks.notes: Connections: Oswego Canal (NY canals), Welland Canal and St. Lawrence Seaway (Seaway Handbook, tolls; VHF 13 'Seaway Sodus' sector).

rules.notes: Crossing to Canada: report to CBSA on arrival and to CBP (ROAM) on return.

season.closures: St. Lawrence Seaway closed by ice from about mid-December to mid-April

months.notes: Winds >33 kn most frequent Oct–Dec (6 % of the time in December); leisure season roughly May–October.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard District 9 (Great Lakes); NOAA charts and Coast Pilot 6

notes: Harbors of refuge are far apart on the US shore (Olcott, Rochester/Charlotte, Sodus Bay, Oswego). Cold water even in summer. NOAA Weather Radio and Canadian/US Coast Guard VHF weather broadcasts. Distances (statute miles): Toronto – Kingston 160, Toronto – Port Weller 28, Toronto – Hamilton 30, Kingston – Picton 37, Kingston – Trenton 71. Watch the forecast before open-lake legs; Seaway ships cross between Port Weller and Cape Vincent. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Lake Erie (US shore)
reach: Detroit River mouth to Buffalo along the US shore (Toledo, Put-in-Bay and the Bass Islands, Sandusky, Cleveland, Erie PA, Dunkirk, Buffalo)

depth.notes: Shallowest Great Lake (average 62 ft, max 210 ft); island region in the west is shoal. Low Water Datum 569.2 ft IGLD85.

current.notes: Wind set-up/seiche: SW or NE gales shift water from end to end — level changes up to 10 ft lasting 12 h observed at Toledo/Buffalo (Sep–Apr, especially Nov–Jan).

locks.notes: Black Rock Lock (Buffalo) leads to the Erie Canal; Welland Canal (Canada) to Lake Ontario.

rules.notes: East of Long Point is a St. Lawrence Seaway sector (VHF 11 'Seaway Long Point'); Canadian waters have gas wells and pipelines — do not anchor near them.

months.notes: Gales 6–9 % of the time in Nov–Dec, under 1 % May–Sep; west end freezes first; mush ice can block Buffalo into May in severe winters.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard District 9 (Great Lakes); NOAA charts and Coast Pilot 6

notes: Steep, short seas build very quickly (5 ft+ seas 30 % of the time lakewide); summer squall lines (87 kn in July 1969). Fog mostly in spring. Trap and gill nets in fished areas.

name: Lake Huron (US shore)
reach: Port Huron (St. Clair River) along the Michigan shore and Saginaw Bay to the Straits of Mackinac and De Tour (Harbor Beach, Port Austin, Bay City, Alpena, Rogers City, Cheboygan, Mackinac Island)

depth.notes: Max 750 ft; Low Water Datum 577.5 ft IGLD85 (same as Lake Michigan). Saginaw Bay is shoal with large wind set-up.

current.notes: Strong current in the St. Clair River at Port Huron; wind set-up pronounced at the mouth of the Saginaw River.

locks.notes: Soo Locks (St. Marys River) to Lake Superior: free for recreational craft; report to the small-craft dispatch station (upbound: east center pier); boats need 75 ft of lines and a lifejacket per person.

rules.notes: Canadian Coast Guard VTS covers Canadian waters from Long Point through the St. Clair River to De Tour Reef.

months.notes: Gales most frequent in autumn (5–10 % in Nov–Dec), under 1 % in June–July; violent squalls possible spring–fall.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard District 9 (Great Lakes); NOAA charts and Coast Pilot 6

notes: Long stretches of the Michigan thumb have few harbors of refuge; Port Huron–Mackinac race course along this shore. NOAA Weather Radio; VHF 16.

name: Lake Michigan
reach: Whole lake (entirely in the US): Chicago, Milwaukee, Green Bay and Door County, the Michigan shore (St. Joseph, Holland, Grand Haven, Ludington, Traverse City, Charlevoix) to the Straits of Mackinac

depth.notes: Max 923 ft; Low Water Datum 577.5 ft IGLD85. South-end harbors are artificial (piers), with dangerous currents at entrances in onshore gales.

current.notes: Wind set-up pronounced at Green Bay; harbor entrance currents in strong onshore winds.

locks.notes: Chicago: lock into the Chicago River and the Illinois Waterway to the Mississippi; Sturgeon Bay Ship Canal crosses the Door peninsula.

months.notes: Worst seas Oct–Nov (5–10 ft waves 35 % of the time); summer seas over 10 ft <1 %; by August the fall build-up starts.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard District 9 (Great Lakes); NOAA charts and Coast Pilot 6

notes: Northerlies raise big seas at the south end, southerlies at the north end, over the 300-mile fetch. The east shore ports are a day apart (25–40 mi); crossing Chicago–Michigan shore is 60–90 mi.

name: Lake Superior (US shore)
reach: Whitefish Bay and Sault Ste. Marie west along the Michigan Upper Peninsula (Grand Marais, Munising, Marquette, Keweenaw) to the Apostle Islands, Duluth–Superior and the Minnesota north shore

depth.notes: Max 1,333 ft; rocky shores, few harbors. Level regulated at the St. Marys River between 599.6 and 603.2 ft IGLD85.

current.notes: Wind set-up usually under 1 ft (up to 2 ft); Keweenaw Waterway gives a sheltered short cut across the peninsula.

locks.notes: Soo Locks at Sault Ste. Marie (free for pleasure craft); Keweenaw Waterway and Duluth/Superior ship canals.

season.closures: Navigation season about 8 months (depends on ice breaking)

months.notes: Coldest lake with most shore ice; gales up to 6 % in late autumn; April has the highest mean winds at many ports; fog common in early summer over cold water.

authority.name: U.S. Coast Guard District 9 (Great Lakes); NOAA charts and Coast Pilot 6

notes: Water stays very cold (hypothermia risk) all summer; harbors of refuge are 20–50 mi apart along the UP shore. Plan around NOAA marine forecasts; Canadian shore is remote.

name: St. Lawrence Seaway (Montreal – Iroquois)
reach: Montreal Harbour (Seaway mile 0, Laurier Pier) via the South Shore Canal, Lac Saint-Louis, the Beauharnois Canal, Lac Saint-François and the Snell/Eisenhower locks to Iroquois Lock (mile 97.9)

depth.notes: Channel 8.2 m (27 ft) upstream of Montreal; maximum ship draught 8.1 m. Deep enough for any yacht; the constraint is the lock rules, not depth.

current.notes: Currents and eddies from lock operations at the approaches; heavy drifting weed near locks in summer. Commercial ships pull a lot of water: keep clear.

locks.hours: Pleasure craft 2026: 8 May – 18 Oct. Fixed lockages upbound St-Lambert 09:00, Côte-Ste-Catherine 11:00, Beauharnois 3 15:00, Beauharnois 4 16:00; downbound Beauharnois 4 11:00, 3 12:00, Côte-Ste-Catherine 16:00, St-Lambert 18:00. Iroquois: 10:00/13:00/17:00 up, 10:30/13:30/17:30 down (15 May–7 Sep). Snell and Eisenhower (US): no schedule.
locks.notes: St-Lambert, Côte-Ste-Catherine, Beauharnois 3+4, Snell, Eisenhower, Iroquois. Wait only at the pleasure-craft docks (no overnight stays, fine up to $5,000). Two crew to handle lines; lines supplied at Canadian locks, own lines at US locks. Downbound boats must be at the Larocque (Valleyfield) bridge by 09:00.

rules.permit: Online reservation and payment required for Canadian locks (book by 09:00 on the day; no cash): St-Lambert, Côte-Ste-Catherine and Iroquois $25 CAD each, Beauharnois 3+4 $50 CAD. US locks Snell and Eisenhower $30 per lock, exact cash or pay.gov.
rules.notes: Minimum 6 m (20 ft) and 900 kg; motor-powered only, no sailing in canals/locks; lifejackets worn by everyone in locks; no overtaking within 600 m of a lock; dinghies stowed on deck; no fenders made of tyres; 6 kn in canals. VHF: don't use Seaway working channels, ch 16 in emergency, ch 68 to linehandlers and bridges.

season.best: June – early September (three daily Iroquois lockages 15 May – 7 Sep)
season.closures: Closed to pleasure craft after 18 Oct 2026; reopens about early May 2027.

months.notes: Pleasure-craft season 2026 ran 8 May – 18 Oct (Iroquois one daily lockage 8–10 May and 8 Sep – 18 Oct).

authority.name: St. Lawrence Seaway Management Corporation (Canadian locks); Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation (Snell, Eisenhower)

notes: Closed for pleasure craft until the 2027 season (2026 season ended 18 Oct). Twin CPR bridges at Kahnawake: boats up to 12 m air draft may pass under the lowered spans. Call bridges at Kahnawake, St-Louis-de-Gonzague and Larocque on VHF 68. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Welland Canal (Port Weller – Port Colborne)
reach: Lake Ontario at Port Weller to Lake Erie at Port Colborne (8 locks, 99.5 m rise)

depth.notes: Channel standard 8.2 m; max ship draught 8.08 m.

current.notes: Turbulence from lock operations; no strong river current.

locks.chamber: 233.5 × 24.4 m (lift locks 1–7); guard lock 8 at Port Colborne about 349.9 m long
locks.hours: Pleasure craft 2026: 1 May – 25 Oct. Upbound Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun, be at the Port Weller dock by 09:00; downbound Tue/Thu/Sat, at the Port Colborne dock by 07:00. One transit a day, about 12 hours. Late season weekends only (upbound Sat, downbound Sun).
locks.notes: Locks 4–6 are a twinned flight at Thorold. No pleasure-craft docks inside the canal; partial transits not allowed. Report to the Operations Control Centre on VHF 14 or 289-690-4344 and keep listening watch on ch 14.

rules.permit: $200 CAD for all eight locks, reserved and paid online by 07:00 on the day of transit (no cash).
rules.notes: Minimum 6 m and 900 kg, motor-powered; upbound at least three people on board (operator + two line handlers), downbound two line handlers; lifejackets worn. Max 6 kn near the Port Robinson ferry (nautical mile 12.5).

season.closures: Closed to pleasure craft after 25 Oct 2026; the canal closes to all shipping in winter (usually late December to late March).

months.notes: Pleasure craft 1 May – 25 Oct in 2026; commercial season late March to December.

authority.name: St. Lawrence Seaway Management Corporation

notes: Plan for a 12-hour day with continuous operation; mooring lines thrown from the wall, fenders essential. Toronto to Port Weller is about 45 km across Lake Ontario. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Thousand Islands (St. Lawrence, Kingston – Iroquois)
reach: Upper St. Lawrence from Kingston and Wolfe Island through the Thousand Islands (Gananoque, Rockport, Brockville) to Prescott and Iroquois Lock

depth.notes: Seaway channel 8.2 m, but hidden rocks and shoals among the islands: navigate with charts.

locks.notes: No locks between Kingston and Iroquois; Iroquois Lock (Seaway, fixed lockage times) at the downstream end.

rules.permit: Thousand Islands National Park: mooring or beaching permit by boat length, bought on arrival; max 3 consecutive nights per island or mooring buoy (overnight passes expire 11:00).
rules.notes: Keep clear of Seaway ships in the channel; international border mid-river.

season.closures: Thousand Islands National Park temporarily closed, reopening May 2027 (as of 2026-11-22).

authority.name: Parks Canada (Thousand Islands National Park); St. Lawrence Seaway Management Corporation

notes: Kingston – Gananoque 19 mi, Kingston – Brockville 50 mi (statute). Environment Canada forecast area 'Kingston to Cornwall'. Island docks/buoys on all serviced park islands. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: St. Lawrence River (Montreal – Quebec City)
reach: Port of Montreal via Sorel-Tracy, Lac Saint-Pierre and Trois-Rivières to Quebec City (Cap-Rouge)

depth.notes: Ship channel 11.0–11.3 m; small-craft channels between Lac Saint-Pierre and Sorel and in the Îles de Boucherville; water levels vary strongly with freshet and dry periods (SINECO gauges).

current.notes: Courant Sainte-Marie at Montreal 4–6 kn; 1–2.5 kn in most reaches Montreal–Sorel; up to 3.5 kn under Pont Laviolette (Trois-Rivières) at low tide; Rapides Richelieu ebb up to 8 kn, Barre à Boulard 5.5 kn.

rules.notes: Around the Island of Montreal: 10 km/h within 50 m of shore (30 m in Rivière des Prairies), 25 km/h anywhere 21:00–07:00; 10 km/h in Chenal du Sud (Boucherville). Small craft must keep out of the way of ships. Île aux Sternes is a regulated ecological reserve.

season.closures: Ice from mid-December to early April; light buoys lifted in winter.

months.notes: Ice develops in the first half of December and clears by early April; Lac Saint-Pierre fast ice ~74 cm, ice boom off Pointe Yamachiche Nov–Apr.

tides.notes: Tidal influence felt up to Trois-Rivières (max range about 0.3 m there, about 0.8 m at Bécancour) and dies out on Lac Saint-Pierre; it strengthens below Portneuf towards Quebec City. Above Rapides Richelieu the flood is weak (0.5 kn) and reaches Batiscan only at springs: slow boats should time the ebb downstream. Hourly current forecasts: ogsl.ca.

authority.name: Canadian Coast Guard (MCTS), Transport Canada, Canadian Hydrographic Service

notes: Distances: Montreal – Sorel 70 km, Sorel (Tracy) – Trois-Rivières 32 NM, Trois-Rivières – Québec 70 NM. Marinas at Sorel, Trois-Rivières and the Port of Québec (Bassin Louise). Rescue: MRSC Québec VHF 16 or *16. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Rideau Canal (Ottawa – Kingston)
reach: Ottawa (Ottawa Locks at the Ottawa River) up the Rideau River to the summit at Upper Rideau Lake (Newboro) and down the lakes and the Cataraqui River to Kingston on Lake Ontario; Tay Canal branch to Perth

depth.notes: About 1.5 m (5 ft) in the navigation channel in season, not guaranteed.

locks.chamber: 27.3 × 8.5 m (operational)
locks.notes: 45 locks at 23 stations on the main line plus 2 on the Tay Canal (24 stations). Arrive 30 min before closing per chamber at flights (e.g. Ottawa 8 locks, Jones Falls 4, Kingston Mills 4). Stations unstaffed and closed 22:00–06:00.

rules.permit: Parks Canada lockage permit by boat length, on site only (not sold online in 2026): single lock and return, 1 day, 6 day, one-way transit or seasonal; mooring permits on site.
rules.notes: 10 km/h in speed zones; first and last lockage times not guaranteed.

season.closures: Closed for the season since 12 Oct 2026; reopens about mid-May 2027.

months.notes: Navigation mid-May – mid-Oct. In winter the Ottawa section is the Rideau Canal Skateway (2025–26: 31 Dec – 4 Mar).

authority.name: Parks Canada – Rideau Canal National Historic Site

notes: Ottawa – Smiths Falls 96.8 km, Smiths Falls – Kingston about 105 km. 6.7 m fixed-bridge clearance. name: Trent–Severn Waterway (Trenton – Port Severn)
reach: Trenton on the Bay of Quinte up the Trent River, Rice Lake, the Otonabee and the Kawartha Lakes to the Balsam Lake summit (256 m), then down via Lake Simcoe, Lake Couchiching and the Severn River to Port Severn on Georgian Bay; Murray Canal

depth.notes: About 2.4 m Locks 1–19, 1.8 m Locks 20–45 (shallower in places), 2.7 m Murray Canal, 1.22 m Sturgeon Lake – Port Perry branch; not guaranteed. Call 705-750-4900 if drawing 1.5 m or more.

locks.chamber: max vessel at Port Severn (Lock 45) 25.4 × 7 m
locks.notes: 44 locks at 42 stations incl. the Peterborough (19.8 m) and Kirkfield hydraulic lift locks; Lock 44 Big Chute is a marine railway: max 90 t, 30.3 m, 7.3 m beam (call 705-756-8802 48 h ahead if over 68 t or unusual hull). Be in the blue zone by last lockage; stations closed 22:00–06:00.

rules.permit: Parks Canada lockage permit per foot, on site: single lock and return $1.50, 1 day $2.25, one-way transit $6.00, 6 days $6.50, seasonal $11.25; overnight mooring $1.50/ft. Lockage was free 19 Jun – 7 Sep 2026 (Canada Strong Pass); mooring not discounted.
rules.notes: 10 km/h in speed zones. CN swing bridge above Lock 42 about 3.96 m when closed (trains have priority). Murray Canal bridges VHF 14 in season.

season.closures: Closed for the season since 12 Oct 2026; reopens about mid-May 2027.

months.notes: Navigation season 15 May – 12 Oct in 2026.

authority.name: Parks Canada – Trent–Severn Waterway National Historic Site

notes: Trenton – Peterborough 142 km, Peterborough – Bobcaygeon 77 km, Bobcaygeon – Lake Simcoe 69 km, Washago – Port Severn 49 km. 6.1 m minimum bridge clearance. name: Lachine Canal (Old Port of Montreal – Lachine)
reach: Old Port of Montreal (Lock 1) to Lachine on Lac Saint-Louis (Lock 5), bypassing the Lachine Rapids

depth.notes: Draught 2 m (6 ft 6 in).

locks.chamber: smallest 50.29 × 11 m
locks.hours: 2026: 15 May – 24 Jun daily at 09:30 and 13:00 only; 25 Jun – 16 Aug daily 09:30–16:15 (last complete transit 13:00 at Locks 1 and 5); 17 Aug – 7 Sep weekdays 09:30/13:00, weekends 09:30–16:15; 8 Sep – 12 Oct 09:30 and 13:00 only.
locks.notes: Transit about 3 hours (3–5 h). Arrive 30 min before last lockage; floating docks on starboard. VHF 68, Lock 1 (Old Port) 514-496-1536, Lock 5 (Lachine) 514-595-6594.

rules.permit: Parks Canada lockage permit by boat length, bought on site.
rules.notes: Overhead clearance only 2.45 m (8 ft): most sailboats with masts up and many flybridge boats cannot use it; report to each lock and bridge. Not alone on board; two mooring lines, engine off in the lock.

season.best: Late June – mid-August (open hours, otherwise two fixed lockages)
season.closures: Closed for the season since 12 Oct 2026; reopens about mid-May 2027.

months.notes: Season 15 May – 12 Oct in 2026.

reach: Lac Saint-Louis through the Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue lock, Lac des Deux Montagnes and the Carillon lock to Ottawa (Rideau Canal entrance)

depth.notes: Draught 2.74 m (9 ft) at the Sainte-Anne and Carillon locks.

Carillon: 15 May – 24 Jun Mon–Fri 09:30–16:00, Sat–Sun 09:30–17:00; 25 Jun – 12 Aug 09:30–18:00; 13–26 Aug 09:30–17:00; 27 Aug – 12 Oct as in spring.
locks.notes: Carillon lifts 20 m in one lockage with a ~200 t guillotine gate; arrive 1 h 30 before last lockage, transit about 1 h, VHF 68, 450-537-3534. Sainte-Anne (busiest lock in Canada): arrive 60 min before last lockage, VHF 68, 514-457-5546.

rules.permit: Parks Canada lockage permit by boat length, bought on site.
rules.notes: 10 km/h in the canals; first and last lockage times not guaranteed.

season.closures: Locks closed since 12 Oct 2026; reopen about mid-May 2027.

months.notes: Lock season 15 May – 12 Oct in 2026.

name: Chambly Canal (Chambly – Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu)
reach: Bassin de Chambly (Locks 1–3) to Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu (Lock 9), bypassing the Richelieu rapids

depth.notes: Sill depth 1.98 m (Lock Guide: 2 m / 6 ft 6 in); less in extreme low water.

locks.chamber: 33.5 × 7.0 m (smallest)
locks.hours: 2026: 15–18 May 09:00–16:30; 19 May – 25 Jun weekdays 09:00 and 13:00 only, weekends 09:00–16:30; 26 Jun – 23 Aug daily 09:00–16:30; 24 Aug – 12 Oct weekdays 09:00 and 13:00 only, weekends 09:00–16:30. Last complete transit 13:00 on Sundays/holidays.
locks.notes: Hand-operated; Locks 1–2–3 are a staircase at Chambly (arrive 45 min before last lockage). Complete transit at least 4 hours. No overnight mooring in the canal on fixed-hour days. VHF 68; Chambly 450-658-4381, Saint-Jean 450-348-3392. Bridges 1, 10, 12 closed weekdays 11:45–12:20 and 12:45–13:00.

rules.permit: Parks Canada lockage permit per foot, on site: single lock and return $1.50, one day complete transit $2.25, six days $6.50, seasonal $11.25; overnight mooring $1.50/ft.
rules.notes: Lock staff supply lines (no wall wharf inside); loop lines round cleats, fend off with a boathook. Max 10 km/h (5.5 kn).

season.best: Late June – August (open hours every day)
season.closures: Closed for the season since 12 Oct 2026; reopens about mid-May 2027.

months.notes: Open mid-May to mid-October.

authority.name: Parks Canada – Chambly Canal National Historic Site

name: Georgian Bay (Thirty Thousand Islands)
reach: Georgian Bay east of the Bruce Peninsula and Manitoulin Island: Midland, Penetanguishene, Port Severn, Parry Sound, the Thirty Thousand Islands, Killarney, Owen Sound, Collingwood (mapped as part of Lake Huron)

depth.notes: Thousands of rocks and shoals among the eastern islands: navigate with charts.

authority.name: Environment Canada marine forecasts (Northern and Southern Georgian Bay); Canadian Coast Guard

notes: About 190 × 80 km, ~15,000 km². Distances (statute miles): Midland – Little Current 140, Parry Sound – Little Current 111, Owen Sound – Little Current 119. The Trent–Severn enters at Port Severn. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: North Channel (Lake Huron, Killarney – Little Current – De Tour)
reach: Between Manitoulin Island and the Ontario north shore from Killarney and Little Current via Gore Bay to the False Detour Channel / De Tour (mapped as part of Lake Huron)

authority.name: Environment Canada marine forecast 'North Channel'; Canadian Coast Guard

notes: Former steamship route, now a pleasure-craft cruising ground. Distances (statute miles): Little Current – Gore Bay 33, Little Current – Thessalon 86, Mackinac Island – Little Current 137. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Strait of Georgia and Gulf Islands (BC)
reach: Strait of Georgia from the Canadian Gulf Islands, Vancouver and Howe Sound north past Nanaimo and Comox to Cape Lazo

rules.notes: Military range Area WG (Whiskey Golf) off Nanoose Bay / Winchelsea Islands is closed to all traffic when active: check CMB (WX/ch 21B) or Winchelsea Island Control VHF 10/16; keep about 1,000 yd north of Winchelsea Island or follow the mainland side.

season.closures: Winter SE gales; Squamish outflow winds (>50 kn recorded) in Howe Sound and the mainland inlets.

months.notes: Summer NW Westerly builds in the morning and usually drops late afternoon (cross the strait around 17:00–18:00); 'three-day Westerly' 2–3 times a season. Winter: E/SE more than 60% of the time; fog mostly Sept–March; forest-fire smoke Jul–Sep.

tides.notes: Mixed semi-diurnal; range about 5 m in the strait (max 5 m at Vancouver, 4.3 m Chemainus). Use the Canadian Tide and Current Tables for the narrow passes between the Gulf Islands.

authority.name: Canadian Coast Guard (MCTS Victoria), Transport Canada, Canadian Hydrographic Service

notes: Popular crossings Nanaimo – Welcome Passage and Silva Bay – Burrard Inlet. Strong local winds off Qualicum Beach. Vancouver – Nanaimo 36 NM, Nanaimo – Lund 63.5 NM, Nanaimo – Campbell River 77.7 NM. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Desolation Sound (Lund – Cortes – Redonda Islands)
reach: Northern end of the Strait of Georgia: Lund, Sarah Point, Desolation Sound Marine Park (Prideaux Haven, Tenedos Bay, Malaspina Inlet / Grace Harbour), Cortes and the Redonda Islands, Refuge Cove

rules.notes: Desolation Sound Marine Park: no sewage discharge (holding tank; pump-out at the Lund public dock), no campfires, anchoring restricted near Williams and Copplestone Islands (eelgrass), no potable water, shellfish closures (biotoxins) – check before harvesting.

season.closures: Winter Squamish outflow winds in Toba and Bute Inlets.

tides.notes: Max tidal range 4.8 m at Campbell River; the sound itself has little current (warm water by BC standards) but streams run hard in the passes to the north.

authority.name: BC Parks (Desolation Sound Marine Park); Canadian Coast Guard

notes: Over 60 km of park shoreline with many sheltered coves. Nanaimo – Sarah Point 69.4 NM (avoiding WG), Lund – Refuge Cove 10 NM, Campbell River – Desolation Sound 18.5 NM via Baker Passage. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Discovery Passage, Johnstone Strait and Queen Charlotte Strait
reach: Campbell River and Seymour Narrows through Discovery Passage and Johnstone Strait (or the Discovery Islands back channels) to Port McNeill, Port Hardy and Queen Charlotte Strait

current.notes: Seymour Narrows (750 m wide) runs up to about 15 kn (some guides 16 kn flood): transit at or near slack using the Canadian Tide and Current Tables Vol. 6; rapid tidal streams and sills throughout.

season.closures: Winter easterly gales; outflow gales from Knight, Kingcome and Loughborough Inlets.

months.notes: Summer sea-breeze westerlies build from late morning to about 30 kn by late afternoon (worst in western Johnstone Strait), dying before dusk: move early. Fog in Queen Charlotte Strait in late summer/early autumn, usually clearing by late morning.

tides.notes: Queen Charlotte Strait range about 5.5 m, Campbell River about 4.6–4.8 m. Surface water seldom above 10 °C.

authority.name: Canadian Coast Guard, Canadian Hydrographic Service

notes: Campbell River – Port Hardy 106 NM, Campbell River – Port McNeill 86.5 NM. Ripple Rock in Seymour Narrows was removed in 1958 but the narrows remain the key tidal gate. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.

name: Inside Passage north (Queen Charlotte Sound – Prince Rupert)
reach: From Cape Caution across Queen Charlotte Sound and up the mainland channels (Fitz Hugh Sound, Bella Bella / Shearwater, Klemtu, Grenville Channel) to Prince Rupert and Dixon Entrance

season.best: June – August (NW in Queen Charlotte Sound, W in Dixon Entrance)
season.closures: Strong gales are frequent in Queen Charlotte Sound, with heavy swell and dense fog; SE gales more frequent and stronger in the northern sector.

months.notes: Most pleasant months June, July, August. Autumn–winter storms bring sustained winds over 65 kn on exposed coasts; summer fog from cold upwelling.

tides.notes: Max tidal range 7.5 m at Prince Rupert (6.6 m Kitimat); the tide reaches Dixon Entrance about 50 min after Queen Charlotte Sound.

authority.name: Canadian Coast Guard, Canadian Hydrographic Service

notes: Queen Charlotte Sound is the one open-ocean crossing of the Inside Passage: wait for a forecast window. BC Ferries Port Hardy – Prince Rupert 274 NM (about 15 h, stops at Bella Bella and Klemtu off-season). Campbell River – Prince Rupert about 391 NM via Port Hardy and Shearwater. Proof of competency (Pleasure Craft Operator Card) for anyone operating a power-driven boat; visiting non-residents in their own foreign boat are exempt for under 45 consecutive days (carry proof of residence); rental boats: completed rental safety checklist.
